structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development offers a program that provides zero percent interest, deferred loans for up to 30 years or grants to help seniors make accessibility improvements to their homes. These improvements allow older people to remain in their homes while maintaining their independence.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers zero percent interest, deferred loans for terms of up to 30 years or grants up to $25,000. The maximum loan amount is up to 110 percent of the property value, accounting for any superior mortgages. All closing costs are included in the loan. Loans must be repaid upon sale, transfer, or refinance of the property. Loans in excess of $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage. Interest rates range from 0% to 6% based on applicant's ability to pay. Loans serving families with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may have deferred payments if necessary for project feasibility. The maximum loan is $50,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents age 55 or older who own and occupy their homes as their principal residence and meet income requirements.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds may be used for accessibility improvements such as widening doorways, installation of accessible showers, ramps, grab bars, lever handles, first floor bathrooms, laundry rooms, chair lifts, handicap ramps, railings, doors, handrails, rubber treads, and bathroom grab bars for fall and injury prevention.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Applicants must be Maryland residents. Income limits vary for Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties) versus the rest of the state.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident with at least one resident age 55 or older
Own and occupy the home as their principal residence (seniors living with relatives considered on a case-by-case basis)
Reside in a home that is structurally sound and free of health and safety hazards
Have no outstanding federal or state tax liens, open bankruptcy, or foreclosure
Household income cannot exceed 80% of the Statewide or Washington DC MSA median (specific limits vary by household size and region as of July 1, 2025)
For interest rates of 0-4.5%, household income cannot exceed 60% of median income
For deferred principal and interest, household income cannot exceed 50% or 30% of median income
Provide proof of home ownership including deed and current mortgage statement
Provide photo ID (Driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Provide current Property Tax Bill and Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy
Provide lowest qualifying bid from licensed Maryland contractor identifying repairs
Bid should not be more than 60 days old
Grand total of all bids should not exceed $50,000
Provide contractor MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and W-9 form
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are available at local County Housing Offices or Maryland Access Point Agencies. Assistance in completing the application is available at the agency or through an in-home appointment. Applicants must submit completed application and supporting documentation including income verification, proof of home ownership, property insurance documentation, and contractor bid documentation to DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov or by mail to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Once submitted, the application is processed by the department and the applicant will be contacted. Incomplete applications will not be processed.

structured_extraction.program_description: Funding program that supports neighborhood revitalization projects in the Baltimore region, including residential and commercial district improvements aligned with community action plans. The program aims to increase the competitiveness of targeted communities in the Baltimore metro area for new homeownership and private-sector business, residential, and commercial investment through strategic property acquisition, redevelopment, rehabilitation and new infill development.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding for neighborhood revitalization capital projects and limited operating costs in BRNI designated areas of the Baltimore region. Awards are made as grants or loans/recoverable grants. Capital projects must have at least a 15-year shelf life. Operating projects support the management of capital BRNI projects and implementation of the BRNI strategy. Each organization may not be awarded more than 40 percent of the total financial assistance for operating expenditures. Beginning FY2026, a nonrefundable Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee of 4% of the financial assistance awarded will be implemented on all capital awards (except Maryland Façade Improvement Program). The FAAP Fee is included in the award project/program budget and awardees will be invoiced after award execution.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM (FY26 application round closed)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Corporations in Baltimore City, Baltimore County or Anne Arundel County that are implementing a clear revitalization strategy in a specific neighborhood or set of neighborhoods. Cross-jurisdictional partnerships and partnerships with Community Development Financial Institutions are also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects for neighborhood revitalization including residential and commercial district improvements, adaptive reuse projects, neighborhood amenities, and related improvements in BRNI designated areas. Operating projects that support the management of capital BRNI projects and the implementation of the BRNI strategy. Eligible capital uses include real property acquisition, downpayment assistance, construction-level architectural and engineering design, demolition or deconstruction, site development, and infrastructure improvements. Ineligible uses include projects with primary use as pawn shops, gun shops, tanning salons, massage parlors, adult video/book shops, adult entertainment facilities, check cashing facilities, gambling facilities, tattoo parlors, liquor stores, or sectarian religious activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located within Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative areas in Sustainable Communities in Baltimore City, or the inner-beltway communities of Baltimore County or Anne Arundel County. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify project eligibility.
requirements_list: Project must be located in BRNI designated areas within Sustainable Communities
Capital project must have at least 15-year shelf life
Must align with community revitalization strategies and Neighborhood Revitalization Plan
Applicant must be a nonprofit community development corporation, coalition or partnership implementing a clear revitalization strategy in a specific neighborhood or set of neighborhoods
Applicant should have an approved BRNI Neighborhood Revitalization Plan on file with the Department
Current awardees must be in compliance with terms and conditions of current award agreements
Current awardees must have achieved sufficient progress and be in good standing
New organization user requests must be submitted to Project Portal at least two weeks before application deadline (by June 11)

Organizations must provide organizational documents including corporate resolution, articles of incorporation, by-laws, IRS tax exempt determination letter, board of directors list, certificate of good standing, charitable organizations registration, and corporate diversity addendum
Maryland Historical Trust review required for all capital projects prior to starting work or disbursement of funds
Evidence of site control required
Documentation of funding commitments required
Cost estimates required
Sustainable Communities map required
Photographs of interior, exterior, and site required for construction/renovation projects
Construction or renovation projects require plans/specs and construction drawings
If awarded funds exceed $250,000, Minority Business Enterprise Plan may be required
Signed Disclosure Authorization and Certification required
IRS Taxpayer Identification and Certification (W-9 Form) required
Operating budget for current fiscal year required
Independent Financial Audit (most recent) or IRS Form 990 from prior calendar year required
Optional: Local Support Resolutions or Letter of Support
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register as a new user in the Project Portal (approval may take up to 72 hours) by June 11 deadline for new organizations. Upload required organizational documents to your profile. Submit application through the Project Portal by July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM. FY26 application period opened May 28, 2025 and closed July 2, 2025. Applications are reviewed by partner agencies including Maryland Department of Commerce, Maryland Department of the Environment, Maryland Department of Health, Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Maryland Department of Natural Resources, Maryland Department of Planning, Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Higher Education Commission, and Maryland Historical Trust. Award recommendations typically occur in Fall 2025, with award announcements in Fall/Winter 2025. Award agreement drafting and execution occurs in Winter 2025. Active award management involves a 2-year award term with 50% of awarded funds required to be drawn down by the first anniversary date of the award.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Baltimore Vacants Reinvestment Initiative (BVRI), formerly known as Project C.O.R.E., provides funding to Baltimore City, the Maryland Stadium Authority, and community-based development organizations to redevelop vacant properties and strengthen neighborhoods. The program provides capital to address vacant properties through acquisition, stabilization, demolition, renovation, and other pre-development activities. BVRI focuses on scaling renovation of vacant buildings on clusters of contiguous blocks, and may also support redevelopment of vacant lots for housing, mixed-use projects, and green space. The initiative is part of the broader Reinvest Baltimore effort to move at least 5,000 vacant properties into homeownership or other positive outcomes over five years.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants and loans to finance acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings; acquisition and aggregation of vacant lots for new infill housing construction, mixed-use projects, and community-managed open space; urgent demolition of properties or vacant buildings for near-term redevelopment projects; and other predevelopment activities for renovation and new construction projects. FY27 BVRI funds may be provided as partially forgivable subordinate loans from Maryland Community Investment Corporation (MCIC), with forgiveness based on Net Sale/Refinance Proceeds and project appraisal gap. Forms of financial assistance include renovation and new construction loans or lines of credit to be repaid through home sales or refinance into permanent financing for rental projects; grant funds to fill the gap between total development costs and sale prices; and credit enhancement to leverage private capital. Awards can be structured as grants, loans, or recoverable grants. A non-refundable Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee of 4% of the awarded amount applies to all capital awards (included in the award budget, not requiring separate application contribution). Capital projects must have at least a 15-year shelf life. The Department may place a Deed of Trust on real estate projects receiving $500,000 or more. Operating costs are not eligible under this program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM (FY27 BVRI round); July 2, 2025 at 2:59 PM (FY26 application round closed)
structured_extraction.contact_name: David Birkenthal; Larry Brown, Jr. (Northwest Baltimore); Kate Howard (Northeast Baltimore); Sarah Kim (Southeast Baltimore); Erin Lavitt (Southwest Baltimore/Northern Anne Arundel); Garland Thomas (Statewide Lead); Jean Cannon (Southern Maryland)
structured_extraction.contact_email: ReinvestBaltimore.dhcd@maryland.gov; larry.brownjr@maryland.gov; katherine.howard@maryland.gov; sarah.kim1@maryland.gov; erin.lavitt@maryland.gov; garland.thomas1@maryland.gov; jean.cannon@maryland.gov
structured_extraction.program_audience: Non-profit community development organizations (CDOs) with a track record of completing the rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects, and Baltimore City-based local governments. CDOs must have an organizational mission that include community development work and a service area in Baltimore City. CDOs may have sub-recipients (development partners) that can scale up the pace of rehab to meet the opportunity and need.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Acquisition, stabilization, and renovation of vacant buildings, prioritizing those with a city-issued vacant building notice (VBN). Vacant lot acquisition and aggregation for the purpose of new infill housing construction. Vacant lot acquisition and aggregation for community open space. Urgent demolition of properties that pose a community health risk or when it furthers a near-term redevelopment project. Architectural and engineering, site infrastructure, and site development. Residential rehabilitation, residential infill new construction, modular infill construction, commercial/mixed-use projects, and community-led green space and placemaking projects. Predevelopment activities including site acquisition and assembly, site development and infrastructure improvements, and construction-level architectural and engineering designs. Stabilization of buildings to prevent deterioration, remediate environmental hazards, and prepare properties for rehabilitation and reuse.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Activities must be located in Sustainable Community Areas in Baltimore City. Special consideration will be given to projects in the Baltimore City Vacancy Reduction Priority Geographies (VRPGs), which includes the Impact Investment Areas. Projects in ENOUGH Act Grantee areas and Just Communities areas will receive up to 10 bonus points each. Properties must have Vacant Building Notices (VBNs). Verify eligibility using the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper at https://mmp.maryland.gov.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a non-profit community development organization (CDO) or local government
CDO must have a track record of completing rehabilitation of vacant property and/or infill new construction projects
CDO organizational mission must include community development work and service area in Baltimore City
Projects must be located in Baltimore City Sustainable Community Area
Project must address properties with Vacant Building Notices (VBNs)
Projects must be located in a cluster of contiguous blocks where applicant can demonstrate capacity and plan to address all vacant property over time

Target area should include contiguous clusters of whole blocks where organization can directly abate or facilitate abatement of all vacant property, particularly buildings with Vacant Building Notices
Target area should be approximately 5 blocks by 5 blocks and be walkable
Awarded funds will primarily support activities that accelerate remediation of vacant buildings with city-issued Vacant Building Notices
Emphasis on homeownership outcomes for residential rehabilitation projects
Capital project with at least 15-year shelf life
Current awardees must be in compliance with terms and conditions of existing award agreements and demonstrate sufficient progress
Current awardees must be in good standing with all reporting and payment documentation requirements
If funded, CDOs may be required to provide government resolution, corporate board resolution, and charitable registration

All CDO applicants required to submit organizational documents: By-Laws, Articles of Incorporation, Board Roster, Annual Report, IRS Letter of Determination, Financial Audit, Operating Budget, Profit & Loss Statement, Balance Sheet, and signed Public Disclosure Authorization
Applications without completed property pipeline spreadsheet and partner letters will not be accepted
Strategy must build from community strengths and assets and achieve whole block outcomes
New applicants must request Project Portal access by June 11 before application deadline
Applications must be submitted electronically through the DHCD Project Portal or Survey123 portal by deadline
Site control documentation required

Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) review required for all capital projects prior to starting work or fund disbursement
For awards exceeding $250,000, a Minority Business Enterprise Plan may be required
Prevailing wage requirements apply

Insurance requirements apply
Cybersecurity responsibilities required of awardees
Corporate diversity information required (HB 1210 compliance)
Racial/ethnic demographic information required for organization Board of Directors and senior staff (for Just Communities Initiative investment analysis)
Photographs required (interior and exterior, or site photographs as applicable)
All required organizational documents must be current and submitted with application
Evidence of certificate of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) required
IRS Tax Exempt Determination Letter required for nonprofit applicants
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: FY27 Round: Applications are submitted exclusively through Survey123 portal (no paper applications accepted). Applications open February 18, 2026 at 10:00 AM and close April 1, 2026 at 11:59 PM. Applicants must complete: organization information, organization documents, board and staff demographics, organization experience and capacity, rehabilitation/construction/management experience, geographic targeting, FY27 vacancy reduction strategy, property pipeline, and project-specific information for residential rehabilitation, infill construction, modular infill, green space/placemaking, and/or mixed-use projects. Applications are scored on: Organization Experience and Development Capacity (30 points), Whole-Block Redevelopment Strategy and Program Alignment (30 points), Vacant Property Pipeline and Production Readiness (25 points), and Budget and Financing (15 points). Site visits and follow-up discussions may occur during review. Training resources and step-by-step instructions are available online. One-on-one scheduling available for applicant questions. FY26 Round (closed): 1) New applicants request a Project Portal account, identifying the organization, project location, and funding program; deadline is 72 hours before application round closes. 2) Returning applicants log into existing Project Portal accounts. 3) Upload required organizational documents to profile. 4) Complete project application in Project Portal with individual project information. 5) Provide additional supporting documents: photographs (interior and exterior), construction plans/specifications if applicable, evidence of previous Maryland Historical Trust review (if applicable), and Minority Business Enterprise Plan (if award exceeds $250,000). 6) Provide demographic information for organization Board of Directors and senior staff racial/ethnic composition. 7) Provide project impact data sheet quantifying accomplishments with requested funds. 8) Submit complete application through Project Portal by deadline. 9) DHCD reviews applications. 10) Award recommendations made. 11) Award announcements. 12) Award agreements drafted and executed. 13) Active award management with 2-year award term begins; 50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by first anniversary date of award.

structured_extraction.program_name: BeSMART Energy Efficiency Loan for Homeowners
structured_extraction.program_description: The BeSMART Home Loan Program provides financing to improve the energy efficiency and comfort of your home. By replacing and upgrading appliances, heating, ventilation and cooling systems, and whole house envelope improvements, homeowners can save on utility bills.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Unsecured loan with a 6.99% annual percentage rate (APR). Up to $30,000 in financing is available for energy efficiency measures for a term up to 10 years. Minimum loan amount is $5,000. Borrowers must have a credit score of 640 or greater and a debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%. The loan is based on verification of credit and ability to pay. Funds are distributed as a 30% down payment 2-party check to you and your contractor upon loan approval, and the remaining 70% is distributed upon completion and certification. There are no pre-payment penalties, and borrowers can pay off the loan early to avoid interest.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners seeking to improve energy efficiency and comfort of their homes
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy saving measures including insulation and air sealing, ENERGY STAR heating and cooling systems, ENERGY STAR hot water heating equipment, ENERGY STAR appliances (excluding stoves, ovens, and microwave ovens), windows, doors, lighting and controls, programmable and smart thermostats, ceiling fans and ventilation fans, geothermal heat pumps, solar photovoltaic (capped at 50% of total loan amount, or 1:1 match to cost of energy efficiency measures), health and safety costs related to energy improvements including mold remediation and radon mitigation (up to 25% of total loan amount), and other improvements identified in a certified energy audit.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Maryland homeowner
Credit score of 640 or greater
Debt to income ratio that does not exceed 50%
Minimum loan amount is $5,000
Maximum loan amount is $30,000
Loan term up to 10 years (flexible term less than 10 years available)
Projects must not be already purchased or already completed
Contractor must be licensed and insured in Maryland
Driver's license required
30 days of pay stubs required
Recent mortgage statement required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Fill out the Online BeSMART Loan Application or request a paper application by email. 2. Provide required documentation: Driver's License, 30 days of pay stubs, and recent mortgage statement. 3. Complete a DocuSign form to privately provide your Social Security number and authorize a credit report pull. 4. Obtain an estimate or proposal from your licensed and insured contractor or from a retailer for any appliances you wish to finance. Submit the contractor's proof of License and Insurance. 5. Receive a set of loan documents from DHCD to sign and return. 6. Upon approval, receive a 30% down payment 2-party check (made to both you and your contractor, or 1-party check if retail purchase with no contractor). 7. Work is completed with contractor. 8. Upon completion, you and the contractor sign Certificates of Completion. 9. Receive the remaining 70% final draw check. 10. Begin making loan payments.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Business Boost Microgrant provides funding to support small businesses seeking to expand their business or establish a new commercial location, with a preference for helping home-based businesses move to their first commercial location outside the home. Microgrants range from $20,000 to $50,000 and are available to eligible new and expanding small businesses in designated Sustainable Communities. The program prioritizes businesses within Sustainable Communities areas and those with minority business enterprise status.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Microgrants ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 are available to support small business growth and expansion. Applicants must provide a matching contribution equal to or greater than the grant request amount. Up to $2,000,000 in total funding is available. Funds can be used towards capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth from September 23, 2024, to March 23, 2025, including salary, rent, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, and professional services. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses cannot be used.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The application round is projected to close on Monday, October 14th, 2024, at 5 PM EST. The round may close sooner if grant requests exceed available funding.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit small businesses with growth and expansion plans, particularly home-based businesses establishing their first commercial location outside the home. Businesses must have greater than 2 employees and 50 or fewer employees (full-time equivalent) and annual revenue greater than $50,000 but less than $1 million.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital and operating expenses that support revenue growth, including salary increases from hiring new employees, increased rent for expanded space, utilities, product advertising, product development, commercial real estate acquisition, professional services, and new equipment. Only new expenses are eligible; existing expenses cannot be used.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a Sustainable Communities area in Maryland. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify their business location qualifies at https://portal.dhcd.state.md.us/GIS/revitalize/index.html

Provide Articles of Organization for the business
Provide by-laws for the business

Provide screenshot showing business is in eligible location

Provide screenshot of Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Business name on application must exactly match SDAT Certificate of Good Standing and W-9
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted online through the DHCD portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/NBWOZGrant/account/login. The application round is projected to open on September 23, 2024, at 12:00 noon and close on October 14, 2024, at 5 PM EST. Applicants must create an account, provide a brief description of their organization, answer questions about the business, complete a budget table showing use of grant funds and matching contribution, and submit all required supporting documents. Only fully completed applications at the time of submission will be considered; incomplete applications will be returned. Applications are evaluated based on meeting eligibility requirements, review of business financials, location of business, impact of business expansion (new employees, capital investment, additional square footage), and presentation of supporting documents. Award announcements will be made on a rolling basis during December 2024 to January 2025. Grant awards are expected to be paid in February-March 2025. DHCD will initiate a local resolution approval process with the applicant's governing executive body; the local jurisdiction will have 45 days to respond. If approved within 45 days, funding will be processed; if no reply within 45 days, funding is deemed approved. Awardees must submit a final report by March 31, 2026, documenting how funds were used and will complete a questionnaire nine months after receiving funds.

structured_extraction.program_name: Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Federal disaster recovery funding provided through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to support recovery activities in areas affected by disasters. Maryland received multiple allocations of CDBG-DR funds following Hurricane Sandy (2012) and other qualifying disasters. The first allocation of $8.6 million (Disaster Grant #1) was designated specifically for Somerset County. A second allocation of $20 million (Disaster Grant #2) was awarded for remaining recovery needs in multiple counties including Somerset, Allegany, Charles, Dorchester, and Garrett counties. Funds support long-term recovery, restoration of infrastructure and housing, and economic revitalization in the most impacted and distressed areas.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Multiple phases of Community Development Block Grant Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funding administered through the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Disaster Grant #1 provided $8.6 million allocated entirely to Somerset County for housing and economic recovery activities. Disaster Grant #2 provided $20 million for remaining recovery needs, with at least 80% directed to Somerset County (the most impacted and distressed county). Total funding across both grants exceeded $28.6 million. Funds support: (1) Housing recovery activities including rehabilitation and replacement of damaged homes through deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property; (2) Economic recovery including grants and loans to businesses and watermen; (3) Infrastructure improvements including generators, dredging, drainage improvements, water/sewer system upgrades, street resurfacing, bulkhead replacement, jetty construction, shoreline stabilization, and wastewater plant decommissioning; (4) Public facilities including homeless shelters, community buildings, and Head Start facilities; (5) Planning and feasibility studies; (6) Job training activities. All housing assistance provided as deferred loans for low and moderate income households with household income not exceeding 80% of area median income. Business loans available up to $60,000 interest-free for up to 10 years.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications were accepted by January 28, 2014 for Disaster Grant #2. Subsequent phases had varying deadlines as amendments were proposed.
structured_extraction.program_audience: County governments, municipalities, nonprofit organizations, businesses, individuals, and residents in disaster-affected areas. Primary focus on low and moderate income persons and households. Specific audiences include: homeowners and renters with storm-damaged properties; small businesses and watermen; farmers; individuals needing job training; public housing authorities; homeless individuals; senior residents; persons with disabilities; and vulnerable populations in flood-prone areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Recovery activities in disaster-affected areas including: housing rehabilitation and replacement for low and moderate income homeowners; business grants and loans for economic recovery; watermen assistance grants; facade improvement grants; job training; acquisition and demolition of blighted/repetitively damaged properties; infrastructure improvements (generators, drainage systems, water/sewer upgrades, dredging, street repairs); public facilities (homeless shelters, community buildings, Head Start facilities); shoreline stabilization and jetty construction; feasibility studies and planning activities; state and local administrative costs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland counties that received Presidential Disaster Declarations for Hurricane Sandy, Hurricane Irene, Tropical Storm Lee, or the Derecho. Disaster Grant #1 funds allocated entirely to Somerset County. Disaster Grant #2 requires minimum 80% allocation to Somerset County with remaining funds available to Allegany, Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Baltimore City, Calvert, Caroline, Carroll, Cecil, Charles, Dorchester, Frederick, Garrett, Harford, Howard, Kent, Montgomery, Prince George's, Queen Anne's, St. Mary's, Talbot, Washington, Wicomico, and Worcester counties based on disaster declarations and eligible needs.
requirements_list: For housing assistance: Household income cannot exceed 80% of area median income for Somerset County
Proof of homeownership required
Proof of storm damage required
Housing rehabilitation assistance provided as deferred loans repayable upon sale or transfer of property
Full loan amount repaid to county upon property sale or transfer
For business assistance: Proof of business ownership required
Proof of storm damage to business or equipment required
For economic development: Business loans up to $60,000 interest-free for up to 10 years for working capital, construction, inventory, and/or equipment
For job training: Residents must provide household income information compared to HUD income limits; majority of participants must be low and moderate income
For acquisition/demolition: Property must be in floodplain or blighted area with storm damage; must meet relocation assistance requirements if occupied
For public housing: Required to maintain flood insurance in perpetuity on assisted units
All applications received and processed on first-come/first-served basis regardless of race, national origin, or other protected class
No discrimination in program participation based on disability, gender, religion, familial status, marital status, or sexual orientation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications submitted through county governments to Maryland DHCD. Process includes: (1) County conducts comprehensive needs assessment of unmet disaster recovery needs; (2) County holds minimum two public hearings on proposed projects; (3) County adopts written Citizen Participation Plan; (4) County adopts Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan; (5) County passes local resolution authorizing application; (6) County submits application with project proposals and supporting documentation; (7) DHCD reviews applications for completeness and eligibility; (8) DHCD rating committee evaluates projects on benefit (75 points max), readiness to proceed (50 points max), and leveraging (25 points max); (9) DHCD recommends projects for funding to Assistant Secretary; (10) DHCD amends Action Plan to include selected projects; (11) Action Plan amendment made available for 30-day public comment period; (12) DHCD conducts public hearings during comment period; (13) DHCD submits amendment to HUD for approval; (14) HUD reviews and approves amendment; (15) Grant agreements executed between State and HUD; (16) County implements approved projects. Individual housing assistance applications: Homeowners apply through Somerset County; county determines eligibility based on income, damage, and homeownership; county processes loans as deferred obligations. Business assistance: Applications submitted to Somerset County Economic Development Commission; evaluated for eligibility and impact; approved for grants or loans.

structured_extraction.program_description: Program funded by Congress to develop viable communities, provide decent housing and suitable living environments, and expand economic opportunities. Funds help strengthen Maryland's communities by expanding affordable housing opportunities, creating jobs, stabilizing neighborhoods and improving overall quality of life.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Federal funds are allocated by Congress annually to states to distribute to non-entitlement counties, small cities, and towns. For State Fiscal Year 2026, Maryland received $7,416,560 allocated as follows: State Administration $248,331, Technical Assistance $74,165, Community Development $6,000,000 (82% of funds), and Special Projects $1,094,064 (15% of funds). Funds are awarded through two funding categories: the Community Development category, which is competitive and applications are accepted once per year, and the Special Projects category for planning, economic development, and projects meeting special project criteria that can be submitted any time throughout the year after written approval is received. Over a three-year period, the state must use 70 percent of its allocation to benefit persons of low and moderate income. Funds are provided as gap funding for projects selected by jurisdictions to meet their needs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Community Development applications accepted once each year through competitive process. Special Projects applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000. Multiple jurisdictions may jointly apply. Subrecipients may include governmental agencies, non-profit organizations with 501(c)(3) status, for-profit businesses in good standing, Community Based Development Organizations (CBDOs), and Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Eligible projects include acquisition of real property; construction, reconstruction, or installation of public works facilities (water/sewer, streets, parks); code enforcement; demolition and rehabilitation of buildings; removal of barriers for elderly and handicapped persons; public services; planning; relocation assistance; housing activities including acquisition and rehabilitation of housing, rental housing construction, single family housing rehabilitation, homeownership assistance; economic development projects including infrastructure to support businesses; community facilities such as childcare centers, senior centers, community centers, and shelters. All funded projects must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applications from projects in the following entitlement counties and cities cannot be accepted by the State: Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties; and Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury cities. Units of general local government in non-entitlement counties with population less than 200,000 and non-entitlement cities and towns with population less than 50,000 are eligible. Other entities, public or private, may be sub-recipients of eligible local government. Projects must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area, except for public services, single family housing rehabilitation, acquisition and renovation of existing houses, downpayment assistance, or where the Secretary of DHCD determines that the project is necessary to protect public health, to alleviate personal economic hardship in an emergency situation, to promote economically integrated housing, or is consistent with an overall economic development strategy. Towns with population over 51% low and moderate income may use area benefit activities.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a unit of general local government in a non-entitlement county with population less than 200,000 or a non-entitlement city or town with population less than 50,000

Project must meet one of three national objectives: benefit persons of low and moderate income, eliminate slum and blight, or meet an urgent need of recent origin that threatens public health and safety
Project must be eligible activity under CDBG program regulations (Title I of Housing and Community Development Act of 1974)
Project must be located in a Maryland Priority Funding Area (with exceptions noted above)
Over three-year period, state must use 70 percent of allocation cumulatively to benefit persons of low and moderate income
Proposed activities must be eligible under Title I of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, as amended
Proposed subrecipient or business must be eligible

Non-profit organizations must have specific information in organizational bylaws and mission statements that clearly state they primarily serve persons of low and moderate income and/or specific populations eligible for CDBG assistance

For housing rehabilitation: maximum of $40,000 grant per house; grantees may use up to 25% of award for emergency repairs; all housing must be improved and meet local livability code requirements or housing quality standards upon completion
For housing acquisition, renovation and resale: maximum CDBG funds of $200,000 per house

For housing with rental assistance: rents may not exceed Fair Market Rents established annually by HUD for the county; affordability period required based on funding amount (10 years for up to $400,000; 15 years for $400,001-$600,000; 20 years for over $600,001)

For homeownership financial assistance: lien required for 5 years if assistance up to $10,000 or 10 years if assistance over $10,000; no subprime mortgages allowed; no adjustable rate mortgages allowed; mortgages must be fixed rate for minimum 30 years; minimum 8 hours housing counseling from HUD approved agency required
For construction projects with $200,000 or more in HUD funding: Section 3 requirements apply (25% of labor hours by Section 3 workers, minimum 5% by Targeted Section 3 workers)
For multi-family rental housing or government facilities: generators must be installed with sufficient capacity to power lighting in common areas at minimum

For construction or substantial rehabilitation of buildings with more than 4 rental housing units: broadband infrastructure required to provide access to internet connections in individual units (with possible exceptions)
For housing rehabilitation programs: only county governments may apply as grantee, except active municipal programs with open or recent CDBG housing rehabilitation grants

Build America, Buy America (BABA) requirements: all iron, steel, manufactured products and construction materials must be produced in United States; BABA does not apply to projects totaling $250,000 or less or to housing rehabilitation per house costing $250,000 or less
Grantee must comply with Uniform Relocation Act (49 CFR Part 24) for property acquisition and relocation
Grantee must comply with National Environmental Policy Act and 24 CFR Part 58; Environmental Review must be completed prior to project initiation
Grantee must comply with Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity laws and requirements
Conflict of Interest Policy required; no employee, officer or agent may participate in selection, award, or administration of contract if they have real or apparent conflict of interest
Financial management system required meeting federal requirements in 2 CFR Part 200 and 24 CFR 570.489
Single Audit required if grantee spends more than $750,000 of federal funds from any source during fiscal year
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The State notifies eligible localities of fund availability and conducts training sessions on application development. Community Development applications are accepted once each year through a competitive process. The State conducts rating and evaluation of Community Development applications and awards funds based on competitive criteria. Special Projects applications can be submitted at any time throughout the year after written approval is received from the state. Upon approval of funding, applicants must submit required documentation including Citizen Participation Plan, Public Hearing Notice, Local Resolution, Residential Anti-Displacement and Relocation Assistance Plan, Program Income Re-Use Plan, Certification Regarding Debarment and Suspension, and other exhibits as applicable. For housing rehabilitation programs, local program policies must be submitted and approved to ensure all current federal and state policies and requirements are included. Applicants must meet all eligibility requirements and provide documentation demonstrating compliance with program requirements.

structured_extraction.program_description: Grant opportunities to improve the livability and economic potential of Maryland communities through targeted investments in the physical environment that impact health and safety. Provides funding to nonprofits and local governments to implement crime control and prevention strategies through physical design improvements to make facility-related safety improvements and business district public and private spaces safer and more defensible.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding to support community improvements related to health and safety and physical environment enhancements. Funding is provided to implement crime control and prevention strategies through physical design improvements, facility-related safety improvements, and making public and private spaces safer and more defensible.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Currently closed; uncertain if another round will be offered
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland nonprofits (including faith-based organizations), local governments, and communities seeking to improve livability and economic potential through health and safety investments
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Targeted investments in the physical environment that impact health and safety to improve community livability and economic potential. Crime control and prevention strategies through physical design improvements, facility-related safety improvements, and making public and private spaces safer and more defensible.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Application portal is currently closed. Sign up for DHCD news and alerts to stay informed about future rounds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations by awarding allocations of State tax credits that nonprofits can use as incentives to attract contributions from individuals and businesses to benefit local projects and services.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Nonprofit organizations approved for the program receive allocations of State tax credits to incentivize donations. When donors give $500 or more to a qualified organization's approved project, they earn tax credits equal to 50 percent of the value of their money, goods or real property contribution. These tax credits reduce the donor's Maryland tax liability for the year the contribution was made and cannot be carried back to prior years. The maximum request for an award of tax credits is $50,000. Annual awards total $1.75M in Maryland income tax credits. Awards typically require organizations to raise double the amount of tax credits requested (for example, a $50,000 credit award requires $100,000 in donations). All CITC award contracts have a 24-month life, with credits that must be used during that two-year interval.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 19, 2025 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community projects and services including education and youth services, housing and community development, job and self-sufficiency training, enhancing neighborhoods and business districts, arts and culture and historic preservation, economic development and tourism promotion, technical assistance and capacity building, and services for at-risk populations. Eligible expenses include staff costs, rent, utilities, program supplies, training, travel, construction soft costs such as planning, design, engineering, and permitting, as well as direct construction expenses for capital projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA). For capital projects, the project site must be located within a PFA boundary. For operating projects, organizations must document that clients served reside within a Priority Funding Area boundary.
requirements_list: Applicant must be an IRS designated 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization with current IRS Determination Letter
Organization must be in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Organization must be registered as a charity with the Office of the Secretary of State (or have religious exemption documentation)
Projects must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area
Donors must contribute $500 or more to receive tax credits
Donors must be individuals or businesses subject to State income tax, public service company franchise tax, or insurance premiums tax
Contributions can be in the form of money, goods, or real property
Donors must complete a Donor Acknowledgement Form
Tax credits equal 50 percent of the value of the contribution
Tax credits must be used against taxes owed for the year the contribution was made
For capital projects, organization must document site control via deed, title/real estate settlement documents, executed lease with owner's permission, or similar evidence
All project work must commence on or after January 1, 2026 and conclude by December 31, 2027
Maximum tax credit request is $50,000; typical awards are at least $10,000
New applicants must complete registration in the IGX Project Portal (up to 72 hours for approval)
Organization Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws must be current and include all amendments
Current list of Board of Directors and Officers must be provided
Current Priority Funding Area maps required for all project locations
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Nonprofit organizations apply through an annual competitive application process. The FY26 application round opens May 19, 2025 and closes June 19, 2025 at 5 PM. Applicants must be registered users in the DHCD IGX Project Portal. New users must complete a registration request form which may take up to 72 hours to be approved. Prior to starting an application, organizations must ensure all organization information and required legal documents are uploaded to their Profile. Applications are submitted entirely online through the Project Portal and must include: Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, IRS 501(c)(3) Determination Letter, current Board of Directors list, current Charitable Registration Letter or exemption letter from Maryland Secretary of State, SDAT good standing status screenshot, executed Corporate Resolution, and Priority Funding Area maps for each project location. For capital projects, evidence of site control must be provided. All uploaded documents must be in PDF format. Award decisions will be announced in Fall 2025. The FY26 award period runs from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027. Awardees must submit electronic Tax Credit Certification Requests within 30 days of receiving donations and four Semi-Annual Reports (due July 10 and January 10 during the award period). Organizations must maintain charitable registration, good standing status, and records for seven years following award completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Legacy program provides local governments and community development organizations with funding for essential projects aimed at strengthening communities through activities such as business retention and attraction, encouraging homeownership and commercial revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding is provided for projects located in Sustainable Communities or in Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset and Wicomico Counties. Projects can support mixed-use development, business retention and expansion, streetscape improvements, homeownership initiatives, façade improvements, and real estate acquisition.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community development organizations including county councils, community development corporations, main street organizations, and downtown partnerships, and groups of local governments sharing a common purpose or goal.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects must capitalize on the strengths of a community while addressing revitalization challenges and help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Eligible uses include mixed-use development consisting of residential, commercial and/or open space, business retention and expansion initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation programs, residential and commercial façade improvements, and real estate acquisition including land banking and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Community Legacy funding can only be used in areas known as Sustainable Communities or in an Opportunity Zone in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset and Wicomico Counties. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to determine geographic eligibility.
requirements_list: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities or Opportunity Zones in Allegany, Garrett, Somerset and Wicomico Counties
Projects should address community revitalization challenges
Projects should help achieve a local government's Sustainable Communities Action Plan
Projects should aim to stabilize a community, reverse social, economic or physical decline or encourage sustainable growth
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For information on how to apply, refer to the State Revitalization Programs webpage.

structured_extraction.program_description: Emergency financial assistance for families and students enrolled in community schools who are struggling with rent payments, facing eviction, or experiencing homelessness. The program helps eligible households secure housing and avoid housing instability.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides emergency financial assistance to eligible families and students in community schools. Assistance covers: (1) past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; (2) moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, application fees, and first month's rent; and (3) future rent and utility assistance related to housing instability, up to 3 months at a time. The maximum length of assistance a household can receive is 15 months. Assistance is provided based on need and availability of funds. Households may receive repeat assistance contingent on availability of program funds and qualifying circumstances. Funding is limited with most jurisdictions on interest-only status or waitlist.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families and students enrolled in community schools who are experiencing housing instability including homelessness, at risk of eviction, or behind on rent or utility payments.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Assistance can be used to pay past due rent or utility bills including late fees and court fees related to eviction; moving costs and deposits needed to rent a new home such as security deposit, application fees, and first month's rent; and future rent and utility assistance (up to 3 months) related to housing instability. The program can also assist with relocation costs for households living in uninhabitable or unsafe conditions.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in participating jurisdictions: Anne Arundel County, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Frederick County, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Washington County, and Wicomico County. Applicants must be renting or trying to rent a home in one of these jurisdictions. Assistance can only be provided to households that have a student enrolled in a community school in the county where they are requesting assistance.
requirements_list: Have at least one student enrolled in a Community School in a participating jurisdiction
Be experiencing homelessness or at risk of housing instability (such as a past due utility or rent notice, an eviction notice, or unsafe or unhealthy living conditions)
Be responsible for paying rent or utilities in a qualifying rental unit
Students must attend a community school, not a public school outside the community school designation
Proof of student's community school enrollment is required
Proof of rental agreement is required
Invoice or proof of missed rent or utility payments is required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications can be obtained from the local nonprofit organization serving your county. Each county has its own application process and local provider contact information available through DHCD's website. If you are unable to complete the application online, you can reach out to the agency and request a paper copy of the application. Community school staff may help identify eligible families, coordinate referrals, and support outreach and engagement. The specific application contact for each county's nonprofit provider is available on DHCD's Community Schools page.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program supports a range of direct services designed to assist low-income individuals and families with achieving self-sufficiency. Services are provided through a statewide network of seventeen Community Action Agencies that serve every jurisdiction in Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Community Action Agencies receive 90 percent of the federal CSBG allocation to Maryland to operate programs and services that help low-income individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency. The state utilizes five percent of the federal allocation as discretionary funding to support activities and programs conducted by Community Action Agencies or other non-profit organizations to eliminate poverty, promote self-sufficiency, and stimulate community revitalization. Discretionary funds may support training, technical assistance, and coordination among Community Action Agencies. For FFY 2025-2026, the total 93 percent allocation to eligible entities is $9,786,612.00 per year. Eligible entities must meet organizational standards and demonstrate measurable outcomes that help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: The FY25 application round is closed. Check this page for information about future funding rounds.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Angela Fraser, Assistant Director, Division of Homeless Solutions
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low-income individuals and families in urban and rural areas throughout Maryland. Services are provided in all twenty-three Maryland counties and Baltimore City through the statewide network of seventeen Community Action Agencies.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Direct services to help individuals and families achieve self-sufficiency, including elimination of poverty, promotion of self-sufficiency, and community revitalization activities. Eligible uses include support for poverty solutions and linkages between Eligible Entities and State government agencies to better serve Maryland's most vulnerable populations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services are provided in all twenty-three Maryland counties and the City of Baltimore through the statewide network of Community Action Agencies. Each county is served by a designated Community Action Agency.
requirements_list: Individual and household income at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty guidelines
For CSBG Discretionary funding, proposed programs must display measurable outcomes that help families and individuals move toward self-sufficiency
Eligible entities must meet CSBG Organizational Standards Center of Excellence (COE) standards

Community Action Agencies that are designated eligible entities must maintain a tripartite board with representation from persons in poverty, providers of services to the poor, and other interests in the community
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Community Action Agencies that are designated eligible entities apply for the 90 percent allocation of funds through the state's funding formula based on poverty, unemployment, and rural status. For CSBG Discretionary funding, Community Action Agencies, non-profit organizations, and units of local government may apply. Payment requests are processed through the Department's online project portal and reviewed by the Division of Finance and Administration. The FY25 application round is currently closed. Contact the state CSBG point of contact or visit the program website for information about future funding rounds.

structured_extraction.program_description: Supports local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions in creating computer labs and centers that provide public computer access for underserved populations including people with disabilities, unhoused individuals, veterans, and formerly incarcerated individuals.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants up to $65,000 covering 100% of eligible costs for creation, upgrade and retrofit of computer labs and centers, plus up to $10,000 for internet service subscription costs for up to three years. Majority (50% or higher) of lab users must be from covered populations: individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens. Eligible uses include computer equipment (desktops, laptops, keyboards, mice, monitors), networking equipment (routers, switches, cables, Wi-Fi access points, firewalls), internet service subscriptions, marketing and outreach (up to 10% of budget), operational expenses (up to 15% of budget including staff salaries and lab maintenance), administrative expenses (up to 15% of budget including training and security monitoring), software (operating systems, productivity suites, educational training software, antivirus), audiovisual equipment (projectors, screens, smartboards for training), assistive technology (screen readers, magnifiers, adaptive keyboards), and miscellaneous connectivity items. Total of $2 million available from American Rescue Plan Act funding.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: November 29, 2024 by 11:59 PM ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions seeking to provide public computer access to individuals with disabilities, unhoused individuals, veterans, and incarcerated/returning citizens
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Creation, upgrade and retrofit of computer labs and centers to provide public computer access; computer equipment and networking equipment purchases; internet service subscription costs for up to three years; staff salaries and lab maintenance; training for instructional staff; marketing and outreach to covered populations; assistive technology for accessibility; and security monitoring exclusively for the computer lab/center
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide (all Maryland counties eligible); projects must be completed by December 31, 2026
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include Maryland local jurisdictions, incorporated municipalities, local government agencies delegated by Maryland jurisdictions, not-for-profit IRS-approved 501(c) entities providing services within Maryland, and Community Anchor Institutions within Maryland

Community Anchor Institution defined as entity such as school, institution of higher education, public housing organization, or community support organization that facilitates greater use of computer devices by vulnerable populations including veterans, formerly incarcerated individuals, unhoused individuals, and people with disabilities
50% or more of lab users must be individuals with disabilities, homeless/unhoused individuals, veterans, or incarcerated/returning citizens
Computer equipment must come with standard manufacturer warranty or extended warranty
Desktops or laptops must have updated operating systems
Internet service subscription must include only wired internet connection (no Wi-Fi hotspots)
Marketing and outreach limited to 10% of total project budget
Operational expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
Administrative expenses limited to 15% of total project budget
Applications must be complete in their entirety; missing information may result in application being deemed ineligible
Applicants must provide proof of non-profit status (501(c) documentation) or local jurisdiction documentation
All federal rules regarding ARPA funding must be adhered to
Technical assistance requests must be made prior to November 22, 2024

Ineligible uses include routine operational costs (utilities, rent), building construction or renovation, non-broadband utility infrastructure, furniture (desks, chairs, ergonomic accessories), office furniture not tied to broadband use, non-technical office supplies, printers, photocopiers, scanners, Wi-Fi hotspots, entertainment/video games, personal use devices, travel expenses, political/lobbying activities, traditional textbooks, duplicative projects, and advertising unrelated to digital equity
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted by November 29, 2024 at 11:59 PM ET. Electronic submission is preferred via email to osb.de@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Computer Labs Program Application–Organizational Applicant name'. Files should be converted to PDFs prior to sending and clearly named. Alternatively, paper applications with original signatures may be postmarked, shipped, or hand-delivered to: Ronnie Hammond, Office of Statewide Broadband, Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Paper applications must show proof of mailing via legible USPS postmark, USPS-dated mail receipt, or dated shipping label/receipt from commercial carrier received on or before deadline. Hand-delivered applications accepted daily 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM ET, except Saturdays, Sundays, and State or Federal holidays; valid identification required. Applications must include: completed Application Form, written Executive Summary and Scope of Work with timeline, Project Budget with detailed breakdown by category (Operations, Contracted Services, Travel, and other funding sources), Federal Form W-9, 501(c) documents for nonprofits (if applicable), and Certificate of Good Standing (if applicable). Project narrative must address Executive Summary, Potential Barriers, Partners and Local Engagement, Intended Outcomes and Metrics, Statement of Experience, and Timeline. All applicants selected for funding will be required to execute a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) outlining obligations. OSB intends to award funds beginning December 2024. Technical assistance available prior to November 22, 2024.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY23 Network Infrastructure Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions or their ISP partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households and businesses. Grant funding covers 70-90% of capital construction costs based on project density, with applicants required to provide matching funds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $800,000 and $4,500,000 covering 70-90% of capital construction costs for broadband infrastructure. Match requirement ranges from 10-30% of total construction costs based on project density: Wired infrastructure projects require 10% match (fewer than 8 premises per mile), 20% match (8-14 premises per mile), or 30% match (15+ premises per mile). Wireless infrastructure projects require 10% match (fewer than 40 premises per tower), 20% match (40-69 premises per tower), or 30% match (70+ premises per tower). Match must be in cash and cannot fund operational costs. Exceptions available for federal funding as match and Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul services (up to 3 years). Tower construction/upgrades may be treated as match. Areas receiving prior state grant funding are ineligible. Grants must comply with American Rescue Plan Act requirements and provide broadband service at minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable and certified). All grant-funded costs must be for new, non-depreciated capital assets including outside plant, middle mile infrastructure, and electronic equipment.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 5, 2022, 11:59pm ET
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland local jurisdictions and their ISP partners (for-profit, non-profit, and cooperative entities recognized as partners by local jurisdictions)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure serving unserved homes and businesses. Eligible uses include: construction of outside plant (last mile and middle mile infrastructure), electronic equipment necessary to deliver service (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radios, antennas, equipment shelters), customer drops, customer premises equipment (up to ONT or fixed wireless antenna), middle mile infrastructure (if no other provider available), tower construction and structural improvements (as match only), and engineering costs tied to funded capital assets. Ineligible uses: operating expenses, bandwidth and spectrum expenses, salaries not directly related to construction, leases, building purchases or renovations, land purchases, laptop/handset/tablet devices, tower purchases, duplication of existing broadband service, or expenses incurred before application submission.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide, excluding areas that have received prior state grant funding (2019-2021 Expansion, 2020-2021 Infrastructure, 2022 Neighborhood Connect, 2022 Infrastructure programs). All Maryland counties eligible. Proposed Funded Service Area (PFSA) must be entirely unserved with no broadband service currently available, verified by OSB prior to award.
requirements_list: Applicant must be Maryland local jurisdiction, incorporated organization recognized as partner by local jurisdiction, or other legal entity (cooperative, private corporation, limited liability company) recognized as partner by local jurisdiction. Cannot be individual or partnership.
Must serve entirely unserved premises where no Broadband Service exists (no service at 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up)
Must provide minimum broadband service at 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 millisecond latency, or 100 Mbps down/20 Mbps up if scalable and certified
Areas with prior state grant funding are ineligible
Match requirement 10-30% of total construction costs based on project density (wired or wireless)
Match must be in cash and available upon grant agreement execution
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
Project commencement by September 1, 2023 and completion by August 31, 2026
Applicant must have legal capacity and authority to own and operate broadband facilities
Applicant must comply with all federal, state, and local statutes and regulations
If partnering with another entity, must provide written agreement addressing financial terms
Minimum grant request $800,000; maximum $4,500,000
Must pass all unserved premises in PFSA at Broadband Grant Speed
If federal funding used as match, must be eligible federal funds and cannot supplant previously awarded federal funds
All grant-funded costs must be capital expenses capitalized on balance sheet
Projects over $10 million may require Davis-Bacon wage certification or project labor agreement certification and documentation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete application package by December 5, 2022, 11:59pm ET by mail (with proof of postmark/shipping), email to OSB.MD@maryland.gov, or physical delivery to Kenrick M. Gordon, OSB Director, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. If mailed, proof of mailing required (USPS postmark, USPS-dated mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier). Electronic submissions via email should use subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – your company name' and include zipped files converted to PDF format (except where specified otherwise). Required application components: (A) Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS W-9, proof of legal existence and good standing, local jurisdiction partnership letter; (B) Executive Summary describing PFSA, applicant history, partnership details if applicable, community benefits, and project need; (C) Scoring Criteria Documentation; (D) System Design including network diagram; (E) Service Area Demographics and map in .shp/.kml/.kmz format with property list; (F) Scope of Work including construction build-out/milestones and project budget; (G) Financial Information and Sustainability including historical financial statements, pro forma financial statements, and assumptions; (H) Statement of Experience; (I) Evidence of Funding Commitments from Other Sources. Prior to official submission, applicants may request technical assistance through November 18, 2022. Upon award, applicants must execute grant agreement and comply with conditions precedent including submission of project plans and compliance with all terms. Grant funds disbursed on reimbursement basis upon submission of detailed expense requests with supporting invoices. Interim progress reports required quarterly on January 1, April 1, July 1, and October 1. Final report required within 45 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_name: Connect Maryland: FY24 Network Infrastructure Grant Program - Smith Island
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to local jurisdictions or their ISP partners to construct new broadband networks serving unserved households on Smith Island. Grant funding covers up to 90% of capital construction costs with a minimum 10% cash match required. Funding source is the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Capital Projects Fund administered by the US Treasury.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $1,000,000 and $3,000,000 covering up to 90% of eligible capital construction costs. Minimum 10% cash match required (11.11% equivalent of grant amount). Grant funds support construction of broadband infrastructure to deliver service at 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds (100x100 symmetrical) with maximum 50 millisecond latency to all unserved premises on Smith Island. Eligible expenses include outside plant infrastructure (fiber optic cabling, conduit, poles), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, wireless radios, antenna, equipment cabinets), middle mile infrastructure, engineering costs tied to funded capital assets, and tower construction/structural improvements. Ineligible expenses include operating costs, bandwidth costs, tower purchases/leases, land/building purchases, building renovations, customer premise equipment beyond ONT, and customer devices (laptops, tablets, handsets). Match funds must be in cash; in-kind contributions are not eligible. Exceptions to match requirement may apply for federal funding or Maryland Broadband Cooperative backhaul service costs (up to 3 years).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 11:59pm ET January 31, 2024
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions and their ISP partners (incorporated organizations, cooperatives, private corporations, limited liability companies recognized as partners by local jurisdictions) seeking to construct broadband infrastructure serving Smith Island
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for new broadband network infrastructure on Smith Island including outside plant (fiber, conduit, poles, cabling), electronic equipment (OLTs, ONTs, routers, switches, wireless equipment), middle mile infrastructure, equipment cabinets/shelters, tower construction, and engineering services directly tied to capital assets. Funds must serve all unserved households and businesses on Smith Island.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Smith Island, Somerset County, Maryland. All locations on Smith Island included in Identified Service Area (ISA) as defined by latitude/longitude coordinates. Applicant must provide evidence of legal existence and good standing with the State of Maryland
Applicant must have Unique Entity ID from SAM.gov and current IRS Form W-9
Applicant must not be debarred by any federal, state, or local government entity or subject to civil claims for non-payment of $30,000 or more in past 4 years
Project must serve entire Identified Service Area where broadband service does not currently exist

Project must comply with all federal rules regarding ARPA funding and Treasury regulations

All work must conform to approved application and comply with local, state, and federal requirements

No duplication of existing broadband service provided by other entities
