structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications must be submitted postmarked or received by 11:59pm ET on January 31, 2024. Submit via: (1) paper copy with original signatures and electronic version on USB Flash Drive to Kenrick M. Gordon, P.E., Director, OSB of Statewide Broadband, DHCD, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706, or (2) email with files as zipped attachment to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'Maryland Network Infrastructure Grant Application – Smith Island – your company name'. Paper applications must show proof of mailing (USPS postmark, dated mail receipt, or dated shipping label from commercial carrier). Late applications will not be considered. Required application components include: (A) Completed Broadband Grant Application Form (Schedule A-1), IRS Form W-9, proof of good standing/legal existence, and partnership documentation from local jurisdiction(s); (B) Executive Summary covering ISA description and project need, applicant description and history, total project costs, and general system overview; (C) Scoring Criteria Documentation addressing project strength, project description, contribution above match, organizational experience, and timeline; (D) System Design including network diagram showing technologies and route map; (E) Service Area Demographics; (F) Scope of Work with construction build-out/project milestones (Schedule F-1) and project budget (Schedule F-2); (G) Financial Information and Sustainability including historical financial statements and pro forma financial statement (Schedule G-1); (H) Statement of Experience; (I) Evidence of Funding Commitments from Other Sources. Technical assistance available upon request made prior to January 19, 2024. Applicants may request clarification after submission. Applications scoring highest receive funding as available. Grant Agreement required upon award. Disbursement on reimbursement basis as project progresses with requests submitted per Procedures Guide. Minimum 50% of grant funds must be expended by second anniversary of agreement effective date. Project completion required by August 31, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: Assists local community-based organizations, non-profits, anchor institutions, and local governments in creating gap networks and community networks designed to address internet affordability challenges for low to moderate income households by providing equipment, infrastructure, and services at low or no cost.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $25,000 and $250,000 (or potentially higher as evidenced by awards exceeding these amounts) covering up to 100% of costs for construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of community-based gap networks and community networks. Funds support equipment (optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems), network infrastructure, operations, and maintenance. Total of $5 million available from American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (counties and municipalities), nonprofit corporations (501(c) entities), community-based anchor institutions, and community-based organizations providing services within Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction, deployment, expansion, or continuation of gap networks and community networks; network equipment and infrastructure; operations and maintenance of networks; equipment necessary to deliver service to end users including optical line terminals (OLT's), optical network terminals (ONT's), routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters; making broadband services available to covered populations at low or no cost
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Eligible project areas must be identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connections reliably meeting or exceeding symmetrical 100 Mbps download and upload speeds, lack of affordable access to broadband service, or lack of reliable broadband.

Must be registered and in good standing with Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation

Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps symmetrical download and upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds, or alternatively 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload if scalable to symmetrical 100 Mbps speeds
Technology neutral - any technology capable of meeting speed and latency requirements is permissible

Must attach IRS W-9 Form and Certificate of Good Standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit complete applications by March 31, 2022 to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with subject line 'MD-GAPS: Name of Applying Organization'. Applications must include: Applicant Information (legal name, EIN, DUNS number, address, contact information), Project Information (funding sources, project area description, required speed capabilities, delivery method), Project Summary addressing executive summary, statement of experience, network design, community profile, subscriber cost, potential barriers, partners and local engagement, intended outcomes and sustainability, implementation schedule, and funding scope and budget. Application must also include Project Budget and Federal Form W-9 and Certificate of Good Standing. Awards will be announced May 2022 with projects required completion by December 31, 2023. Successful applicants selected based on qualifications and evaluation of responses with possible interviews.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that funds digital inclusion efforts to enable access to high-speed internet and expand digital literacy in Maryland. Provides funding to local jurisdictions, 501(c) non-profit entities, and community-based anchor institutions to advance digital inclusion efforts through planning and implementation projects to address the digital divide in Maryland. Applicants can receive funding to develop digital inclusion plans, implement digital inclusion activities, facilitate broadband adoption, provide training programs, and construct or operate public access computing centers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Two funding tracks: Digital Inclusion Planning provides up to 50% of planning costs with a maximum request of $30,000 and minimum of $5,000. Digital Inclusion Program Implementation provides up to 100% of implementation costs with a maximum request of $75,000 and minimum of $10,000. Total of $2 million available. Funding source is American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds administered by the US Treasury. Grant amounts may be reduced based on the impact of the applicant's intended population and ability to deploy funds responsibly. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions, 501(c) non-profit entities, and community-based anchor institutions serving covered populations including individuals with income at or below 150% of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups, and individuals in rural areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Digital inclusion planning and implementation of digital inclusion programs including: enhancing understanding of internet service, assisting households with internet service applications, providing digital literacy training, enhancing community capacity for civic participation and educational opportunities, researching and assisting populations with low adoption rates for home internet and computers, constructing or operating public access computing centers, implementing workforce development programs, developing digital inclusion plans, implementing digital inclusion activities, and facilitating broadband adoption for covered populations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland communities eligible. Services must be provided within the State of Maryland. Funding priority given to covered populations most in need.

Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
All funded projects must comply with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) requirements and federal rules

structured_extraction.program_name: EmPOWER Maryland Limited Income Energy Efficiency Program
structured_extraction.program_description: EmPOWER provides free energy efficiency upgrades and improvements to limited income households to reduce energy use, lower monthly power bills, improve home comfort, and enhance air quality and family health.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides free installation of energy efficiency materials and equipment at no charge to eligible homeowners. Improvements may include attic, floor, and wall insulation; hot water system improvements; lighting retrofits; furnace cleaning, tuning, and safety repairs; refrigerator retrofits; and health and safety items. A local agency conducts an energy audit to identify the most effective energy-saving improvements, coordinates contractor work, and performs a follow-up evaluation. There is no cost to applicants for the audit, installation of improvements, or follow-up evaluation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - applications accepted year-round
structured_extraction.program_audience: Limited income homeowners in Maryland who are utility customers of BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy efficiency upgrades and home improvements including insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofits, furnace work, refrigerator retrofits, and health and safety items.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide in Maryland for customers of participating utility companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, and Washington Gas.
requirements_list: Household income must be at or below 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Level based on household size (ranging from $72,950 for a single-person household to $165,050 for a ten-person household)
Must have an active utility account with one of six participating companies: BGE, Delmarva Power, FirstEnergy, Pepco, SMECO, or Washington Gas

Automatically income-eligible if currently receiving Utility Bill Pay Assistance through OHEP, SNAP, TANF, SSI, HUD housing assistance, Fuel Fund Assistance, DHCD Rehab Programs, Baltimore Lead Hazard Control Program, Medicaid, MEA Energy Equity Grant, or MEEHA
Applicant must own the home or have documented proof of home ownership
If in a mobile home, copy of title or bill of sale required to prove ownership
For quick application track: must receive benefits from one of the eligible assistance programs
For standard application track: must provide proof of last 30 days gross household income
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can complete an easy online pre-application or submit a paper program application with required documents. There are two application tracks: (1) Quick Application Track - for those currently receiving benefits from eligible assistance programs; (2) Standard Application Track - for those meeting income requirements. After eligibility determination, a local agency schedules a home energy audit, discusses results with the homeowner, coordinates contractor work for recommended improvements, and conducts a follow-up evaluation. Individuals currently approved for Energy Assistance payments from the Maryland Department of Human Services can contact the intake line at 1-855-583-8976. Applications should be submitted to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Net Zero Loan Program provides low-interest construction financing to support the building of energy-efficient homes that produce as much or more energy than they consume. Eligible projects include new construction or deep energy retrofits of existing homes that achieve a Home Energy Rating System (HERS) rating of 50 or lower. The program offers direct construction loans to builders, developers, and homeowners, as well as loan enhancements for those securing financing from private lenders.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low-interest construction loans are available with interest rates ranging from 2% to 5% depending on the HERS score and whether more than 50% of units are affordable to households at or below 60% of Area Median Income. Market rate loans range from 3% to 5% based on HERS score (0-15: 3%, 16-35: 4%, 36-50: 5%). Discounted rates of 2% to 4% apply when more than 50% of units serve lower-income households. Closing fees include a 1% administration fee and $290 appraisal fee. Loan to value ratio is up to 90%. Typical construction period is 12 months with 12 months for loan repayment for projects intended for sale. Loan enhancements are also available for applicants working with private lenders. An additional fee may apply in the event funding is provided as a loan.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications are accepted until available funds are committed
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, builders, developers, and investors who are qualified to do business in Maryland and can demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction or rehabilitation of new homes or deep energy retrofits of existing homes designed to achieve net zero energy status with a HERS rating of 50 or lower.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be constructed in Maryland and properly zoned for residential use.
requirements_list: Applicant must be qualified to do business in Maryland
Applicant must have legal capacity and all necessary authorization to incur the loan obligation
Applicant must demonstrate creditworthiness and repayment ability acceptable to the department
Applicant must demonstrate ability to complete the project
Project must be new construction or deep energy retrofit of an existing home
Project must achieve HERS rating of 50 or lower
Project must be properly zoned for residential use
Project must be constructed or rehabilitated in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal building codes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the Energy Efficient Homes Construction Loan (Net Zero) Program application form and submit the completed application along with all required documentation by email to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov with a copy to Thomas.Walz@maryland.gov. Required documents include organizational documents (Certificate of Good Standing, Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, Corporate Resolutions), financial statements, evidence of ownership (Deed or Purchase Contract), zoning letter, insurance documentation (Property/Builder's Risk, Borrower's Liability, and Flood Insurance with DHCD listed as certificate holder/additional insured), and construction documents (Plans and Specifications, Budget, Draw Schedule, Construction Schedule, General Contractor's Liability Insurance, General Contractor's Certification, Building Permits, and HERS Rating). The department may request additional documents as needed during the underwriting process.

structured_extraction.program_name: FY24 Home Stretch - Difficult to Serve Properties Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to county jurisdictions to assist with capital construction costs for installing broadband service to remote properties or areas where broadband infrastructure is distant, making service difficult for internet service providers to deliver. The program aims to connect unserved difficult-to-serve premises to existing broadband networks where properties lack terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Up to $24,223,815 total state funding available from Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (CPF). Maximum of $1,100,000 per eligible county jurisdiction applicant; maximum of $8,000 per individual difficult-to-serve property location. Requires 25% match of eligible capital construction costs, which can be contributed by the local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination thereof. County develops sub-grant program with ISP partner(s) for installation of broadband service. Funding covers capital construction costs for deploying facilities to connect unserved premises to existing broadband networks, including minor extensions of ISP infrastructure, equipment such as ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, and access points. All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated. Applicants must pay all non-capital expenses related to required state and federal reporting and ongoing administrative costs for project duration.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: On or before December 22, 2023
structured_extraction.program_audience: County jurisdictions partnered with Internet Service Providers (ISPs)
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs for broadband service installation to difficult-to-serve properties, including: construction of facilities to deploy broadband service; electronics necessary to deliver service to end users (ONTs, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems); necessary equipment shelters; antenna masts, enhanced receiving equipment, and antenna arrays for wireless technologies; satellite receiving equipment for satellite providers meeting speed and latency requirements. Cannot be used for: duplication of existing broadband service; middle mile infrastructure; telephone or video service expenses; land or tower purchases; building construction or renovations; operating expenses.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide - all Maryland counties eligible. Award funding anticipated for February 2024. Projects must be completed by December 31, 2025.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a local county jurisdiction
Applicant must have entered partnership with ISP partner(s) prior to funding agreement
Unserved premises must lack terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds of 100 Mbps download and/or 20 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds
Properties must be remote or distant from broadband infrastructure, or have other geographic issues discouraging ISP service
Maximum $8,000 per difficult-to-serve property location
Maximum $1,100,000 per county jurisdiction applicant
25% match of eligible capital construction costs required
Match can be from local jurisdiction, ISP partner, property owner, or combination thereof; must be in cash form (in-kind matches not acceptable)
All partnering ISPs must participate in federal Affordable Connectivity Program (ACP)
ISPs must promote ACP and provide assistance to subscribers wishing to utilize the program

Network must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload with maximum 50ms latency (or 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload with certification if geography/topography/cost prevents higher speeds, with network scalable to 100 Mbps symmetrical in future)
Applicant must develop jurisdictional-specific funding program with ISP partner(s)
Program must include outreach component to promote the program
Program must address treatment of financially distressed property owners
Sufficient match must be available for each reimbursement requested
All equipment and materials must be new and non-depreciated
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: County jurisdiction must partner with one or more ISP(s) that participate in the federal ACP program. Applicant develops jurisdictional-specific funding program including details on end user selection process, assistance for low-income users, ISP billing methods, acceptable costs, ACP assistance, and ACP promotion. Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete application package to osb.md@maryland.gov by December 22, 2023 with subject line including 'Difficult to Serve Premises Grant Application' and county name. Application must include: completed Grant Application Form (with certifications from both local jurisdiction and ISP partner), Executive Summary describing community needs and project benefits, identification of ISP partner(s) and cooperation offered, statement of senior team experience from applicant and ISP partner, network description including technology and capabilities, subscriber profile with demographic data, subscriber service options and costs, capital construction cost estimates, detailed program overview including user selection and low-income options, schedule with key milestones. All application items must be combined into one zip file or shared via cloud service link. File names must clearly identify contents. Proprietary or confidential information should be identified. Applications will be scored on 45-point scale based on need for service and project benefits (up to 5 points), match contribution source and percentage (up to 15 points), network delivery speed (up to 5 points), and subscriber options including affordability and service limitations (up to 20 points). Awards made high to low score as funding permits. ISP partners may be added after award with OSB approval.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides loans to homeowners to buy out (redeem) ground leases. A ground lease is a long-term lease (usually 99 years) that is renewable forever and requires periodic ground rent payments by the tenant to the ground lease holder. The program was created by the Maryland General Assembly in 2007.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans to homeowners to redeem (buy out) ground leases at 0% interest over 30 years. The maximum loan amount is $3,500, including transactional costs of up to $1,000. Transactional costs are associated with title search and loan closing. The redemption amount is calculated by dividing the annual ground rent fee by a capitalization rate based on the year the ground lease was established (0.04 for April 8, 1884 to April 5, 1888; 0.06 for April 6, 1888 to July 1, 1982; 0.12 for July 2, 1982 or later). A lien is recorded against the property for the loan amount. The program cannot provide grants for this purpose.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners with ground leases who want to redeem (buy out) their leases. Applicants must own the subject property, occupy it as their principal residence, and meet household income limits based on 80 percent of the statewide median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To purchase (redeem) ground leases
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Ground rents are most prevalent in Baltimore City but are held in some other counties as well. Available statewide in Maryland.
requirements_list: Must own the subject property and occupy it as principal residence
Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of statewide median income (varies by household size and region)
Must provide proof of ownership (copy of deed)
Must provide evidence of ground rent (copy of recorded document)
Must provide documentation of household income (most recent month of pay stubs, 2 years of federal tax returns and W-2 statements or Affidavit of Tax Filing Status)
Must provide mortgage verification or current mortgage statement if applicable
Must provide copy of first page of homeowners insurance and flood insurance policies
Must provide copy of most recent county and local property tax bill
Must provide copy of most recent bank statements (all pages)
Must provide copy of most recent ground rent billing statement
If behind on ground rent payments, applicant may still apply
If others are named on the deed but do not live at the property, they must provide proof of residence elsewhere (driver's license copy, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
If ground lease was established as irredeemable, redemption may not be available unless notice of irredeemability was not filed or lapsed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicant must complete the DHCD Ground Rent Redemption Loan application and provide evidence of ownership, ground rent documentation, and household income documentation. The borrower selects a qualified title company to conduct the title search and loan closing. Applications can be obtained from the DHCD website at DHCD.Maryland.gov/wholehome or by calling (301) 429-4150 or 1-844-369-4150. Submit the completed Ground Rent Redemption Loan Application with all required supporting documentation to Special Loan Programs.

structured_extraction.program_description: Helps individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations construct, acquire, or modify existing housing to serve as group homes or assisted living units for people with special housing needs. The program also refinances mortgages on existing group homes. Funding comes from state funds and tax-exempt mortgage revenue bonds.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0 to 7 percent depending on funding source and project cash flow. Maximum term is generally 30 years, though up to 40 years is possible. Construction term may not exceed one year. Loan amounts vary by geographic location and are based on $125,000 per bedroom maximum (15% increase allowed for Montgomery, Prince George's, and Howard Counties). Loans may include provisions for deferral of interest and/or principal (generally not permitted for more than a two-year period). Nonprofit sponsors must contribute 5 percent equity; individual sponsors must contribute 10 percent equity. Loans are typically combined with Special Housing Opportunities Program loans. For refinance loans, financing up to 100% of appraised value for first lien position and 95% for second lien position is available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Program not currently accepting applications
structured_extraction.contact_name: Special Loans Program, Community Development Administration
structured_extraction.program_audience: Individuals, qualified limited partnerships, and nonprofit organizations that provide group homes to eligible residents with special housing needs. Eligible special needs groups include developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, homeless persons, and victims of sex trafficking.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan funds may be used to refinance existing group home mortgages or for development costs including acquisition, closing costs, appraisal and inspection fees, and modification costs. Eligible modifications include repair or replacement of major systems, accessibility modifications, lead paint abatement, general repairs and upgrades, and minor improvements to meet state and local occupancy codes. Group homes that house four or more individuals may use up to 10 percent of building space for nonresidential uses that offer goods or services benefiting lower income or disadvantaged persons, if in conformance with local zoning requirements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects may be located anywhere in Maryland. For Special Housing Opportunities Program financing, property must be located in a Priority Funding Area unless a waiver is granted on an exceptional basis for existing construction. Property must be in compliance with applicable state and local housing and occupancy codes.
requirements_list: Residents must be special needs groups such as developmentally or physically disabled, elderly, juveniles, homeless persons, or victims of sex trafficking
Sponsors must maintain 51 percent of all beds available for residents with incomes 60 percent or less of area median income
Preference given to projects housing residents with incomes below 30 percent of area median income

All applicants must be licensed by the appropriate Maryland licensing authority to operate the project, or be eligible in whole or in part for federal housing programs or incentives including low-income housing credits
Nonprofit organizations must have 501(c)(3) IRS designation for Special Housing Opportunities Program funding
Property must be in good repair and in compliance with state and local housing and occupancy codes or able to be made so with loan proceeds
Appraisal must be completed by an appraiser on the approved appraisers list and is valid for 120 days before approval; if between 120 days and one year old on note date, property may need reappraisal
Property must have home inspection acceptable to the department, completed no more than 120 days before approval

All properties built before 1978 require lead paint risk assessment by certified and accredited lead paint testing company; if hazards exist, sponsor must obtain bid from certified lead paint contractor to reduce hazard as part of renovation
Group homes must meet local government zoning codes
Properties must be located in Maryland
Sponsors must have contract acceptable to CDA with State agency or county government providing operating income and/or grant funds
Sponsors without prior group home experience may be approved if they demonstrate capacity based on other business endeavors and prior satisfactory financial and credit management

Credit reports must demonstrate history of meeting long- and short-term credit obligations; financial risk score/credit score must be 3 or lower, no past due accounts, open liens, judgments, foreclosures, bankruptcy filings, or unsatisfied tax liens
Nonprofit sponsors must provide audited financial statements for prior three years plus current quarter balance sheet if most recent audited statement is older than six months
Individual sponsors must submit federal income tax statements for most recent three years and personal financial statements
D&B or consumer credit reports obtained for organizations and individuals respectively (valid for four months from document date to note date)
Maryland Department of Environment Lead Rental Property Registration required for all residential rental properties built prior to 1978 currently owned by sponsor
Application fee of $800 total: $400 for department costs (paid at settlement, nonrefundable, includes credit report and processing fee), and $400 legal fee (due at settlement)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The program is not currently accepting applications. Applications will reopen at a later date. Interested applicants should check the webpage for updates on program and application information. When applications reopen: Sponsors should arrange an initial meeting with the GHFP Manager to discuss the proposed project and review general program requirements. Sponsors not previously approved by CDA as eligible must submit complete application with all supporting documentation. Previously approved sponsors need only updates of financial statements, articles of incorporation, and bylaws (if applicable). Completed applications are submitted to: Department of Housing and Community Development, 7800 Harkins Road, 369B, Lanham, Maryland 20706, ATTN: Group Home Financing Program. Upon receipt, application is date stamped and assigned a case number. Acknowledgement letter is sent identifying required missing documentation with 30-day period to submit. Credit reports are obtained (fee $100 or actual cost if higher, netted from loan proceeds). Historical significance determined if property over 50 years old and substantial rehabilitation planned. For properties built before 1978, lead paint risk assessment evidence required. Initial eligibility review completed within 90-120 days of receiving complete application. Upon completion of eligibility review and determination of funding source, sponsor is notified in writing of determination, estimated loan amount, and general guidance on expected loan terms. If loan is not eligible, rejection letter specifies reasons and includes reconsideration procedures. Federal Funds Notice must be executed by seller prior to entering binding sales contract for all loan requests.

structured_extraction.program_name: HAF WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program that helps Maryland homeowners facing financial hardship due to the COVID-19 pandemic by funding critical repairs in primary residences that could lead to displacement if not addressed. The program is administered under section 3206 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grant funding up to $10,000 per project for critical home repairs. No minimum amount specified. The financial assistance is provided as a grant with no lien recorded on the property. This is one-time assistance per household. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Applicants may select payment preferences: 33% deposit with 67% at completion, or 0% deposit with 100% at completion.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved, whichever comes first
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners who experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020, occupy the property as their principal residence, and whose household income is at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI). Renters and tenants are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical repairs in primary residences including mold or mildew remediation, asbestos removal, non-functioning heating and cooling systems (no heat/no air), electrical repairs, plumbing and septic repairs, wells, roof repair or replacement, lead paint hazard reduction or elimination, structural and maintenance issues, and trip/slip issues. Funds cannot be used for home remodeling or non-health and safety repairs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Applicant must reside in and own the primary residence in Maryland. County-specific income limits apply based on 150% of Area Median Income (AMI) for household size.
requirements_list: Experienced financial hardship after January 21, 2020 (includes hardships that began before January 21, 2020 but continued after that date)
Household income at or below 150% of County Area Median Income (AMI) based on household size
Must be a Maryland homeowner
Must occupy the property as primary residence
Must be named on the property deed
If other individuals are named on the deed but do not occupy the property, must provide proof they live elsewhere (driver's license, utility bill, notarized statement, or other evidence)
Provide at least one detailed estimate within the past 60 days from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor
Contractor estimate must include photographs documenting the critical repairs
Contractor must be currently licensed as a Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or hold appropriate trade license (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, etc.)
Contractor must be in good standing with the State of Maryland
Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000
Contractor must provide completed W-9 form
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing from the State of Maryland
No credit score minimum required
One-time financial assistance per household
Payments or deposits made by homeowners for work or materials at any point will NOT be reimbursed
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the WholeHome Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) grant application and submit it along with: (1) income verification documents (recent paystubs, tax returns for self-employed, award letters for Social Security/disability/pension, unemployment documentation, or notarized zero income statement); (2) proof of home ownership; (3) photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant; (4) documentation of COVID-19 financial hardship after January 21, 2020; and (5) at least one detailed estimate within the past 60 days from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor. The contractor must also complete the Bid Cover Page and provide a copy of their current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and completed W-9. Applications may be submitted by email to rehab.hafapplications@maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA Special Loan Programs - Rehab Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF), 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. Once approved, applicants must sign a commitment letter, grant agreement, rehabilitation contract, W-9 form, and final invoice from contractor accepting the work as completed satisfactorily. The program operates on a first-come, first-served basis. Applications open January 22, 2026 and close September 30, 2026, or until funding is fully reserved.

structured_extraction.program_name: Healthy Homes for Healthy Kids Lead Initiative
structured_extraction.program_description: A partnership initiative between Maryland state agencies that helps families reduce lead exposure in homes built before 1978 by covering lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Funding to cover lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed in homes where children with elevated blood lead levels live or spend significant time. The program pays for lead elimination at no cost to the homeowner or renter.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Families with children under 19 years old who have elevated blood lead levels and live in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead removal and minor home repairs necessary to ensure lead paint remains properly sealed
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Child must be under 19 years old
Child must live in Maryland
Child must have a recent blood lead test of 5 micrograms per deciliter (µg/dL) or higher
Child must be enrolled in or eligible for Medicaid or Maryland Children's Health Insurance Program (MCHP)
Child must spend 10 hours or more per week in the location (home, apartment, or day care) where the lead exposure occurred
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Environmental Health Help Line at 1-866-703-3266 or the local health department for more information about eligibility and program details. The program will pay for lead elimination at no cost to the homeowner or renter. The program was created in 2016 through a partnership of three state agencies: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and Maryland Department of Health.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to public housing owners to install broadband-capable wiring to individual dwelling units to address digital equity and inclusion in low-income housing. Round 1 offers funding for new projects while the expanded round (FY24) includes additional opportunities for municipal and non-profit owners of low-income multi-dwelling units.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Round 1: Grants between $500,000 and $9,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with 5% match required. Expanded Round (FY24) for municipally owned and non-profit MDUs: Grants between $250,000 and $5,000,000 covering 95% of eligible project costs with 5% match required. Total funding of $26.9 million available for expanded round. Match funds can come from local, state, or federal sources and are in addition to the grant award. Eligible uses include installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual units, fiber optic extension to buildings, wireless access points in common areas providing free WiFi, building modifications for equipment installation, and community engagement costs (capped at 3% of total project cost, not to exceed $15,000). Administrative costs capped at 1% of total project costs.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Round 1: December 22, 2023. Expanded Round: January 31, 2025
structured_extraction.program_audience: Publicly owned housing authorities, municipal governments, non-profit organizations, and Internet Service Providers operating low-income multi-dwelling units
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Installation of broadband-capable wiring to individual public housing dwelling units, fiber optic facility extension, wireless access points in common areas, building modifications necessary for broadband distribution, community engagement and education for broadband adoption including ACP registration assistance, and related network equipment and electronics necessary for service delivery
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; all Maryland counties eligible. Publicly owned housing developments must be identified as having a need for additional broadband investment, including lack of access to connections reliably meeting or exceeding minimum speeds of 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload.
requirements_list: Eligible applicants include local jurisdictions (county or municipal), housing authorities, municipally owned entities, and non-profit organizations owning public housing or low-income multi-dwelling units
Must demonstrate ownership or operational control of publicly supported housing development
For expanded round, ISPs must be existing Internet Service Providers actively offering high-speed internet services over their own physical network infrastructure
95% of eligible project costs covered; 5% match required (match must be identified in application)
Project must provide minimum 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum 50 milliseconds latency measured at each dwelling unit (or scalable to 100/100 with documented exceptions)
Applicant must agree to maintain and secure project equipment and technology for at least 5 years after project completion
Installation of wireless access points in public and common areas providing free WiFi service to residents
Community engagement strategies must be in place during project development
For expanded round, must offer affordable internet plans for low-income residents
For expanded round, must offer low-cost service options for different speed tiers to all subscribers
Project must align with American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund requirements
All equipment purchased must be new and non-depreciated
For expanded round, ISPs must provide letter of support from municipal or non-profit property owner
For expanded round, property owner must provide documentation of municipal or non-profit status (IRS 501(c)(3) or similar for non-profits)
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit completed applications via email to osb.md@maryland.gov with required documentation including: completed and signed application form, project summary (executive summary, statement of experience, network design description), community profile with demographic data, subscriber cost information, list of community and local government partners, implementation schedule with major milestones and timeline for construction through project completion, detailed line-item capital construction budget on provided forms, sustainability plan, and all required attachments. Round 1 applications were due December 22, 2023, with awards announced February 2024. Expanded round applications accepted October 31, 2024 through January 31, 2025, with awards to be announced by February 28, 2025. Applications must include IRS W-9 form, evidence of organizational status, and letters of support. For expanded round, applicants must provide 3 years of historical financial data and 3-5 years of projected financial data including balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow statements.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Homelessness Solutions Program helps communities across Maryland prevent and end homelessness by providing technical support and funding to Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions that coordinate homelessness services and connect people to housing programs, shelters, and other services. HSP provides over $15 million in annual funding to deliver and organize homeless services in local communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HSP provides grants to lead agencies representing Continuums of Care and Local Homeless Coalitions. The total available funding for SFY2026 is $15.2 million ($14 million state HSP funds and $1.2 million federal Emergency Solutions Grant). Applicants must submit two budget scenarios: one based on level funding to their FY24 award, and one based on a 30% increase above the FY24 award. Funding can be used for street outreach, emergency shelter, rapid rehousing, homeless prevention, permanent supportive housing case management, homeless management information systems (HMIS), administrative costs (up to 10% cap), special events, and system transformation projects. Lead agencies must provide matching funds of at least 25% of requested funding. The grant period is 18 months: July 1, 2025 through December 31, 2026. A minimum of $1 million will be allocated specifically for projects dedicated to serving unaccompanied youth.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 25, 2025 - 5pm
structured_extraction.program_audience: Lead agencies for Maryland Continuums of Care (HUD-approved Collaborative Applicants) and DHCD-approved lead agencies for Balance of State Local Homeless Coalitions that coordinate homelessness services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street outreach, emergency shelter, host homes, rapid rehousing, permanent supportive housing, homeless prevention/diversion, direct cash transfers for highly vulnerable populations (unaccompanied youth, returning citizens, pregnant/parenting families with children under 5), flex funds for landlord incentives and removal of tenant housing barriers, HMIS data entry and system administration, special events (Homeless Resource Days, Point-in-Time Count activities), administrative costs including CoC/LHC and Coordinated Entry staffing, training and technical assistance, and systems transformation projects such as conversion of emergency/transitional shelters into permanent supportive housing or integration of workforce development into rapid rehousing programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All of Maryland with 16 Continuums of Care regions and Balance of State Local Homeless Coalition areas. Specific CoCs include: Allegany County, Anne Arundel, Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Carroll County, Cecil County, Frederick County, Garrett County, Harford County, Howard County, Lower Shore, Mid-Shore, Montgomery County, Prince George's County, Southern Maryland, and Washington County.
requirements_list: Must be a HUD-approved Collaborative Applicant/lead agency of a Maryland Continuum of Care OR a DHCD-approved lead agency for a Balance of State CoC Local Homeless Coalition
Must apply on behalf of homeless services providers in their community
Lead agencies may subgrant all or part of their HSP grant to government agencies or nonprofit organizations
Lead agencies must certify that subgrantees meet HSP requirements
Lead agencies must perform at least one risk assessment of all grantees over the term of the grant period
Lead agencies must conduct monitoring and compliance visits to all grantees deemed high-risk
Lead agencies must conduct monitoring and compliance visits to medium- and low-risk subgrantees based on risk assessment criteria

All grantees/subgrantees must enroll in HMIS (or comparable database for victim services providers) and be in full compliance with HMIS implementation guidelines at time of application (new subgrantees at time grant agreement is signed)
All grantees must be participating in the Maryland State Homelessness Data Warehouse (MSHDW)
Must provide matching funds of at least 25% of requested funding from local or private sources, or federal CSBG or state Emergency Assistance Program funds
Subgrantees must demonstrate collaboration with local homeless provider groups and local mainstream service providers
Subgrantees must participate in Continuum of Care planning appropriate to jurisdiction where HSP activities are located

Project selection for subgrantees should be based on objective process considering: effectiveness in connecting clients to shelter and permanent housing, past performance on federal/state grants, organizational structure and capacity, participation in provider groups and CoC meetings, and organizational financial policy and controls
All HSP-funded programs must implement Housing First approach
All programs must comply with Fair Housing Act, Americans with Disabilities Act, Equal Access to Housing Final Rule, and gender identity requirements
Programs cannot require participation in religious or faith-based activities
Programs cannot involuntarily separate families
Independent parties or non-affiliated organizations will not be accepted
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the DHCD Project Portal. Key dates: (1) Organization Profile Review materials due March 21, 2025 - submit W-9, agency organizational chart, most recent single audit/independent financial audit, articles of incorporation, bylaws, federal tax exemption letter (nonprofits), certificate of good standing, charity registration status, and board list; (2) Attend optional training session March 3, 2025 10-11am via Google Meet; (3) Complete HSP SFY2026 application and submit all supporting documents by April 25, 2025 at 5pm via Project Portal, including: CoC/LHC application narrative (Word), detailed budget template (Excel) with both level and 30% increase scenarios, project performance tool (Excel), Stella P report, 2024 System Performance Measures report, HUD Annual Performance Reports from HMIS for renewal projects, and 2024 Housing Inventory Count and Point in Time Count data. Applications are evaluated through three reviews: threshold review (organization profile), CoC/LHC performance evaluation (application narrative scoring up to 160 points), and project-level performance evaluation. Award notifications issued June 2, 2025. Grant period begins July 1, 2025.

structured_extraction.program_name: Homeowner Assistance Fund (HAF) WholeHome Critical Home Repairs Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: A limited grant program that provides funds to eligible Maryland homeowners to pay for critical home repairs that could prevent displacement from their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to help eligible Maryland homeowners pay for critical home repairs that could prevent displacement.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland homeowners at risk of displacement
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Critical home repairs to prevent displacement
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program provides affordable funding to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with applicable building codes through a suite of special loan programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Affordable loans to address critical health and safety issues and bring homes into compliance with building codes. Programs include upgrades like accessibility features, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, and structural repairs.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Homeowners needing critical repairs and rehabilitation.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Health and safety repairs, structural maintenance, accessibility features for seniors or those with special needs, lead paint removal, plumbing upgrades, and code compliance improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland
requirements_list: Homeowner
Property must need critical health and safety repairs or code compliance work
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact DHCD for specific program details and application procedures.

structured_extraction.program_description: The federal Housing Choice Voucher Program provides rental subsidies in the form of vouchers to eligible families or individuals to use toward housing payments. The program is administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development through regional offices and subcontractors throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Rental subsidies provided through Housing Choice Vouchers that allow eligible families or individuals to use toward housing payments. The voucher provides the difference between 30% of the family's adjusted income and the payment standard (or actual rent if lower). Each jurisdiction's public housing agency creates eligibility criteria, processes applications, develops and maintains waitlists, and verifies requirements. Families receive a voucher briefing that includes mobility counseling on expanded housing choices outside areas of minority and poverty concentration. The program administers specialized vouchers including Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (VASH), Family Unification Program (FUP), Non-Elderly Disabled (NED2) vouchers, and Mainstream vouchers. Payment standards are established based on fair market rents adjusted for local conditions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 30, 2026, at 5:00 PM (for Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton waitlist opening)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible families or individuals seeking rental housing assistance. Priority populations include extremely low-income families (at or below 30% of Area Median Income), elderly families, families with disabilities, veterans, families involved in child welfare, and non-elderly disabled individuals.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Rental housing payments. Vouchers subsidize the rent portion of housing costs, with families typically paying 30% of their adjusted gross income toward rent.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide through local public housing agencies. Program is administered by DHCD through the following offices: Allegany County and City of Cumberland (Human Resources Development Commission); Frederick County (Frederick County Department of Housing and Community Development); Garrett County (Garrett County Community Action Committee, Inc.); and Eastern Shore Regional Office serving Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Somerset, Talbot, Worcester, and Wicomico Counties. Waitlist is reopening for Eastern Shore counties (Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Talbot, Somerset, Wicomico, Worcester Counties) and the Town of Elkton starting April 1, 2026. The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development directly administers the program for Caroline County, Dorchester County, Kent County, Somerset County, Talbot County, Wicomico County, Worcester County, and the City of Elkton. Other jurisdictions maintain their own local programs.
requirements_list: Meet eligibility criteria set by local public housing agency including income limitations
U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status
Valid Social Security Numbers for all family members
Pass tenant screening including criminal history and rental history review
Selected through lottery process for waitlist placement
Families must attend mandatory voucher briefing before issuance
Families with disabilities have reasonable accommodations available upon request
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a preliminary application through the Waitlist Status Portal or check status online. Applicants provide required documentation including proof of income, residency, identity, and Social Security numbers. For Eastern Shore and Town of Elkton locations, the application period runs from April 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM to April 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM. A lottery selection process is used for waitlist placement. Selected applicants are notified and scheduled for a full application completion appointment. Verification of all stated information is conducted including income, citizenship status, and screening criteria. Eligible applicants receive notification and proceed to voucher briefing. Families receive housing search assistance and voucher mobility counseling to encourage participation in areas outside low-income or minority concentration. In-person assistance is available at specific locations for individuals with disabilities or those needing extra support. The PHA assists families in locating suitable housing and conducts initial housing quality standards inspection before contract execution.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Housing Innovation Pilot Program provides low- or no-interest loans to local housing authorities or county governments partnering with housing developers to increase housing production and support innovative housing solutions. The program may also fund projects where counties purchase existing privately owned housing in conjunction with local housing authorities or developers.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Low- or no-interest loans provided through the Housing Innovation Fund to support new construction, acquisition, or rehabilitation of rental housing. Eligible housing includes apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. All projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized rental housing with at least 20% of units set aside for households earning 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households earning 60% or less of area median income. Loan terms include: Short-term loans (3-5 years) at approximately 3% interest rate, or Longer-term loans (7-10 years) at approximately 5.5% interest rate. HIPP loans will be subordinate loans, with positioning considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum award per project is $2.5 million. $5 million in FY 2026 funding is available, with up to 3 projects selected (maximum one award per jurisdiction). Application fee is $2,500.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Public housing authorities and county governments partnering with housing developers
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction and acquisition or rehabilitation of rental housing including apartment buildings, townhouses, single-family homes, single room occupancy buildings, and shared housing facilities. Purchase of existing privately owned housing to increase housing production.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide—all Maryland counties. Projects must be located in Maryland.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a public housing authority or county government partnering with a housing developer, or a county in conjunction with a PHA or developer acquiring existing housing
Sponsor must have an ownership interest in the project's ownership entity, as demonstrated by an organizational chart and/or partnership agreement
Projects must provide mixed-income, cross-subsidized housing

At least 20% of units must be set aside for households with gross annual income of 50% or less of area median income, or at least 40% of units for households with gross annual income of 60% or less of area median income
Proposed projects must be ready for occupancy within two (2) years of the award selection date
Projects must meet all threshold criteria established in the Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide
Affirmative Fair Housing Marketing Plan (AFHMP) required using form HUD-935.2A
Tenant selection policy must be submitted prior to closing and must meet Department requirements
Compliance with federal and state fair housing and equal opportunity laws required
No tenant displacement without cause in the 12 months prior to application submission except for renovation in compliance with approved relocation plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Virtual information session held March 11, 2026 at 12 p.m. for questions about the program. 2. Submit application fee of $2,500 (check payable to 'Community Development Administration') separately to: Community Development Administration, Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Post Office Box 2524, Landover Hills, MD 20784. 3. Complete full Application Submission Package including: Housing Innovation Pilot Program Application Form, CDA Form 202 Multifamily Rental Financing Application (dated February 2025), Certifications, Threshold Checklist, Applicant Self-Scoring form, Organizational Chart, and all required exhibits. 4. Application forms must not be retyped or modified. All information must be completed or marked not applicable. 5. Submit one complete electronic application via Procorem WorkCenter by May 18, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. Each section, attachment, and exhibit must be clearly tabbed. Include copy of fee check with application submission. 6. DHCD staff reviews for completeness; incomplete submissions will not be processed. 7. Complete proposals are submitted to scoring committee (may include state and local government agencies). 8. Proposals ranked by score; highest-scored selected and recommended to CDA Director for approval, then Secretary for final approval and allocation. 9. If two competing applications from same jurisdiction, they are ranked within jurisdiction by elements and points, with number of units as tiebreaker. 10. Waiver requests available and must be submitted at least 15 days prior to application deadline (by May 4, 2026) using Waiver Request Form on DHCD website.

structured_extraction.program_description: A tax credit program that provides financial assistance to eligible Maryland residents who make their homes more accessible by adding accessibility features. Eligible applicants can receive up to 50% of renovation costs back, up to a maximum of $5,000 per year.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Applicants can receive a tax credit equal to up to 50% of their home renovation costs, with a maximum credit of $5,000 per year. The credit applies to renovations completed in the previous tax year that add accessibility features to the applicant's own home, a family member's home, or a rental property. DHCD can approve up to $1,000,000 in tax credits per year; if demand exceeds this amount, individual credits may be reduced proportionally. If approved, applicants receive a tax credit certificate by August 31st of the current calendar year and must file an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certificate attached to claim the credit.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: June 1st of the current calendar year
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland residents who have completed home renovations that add accessibility features for themselves, family members, or rental properties.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The tax credit can be used to offset Maryland tax liability for home renovation costs that include accessibility features such as no-step entrances, grab bars, handrails, chairlifts, elevators, roll-in showers, accessible parking spaces, rocker panel light switches, accessible door hardware, visual/auditory alarms for individuals with sensory disabilities, lever water controls, accessible kitchen appliances and workspaces, bathroom mirrors within reach ranges, slip-resistant floors, accessible storage, and other modifications that improve home accessibility.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Program is available statewide to all Maryland residents.
requirements_list: Be a Maryland resident
File taxes in Maryland for the same calendar year you made the renovations
Have proof of payment for home renovations that include accessibility features
Submit a completed application to DHCD with supporting documentation
Completed renovations must have occurred during the previous tax year
Provide receipts, invoices, and before-and-after photos as proof of expenses
Applicants must not have received funds or tax credits from other sources for the same renovation project
Only one application for services may be submitted per household
Applicants must keep documentation and provide it upon request to verify funds were used for intended purposes
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, complete your home renovation and file your taxes for the year the renovation was completed. Then, submit your completed application and supporting documentation (detailed invoices, proof of payment, pre-renovation pictures, post-renovation pictures, and other supporting documentation/permits) by June 1st of the current calendar year. Submit your application by email to DHCD.SLP_Documentation@Maryland.gov or by mail to: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs- Independent Living Tax Credit Application, Attention: SLP Intake Team, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. DHCD will review your application and notify you by August 31st of the current calendar year. If approved, file an amended tax return (Form 502X) with the DHCD tax credit certificate attached to claim the credit. A representative from DHCD may contact you to gather additional information during the review process.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides loans to help homeowners and rental property owners install or repair indoor plumbing systems in residential properties that are structurally sound.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on the applicant's ability to pay and household income. Interest rates are 4.5% to 6.0% for households at 80% of median income, 0% to 4.5% for households at 60% of median income, and 0% for households at or below 50% of median income. Maximum loan amount is $50,000. Maximum loan term is 30 years. Deferred loans are available to borrowers at or below 50% of median income if necessary for project feasibility. Deferred amounts or portions of deferred amounts may be forgiven annually for families with incomes at or below 30% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes and owners of rental residential properties with household incomes at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Wells, septic tanks and drain fields, piping from septic system into the residential building, connection expenses to public water or sewer systems including fees and assessments, plumbing fixtures and equipment including handicapped fixtures, additions and modifications required to provide private space for toilet and bath facilities, sand mound systems, purification systems, cost of percolation tests, and alternative and innovative septic and water systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties. Loans are generally processed directly by local governments for properties within their jurisdiction. For Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area income limit purposes, the following counties are included: Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's. All other Maryland counties use the Rest of State income limits.
requirements_list: Owner-occupants of single-family homes must have an income at or below 80% of the statewide or Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income (based on household size and location)
Owners of rental residential properties must ensure units will be occupied by income-eligible households
Properties must be structurally sound
Single-family homes must be owner-occupied and have inoperative or unsafe plumbing
Applicants must provide photo ID (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Proof of home ownership through deed and current mortgage statement required

Lowest qualifying bid from licensed Maryland tradesperson identifying repairs, not more than 60 days old

structured_extraction.program_name: Lead Hazard Reduction Loan and Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A state and federally-funded program that helps make Maryland homes safer by removing or reducing lead hazards in owner-occupied single family homes and rental properties. The program provides grants and loans to eligible applicants, including owner-occupants, for-profit sponsors, nonprofit sponsors, and licensed childcare facilities, using funds from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development's Office of Lead Hazard Control and Healthy Homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Financial assistance provided as either a grant or loan based on the applicant's ability to repay and location. Grants up to $25,000 per eligible property are available in target areas or for innovative lead hazard reduction treatments and require a match (20% for for-profit sponsors, 10% for nonprofit sponsors, 10% for owner-occupants with income above 80% of median; no match required for owner-occupants with income below 80% of median). Amortizing loans have interest rates from 0%-7% with 20-year terms; deferred loans have 0% interest with 20-year terms and are available only if underwriting shows no affordability to repay or for properties without sufficient equity. Maximum unit assistance is $25,000; maximum annual sponsor assistance is $100,000. Loan terms vary based on income level: 0%-4.5% interest for households at 60% of median income, 4.5%-6.0% for 80% of median income. Funds must be used for lead hazard reduction activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning to meet risk reduction standards and lead dust clearance standards. Licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors must perform services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 1, 2029
structured_extraction.program_audience: Maryland homeowners, landlords, for-profit sponsors, nonprofit sponsors, licensed residential childcare facilities, and licensed day care centers with incomes up to 80% of Area Median Income (AMI), with more favorable terms available for those at 60% or below of AMI. Special considerations apply if children under age 6 or pregnant women reside in or regularly visit the property.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Lead hazard reduction and lead-based paint abatement activities including door and window treatments and replacement, floor treatments, paint removal, stabilization and repainting, encapsulation, enclosure, and specialized cleaning to meet risk reduction standards and lead dust clearance standards. Services must be performed by licensed and accredited lead abatement contractors and include lead clearance testing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide. Grants require location in target areas or use of innovative lead hazard reduction treatments. For amortizing and deferred loans, income limits vary by household size and region: Washington DC PMSA (Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, Prince George's counties) and Rest of State.

For amortizing loans: 0%-7% interest rates based on income level and ability to repay over 20 years
For deferred loans: only available if underwriting shows no affordability to repay

For sponsors (nonprofits and for-profits): Complete the Sponsor Application Form and provide organizational documents, financial statements, and project details. 4.
