Incomplete applications will not be processed. 7. Underwriting will evaluate affordability to repay and property value. 8. Lead clearance testing will be required upon completion of work.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development issues tax-exempt bonds on behalf of counties, municipalities, and their agencies to finance community infrastructure projects. The program provides long-term capital financing with advantageous terms, reduces issuance costs through economies of scale, and helps local governments navigate the complexities of tax-exempt bond financing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Community Development Administration issues tax-exempt bonds and loans the bond proceeds to local governments. The interest rate on the loans is based on market conditions and the rate attained on the pooled bond issue. Local governments repay the debt and pay their pro-rata share of the pooled bond issuance costs. Each participant pledges its full faith and credit to secure payment. The loan term is set by the local government but cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less. The program is available for projects ranging from $150,000 to $10 million or more.
structured_extraction.program_audience: All Maryland counties, municipalities, and their agencies with legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain projects, pledge security for and repay loans, and pledge income tax payments and shared revenue from the State.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Street lighting, landscaping, sidewalks and public space improvements; public safety vehicles and equipment; water production, treatment, storage and distribution systems; storm water control and sewer collection and treatment facilities; government office and meeting facilities; police, fire, transportation, education, health, recreation, maintenance and other service related facilities; and refinancing of existing debt for eligible projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties and municipalities are eligible.
requirements_list: Must be a Maryland county, municipality, or their agency
Must have legal authority to construct, operate, and maintain the proposed project
Must have legal authority to pledge security for and repay the proposed loan
Must have legal authority to pledge income tax payments and various other shared revenue from the State
Project must support an essential physical element of a municipality's public service system
Project must meet federal tax law requirements
Project must be undertaken by or on behalf of a local government, including its agencies
Loan term cannot exceed the useful life of the project or thirty years, whichever is less
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The local government completes an application that provides information similar to what a bond rating agency would require to evaluate credit worthiness. When bonds are issued is influenced by the volume and frequency of participation by local governments. Technical assistance is available to help local governments complete the application. Those requesting technical assistance may submit an Expression of Interest form outlining the proposed project or specific questions.

structured_extraction.program_name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A federal tax credit program that encourages private sector investment in constructing and rehabilitating rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. States receive an annual tax credit allocation based on population, and tax credits are awarded competitively to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors of eligible housing projects based on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Sponsors of eligible low-income rental housing projects receive a federal tax credit equal to the applicable percentage of the qualified basis of each qualified low-income rental housing building. The applicable percentage is determined by the Internal Revenue Service and ranges from 4% to 9% of qualified costs. Project sponsors or their investor partners claim the tax credit on their federal income tax return over a 10-year credit period. The tax credit is based on the qualified basis of the building and the applicable percentage, with credits claimed annually. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. During the initial 15-year compliance period, owners must maintain affordability restrictions, and the credit is subject to tax consequences if compliance is violated. After year 15, an extended use period of at least 15 additional years applies with less stringent monitoring but continued affordability requirements. Tax-exempt bond-financed projects may be eligible for tax credits outside of the competitive process.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - competitive allocation basis announced annually; typically published in QAP and Notice of Funding Availability
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit and nonprofit sponsors developing or rehabilitating rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Investors seeking tax credits to offset federal income tax liability.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Construction and rehabilitation of rental housing for low- and moderate-income families. Funds from tax credits are used to provide equity capital for the development of affordable rental properties. Funds must be used to create or preserve affordable rental housing for households with incomes at or below specified percentages of area median income (either 50% or 60% depending on set-aside election).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide throughout Maryland. Projects must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made. All Maryland counties are eligible for consideration. Priority consideration and incentives may be given to projects located in Qualified Census Tracts (QCTs) or Difficult Development Areas (DDAs) as designated by the IRS. Ten percent of the state's annual allocation is set aside solely for nonprofit sponsors. Properties must be located in Maryland and comply with state and local zoning and building requirements.
requirements_list: A residential rental building must be placed in service in or within two years after the year in which the allocation is made
Building must provide at least in part for low-income occupancy

Owner must rent either 20 percent of units to households with incomes at or below 50 percent of area median income or 40 percent of units to households with incomes at or below 60 percent of area median income, or use income averaging (15%, 30%, 40%, 70%, or 80% of units at corresponding income levels)
Building must remain in compliance for a minimum of 40 years with enforced covenant (15-year initial compliance period plus 15-year extended use period minimum)
Projects must be residential rental buildings
Tax credits awarded on competitive basis based on criteria in State's Qualified Allocation Plan
Owner must maintain detailed records of tenant incomes, rents, and compliance for the duration of the compliance period
Owner must submit annual certifications of compliance via Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance (OCPC)
No discrimination in tenant selection; must accept Housing Choice Vouchers
Building must meet local health, safety, and building code standards
Owner must obtain annual tenant income certifications and maintain documentation supporting certifications
Owner must maintain rent-restricted units for non-transient use by general public
Owner must provide utility allowances that are updated at least annually
Owner must maintain project files on-site containing covenant, management plan, tenant selection plan, management agreement, Forms 8609 for each building, and resident files for each unit
Owner must establish and implement affirmative fair housing marketing plan
Owner must not discriminate in tenant selection or evict tenants except for good cause
Owner must maintain property in decent, safe, and sanitary condition suitable for occupancy
Physical inspections and file reviews will be conducted by CDA; during initial 15-year compliance period more frequently; during extended use period (after year 15) at least once every five years
Owner must correct any identified noncompliance within specified cure periods (typically 30-90 days, with possibility of extension to six months for extenuating circumstances)
Owner must report changes in ownership composition, management, or other material project changes to CDA for approval
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Tax credits are awarded on a competitive basis to nonprofit and for-profit sponsors annually following the State's Qualified Allocation Plan (QAP). The process includes: (1) Applicants submit proposals during the competitive allocation round(s) as announced in the annual Notice of Funding Availability and Qualified Allocation Plan; (2) Proposals are evaluated on criteria outlined in the State's Qualified Allocation Plan, including development team qualifications, project feasibility, financial capacity, property condition, and compliance with program priorities; (3) CDA reviews applications and issues preliminary and final allocations to selected projects; (4) Applicants must submit application materials according to the published QAP requirements, including development team information, project details, financial projections, and compliance certifications; (5) Projects may compete for allocations in the general pool or for set-asides designated for specific project types or geographic areas; (6) Developer obtains construction financing and begins project development; (7) Upon project completion and placement in service, owner's CPA certifies total costs for each building and that all program requirements have been met; (8) CDA completes Part I of IRS Form 8609 and issues to owner; (9) Owner completes and signs Part II of Form 8609 and submits to IRS with tax return, providing copy to CDA; (10) Extended Low-Income Housing Covenant must be recorded before end of calendar year in which credits are first claimed; (11) Owner submits annual Owner's Certificate of Continuing Program Compliance (OCPC) by deadline published in annual Notice (typically by end of February for prior year); (12) CDA conducts on-site monitoring inspections and file reviews based on IRS-required sampling; (13) For projects seeking to exit the program after year 15 of compliance period, owners may request Qualified Contract process to market project to qualified purchaser at established price; (14) Tax-exempt bond-financed projects may follow alternative processes for credit allocation outside competitive rounds. Refer to the State's Qualified Allocation Plan and Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide for specific application procedures and deadlines.

structured_extraction.program_description: A grant program designed to assist local jurisdictions, community-based organizations, non-profits, and anchor institutions in creating gap networks and community networks that provide affordable internet access to low and moderate income households and other covered populations.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants of up to 100 percent of project costs for constructing, deploying, expanding, or maintaining community-based gap networks. The maximum grant award is $250,000 and the minimum is $25,000. Funding supports equipment, networking hardware and software, and digital network technology to provide broadband services at low or no cost to covered populations, with a minimum requirement of 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Thursday, March 31, 2022
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments, foundations, corporations, institutions, associations, coalitions that are non-profit 501(c) entities, community-based anchor institutions, and community-based organizations serving Maryland. The programs target covered populations including individuals with household income at or below 150 percent of federal poverty level, aging individuals, individuals with disabilities, individuals with language barriers, and individuals who are members of racial or ethnic minority groups.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Building and deploying new gap networks or community networks; upgrading or expanding existing gap networks or community networks; operating and maintaining gap networks or community networks; purchasing electronics to deliver service including optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennas, access points, modems, and equipment shelters.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be providing services within the State of Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a local government (counties or municipalities), a non-profit 501(c) entity foundation, corporation, institution, association or coalition providing services in Maryland, a community-based anchor institution, or other community-based organization
Be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation
Submit a complete application with all required attachments
Applications must be fully complete at submission to be considered for funding
Projects must reliably provide minimum internet connectivity of 100 Mbps down and 100 Mbps up with identified exceptions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit a complete application and all supporting documents via email to OSB.MD@Maryland.gov. The application must include a project summary explaining how the project closes the digital divide, a network design, community profile, subscriber cost information, identification of potential barriers, partners and local engagement details, intended outcomes and metrics, schedule, and funding scope and budget. All required attachments including the completed application form, IRS determination letter (if nonprofit), Certificate of Good Standing verification, IRS W-9 form, and Dun and Bradstreet DUNS number must be included.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to K-12 schools, libraries, and anchor institutions to close the digital divide for students and school staff by providing internet access or devices needed to connect to classrooms. The program helps communities improve broadband access, adoption and utilization.

The program provided awards ranging from approximately $34,000 to $250,000 for specific projects including digital access initiatives, broadband access projects, and community technology centers.

Funding for qualifying expenses and projects completed between September 1, 2021 and September 15, 2022
Projects must address digital divide and broadband access gaps

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development provides funding to assist Maryland's designated and affiliate Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods in building capacity to achieve their community revitalization and economic development goals in designated Sustainable Community areas throughout the state.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Main Street Improvement Program (MIP) Grant awards provide allocated funds to eligible grantees as follows: Designated Main Street Maryland Communities with full accreditation on their annual assessment receive approximately $33,000 each. Designated Main Street Maryland Communities accredited as affiliate receive approximately $25,000 each. Main Street Maryland Aspiring Communities receive approximately $12,000 each. Final amounts are contingent upon General Assembly approval during the FY2027 legislative session. Grants support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. Capital project costs are not supported through MIP. Funding match is not required. All projects and activities should be completed within one year. Funds may be requested for staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, and other projects identified in the applicant's work plans as key to its Main Street efforts.

structured_extraction.program_audience: Designated and Aspiring Main Street Maryland communities and Baltimore City's designated Main Street neighborhoods
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants support operating expenses only, including salary, professional services contracts, technology costs, market and business recruitment strategies, marketing and advertising, placemaking initiatives, and other costs related to administering the Main Street program. All projects and activities should be completed within one year. Requested funds should support projects and activities that align with the applicant's annual work plan and contribute to the community's transformation strategy. Capital project costs are not supported.

Grants can be used for operating expenses only; capital project costs are not supported

Projects and activities must contribute to community transformation strategy
All projects and activities should be completed within one year

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are submitted through the DHCD Project Portal at https://projectportal.dhcd.state.md.us/. To access the portal, register as a new user and complete the registration request form, which may take up to 72 hours for approval. Ensure your organization profile includes all required documents before submitting your application. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. New organizations should submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. Applications missing required documents may be disqualified. All applications must be submitted online; late applications will not be accepted. Training documents, including a program overview and step-by-step application guide, are available in the DHCD Project Portal. A virtual application training session is scheduled for Tuesday, March 3, 2026 from 1-2 PM EDT. Individual technical assistance sessions are available by scheduling online via Calendly. Upon award, awardees must execute an Award Agreement through DocuSign within five business days of receipt. The authorized signatory for your organization must sign the agreement. Funds cannot be drawn down until after execution and all Special Conditions have been met. Following award execution, awardees should draw down at least 50% of awarded funds within six months of the award execution date. All awarded funds must be drawn down by the award agreement's expiration date. Progress reports are due at 6 months from the grant agreement execution date or whenever a payment request is submitted. A final report is due no later than 30 days after the award agreement's expiration date and must include certification of completion, visual documentation (before and after pictures preferred), financial reconciliation, compliance verification, and results documentation. All progress reports must be submitted electronically through the DHCD Project Portal.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that provides funding to support affordable housing development. The program supplies funding to state and certain local governments to build, buy, or fix rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. HOME funds may be provided as zero-interest deferred loans, regular amortized loans, grants, or recoverable grants depending on project needs and state discretion. A Board of Trustees governs the program, which the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development manages.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HOME funds are provided with flexible terms. Assistance may be structured as zero-interest deferred loans with terms ranging from 20 to 40 years, regular amortized loans, recoverable grants requiring repayment when the property is sold or ceases to be used for low-income housing, or outright grants. Equity sharing arrangements may apply to rental projects when low-income usage is discontinued, with the State sharing in proportion to HOME funds involved. The maximum assistance to a single project generally does not exceed the amount needed to make the project viable and comply with federal HOME regulations. HOME funds are allocated among multifamily rental housing programs, single-family homeownership programs, group homes, and rehabilitation programs. For FFY 2023, the State received $7,319,907 in federal HOME funds, with $6,677,916.30 allocated to ongoing DHCD housing programs and $741,990.70 reserved for administrative costs. At least 15 percent of the State's HOME allocation must be reserved for Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs).
structured_extraction.program_audience: State government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs), and community-based nonprofits seeking to develop affordable housing for low-income residents. Group home sponsors serving special populations also eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Build, buy, or fix rental housing, owner-occupied housing, and special needs housing such as group homes. For rental housing, residents must have household incomes at or below 80 percent of area median household income. For owner-occupied housing and homeownership projects, owners must have household incomes at or below 80 percent of area median household income. HOME funds may also be used for soft seconds to reduce home purchase costs, land acquisition, development costs, construction financing, security deposit assistance, disaster relief assistance, and tenant-based rental assistance on a limited basis. Rehabilitation of owner-occupied housing, lead paint hazard reduction, accessibility modifications, and furnace and roof replacement are eligible uses, particularly as grants.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. HOME funds are used primarily in non-Participating Jurisdictions (all Maryland counties except Baltimore City, Anne Arundel County except City of Annapolis, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties, which receive direct HOME allocations). State government agencies automatically receive either their formula allocation or $3 million, whichever is greater.
requirements_list: For rental housing units, residents' household incomes must be at or below 80 percent of the area median household income based on household size and set annually by HUD
For owner-occupied housing units, owners' household income must be at or below 80 percent of the area median household income based on household size and set annually by HUD
Maximum rent limits must not exceed HUD-calculated High HOME Rent Limits or Low HOME Rent Limits by area
If using HOME funds with other CDA programs, projects must meet both CDA program eligibility requirements and HOME program federal requirements
Eligible applicants include state government agencies, local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, and certified Community Housing Development Organizations (CHDOs)
CHDOs must be certified by the State and meet HUD's CHDO requirements
Projects must comply with federal HOME regulations and monitoring requirements including site inspections and tenant certifications
Properties financed with HOME funds must maintain affordability and low-income use restrictions; if sold or ceases low-income use, borrower must share any equity gain with the agency
Income limits vary by metropolitan area and county; refer to HUD-issued 2024 HOME Income Limits for specific thresholds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the program manager to discuss project feasibility and application procedures. State government agencies are automatically eligible. Local governments, local housing agencies, nonprofit organizations, and CHDOs must submit applications. HOME funds may be requested as part of project applications to DHCD's other housing programs or may be proposed by DHCD staff during project evaluation. For Special Reserve Fund projects, applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis with priority given to CHDOs and nonprofits; awards are recommended to the Director of the Community Development Administration and HFRC. Applicants must provide evidence of readiness to proceed, demonstrated ability, matching contributions, geographic distribution, and performance history on prior awards. CHDOs may request predevelopment loans up to $50,000 on a first-come, first-serve basis.

structured_extraction.program_description: An emergency loan program that provides financial assistance to small businesses affected by disasters. The program is only available when activated by the Secretary of the Department of Housing and Community Development for specific disaster events.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans available for renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues, operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Renovations, repairs and replacement of furniture, fixtures and equipment, inventory replacement, loss of revenues or operating and leasing expense assistance, and other costs associated with business recovery including working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County and show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events.

Business located in commercial space
Located in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Howard County, Frederick County, or Washington County
Show evidence of damage or loss associated with qualifying disaster events
Proof of insurance status required
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development Neighborhood BusinessWorks Program to inquire about application procedures when the program is activated for a specific disaster.

structured_extraction.program_description: A credit enhancement program that helps small businesses in Priority Funding Areas get loans by establishing a loan loss reserve fund. Private lenders, borrowers, and the State of Maryland each contribute to the reserve, which protects lenders if loans default. This enables lenders to approve loans that fall slightly outside their normal credit guidelines.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Participating lenders enroll loans ranging from $10,000 to $1,000,000. Lenders, borrowers, and the state each contribute to a reserve account, typically 1.5 percent from the lender and borrower each, matched by a 3 percent contribution from the program, totaling 6 percent of the loan amount. The reserve protects the lender if the loan defaults. Early loans (the first $2 million of enrolled loans per lender) may draw additional reserves on subsequent loans if needed, provided remaining claim balance does not exceed 75 percent of reserve account balance.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses, including nonprofit organizations, located in Maryland's Priority Funding Areas
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Working capital, expansion, equipment, inventory, and other business purposes. Loan proceeds cannot finance passive real estate ownership, residential or transient living facilities, institutional facilities like hospitals or colleges, adult entertainment or certain service establishments, or sectarian religious instruction.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas approved by the Maryland Department of Planning under the Smart Growth Act of 1997.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a Maryland small business, including nonprofit organizations
Business must be located in a Priority Funding Area
Loan amount must range from $10,000 to $1,000,000
Project cannot involve passive real estate ownership
Project cannot be residential or transient living facilities
Project cannot be institutional facilities like hospitals, colleges, or fire stations

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: A small business applies to a participating lender. The lender underwrites and enrolls the loan if it meets program criteria. structured_extraction.program_description: MEAP helps eligible Maryland households repair or replace heating, cooling, and water heating systems at no cost. The program operates year-round and is federally funded to make homes more comfortable.

Applicants must have household income below 200 percent of the Federal Poverty Level. Specific work eligible for assistance is determined based on a home assessment and funding availability. The maximum initial deposit is 33% of the total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible Maryland homeowners with household income below 200 percent of the federal poverty level who have non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating systems.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Repair or replacement of heating, cooling, and water heating systems.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland. Special flood assistance available in Allegany or Garrett County for homes affected by flooding.
requirements_list: Household income must be lower than the limits based on household size (200% Federal Poverty Level)
Have a non-functioning heating, cooling, and/or water heating system
Currently approved to receive Energy Assistance payments from Maryland Department of Human Services qualifies for expedited intake
Own or rent the property (renters may have additional requirements)
Provide copy of most recent electric utility bill
Provide proof of last 30 days GROSS household income
Provide copy of Social Security card(s) for all household members
Provide copy of Photo ID for the applicant
If mobile home owner: provide copy of title or bill of sale for the home to prove ownership
Complete Zero Income Form for any household member 18 years or older claiming no income
May have medical condition requiring functioning heating, cooling, or water heating systems (physician's letter required)
For homeowners applying for general repairs: provide Supplemental Financial Information, Tax Affidavit, and Credit Pull Consent
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete the DHCD Energy & Repair Programs Application and submit all required documents to Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, Attn: Weatherization, 7800 Harkins Road, Lanham, MD 20706. Instructions for completing and returning the application are located on the first page of the application. For quick application eligibility (with certain benefit programs), submit Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, and copy of most recent electric utility bill plus proof of program benefits. For standard application, submit all pages including Client Information, Household Information, Energy Consent Form, utility bill, proof of income, Social Security cards, Photo ID, and Zero Income Forms if applicable. Once eligibility is determined, a local agency will contact you to schedule a home assessment. The local agency will evaluate your service needs and discuss results with you. A contractor will then be scheduled to complete the recommended work. Incomplete applications missing required documentation cannot be processed.

If award funds support a project with addresses to be determined, awardees should provide addresses and evidence of target area eligibility as they are identified during the life of the award. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify Sustainable Community boundaries.

Capital project with at least 15-year shelf life

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Register as a new user in the Project Portal (approval may take up to 72 hours; new user registration deadline is June 11). Upload required organizational documents to your profile including: Signed Disclosure Authorization and Certification, IRS W-9 Form, operating budget for current fiscal year, most recent independent financial audit or prior calendar year IRS Form 990, articles of incorporation, bylaws, IRS tax exempt determination letter, current board of directors list, evidence of Certificate of Good Standing from SDAT, Maryland Charitable Organizations Registration letter, and corporate diversity addendum. Submit application through the Project Portal by the application deadline with all required supporting documents including evidence of site control, documentation of funding commitments, cost estimates, program guidelines, Sustainable Communities map evidence, photos, and construction/renovation plans if applicable. Maryland Historical Trust review is required for all capital projects prior to disbursement of funds. FY26 application period opened May 28, 2025 and closed July 2, 2025 at 3:00 PM. Review period: Summer 2025. Award recommendations: Fall 2025. Award announcements: Fall/Winter 2025. 50% of awarded funds must be drawn down by the first anniversary date of the award. Award term is 2 years.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides affordable loans to homeowners to address critical health and safety issues and bring properties into compliance with building codes and standards. It helps owner-occupants of single-family homes make necessary repairs. The program preserves and improves single-family properties by bringing them up to applicable building codes and standards or a minimum housing quality standard.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans are available with interest rates based on household income and ability to repay. Zero percent interest fully deferred loans secured by a mortgage are available for applicants with household income at or below 50 percent of area median income. Loans with interest rates ranging from 0% to 6% based on ability to pay are available for applicants with income up to 80 percent of area median income. The maximum loan is generally $50,000, or up to 110% of home equity, whichever is less. The maximum loan term is 30 years. Loans exceeding $5,000 or with deferred payments are secured by a mortgage (deed of trust recorded on property). There is a minimum loan amount of $5,000. Households with incomes at or below 50 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income may qualify for deferred principal and interest payments if necessary for project feasibility. Applicants with incomes at 60% of area median income qualify for 0%-4.5% interest rates. Applicants with incomes at 80% of area median income qualify for 4.5%-6.0% interest rates. The maximum initial deposit from contractors is 33% of total project cost.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owner-occupants of single-family homes whose household income does not exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Mold remediation, gas leak repair, roof repair and replacement, gutters, asbestos abatement, vermiculite removal, lead abatement, combustion appliance repair and replacement, chimney repair, foundation and sub-space waterproofing and drainage including bulk water mitigation by drain tile and sump pump, radon mitigation, electrical hazard and knob-and-tube removal, electrical upgrades for electrification (100A to 200A upgrades), plumbing issues, water and well repairs, septic and sewer work, windows and doors for health and safety or water intrusion and security, structural repair (atrophy, rot, insect damage, settling, storm-related), accessibility improvements for disabled persons and seniors (chair lifts, handicap ramps, bars, railings, doors), fall prevention measures (handrails, rubber treads, bathroom grab bars), HVAC replacement for end of service life, ductwork upgrades and installations (primarily for solid fuel-burning households, mainly in Allegany and Garrett counties), building shell stabilization (repair/replace missing sheetrock on exterior walls, point up deteriorated masonry that allows for water infiltration), and pest treatments (rats, roaches, mice).
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in most Maryland counties. Specifically not available in Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Harford County, Howard County, Prince George's County, and Montgomery County. However, the Washington, D.C. PMSA includes Calvert, Charles, Frederick, Montgomery, and Prince George's counties and has different income limits. Local government housing offices process loan requests for properties within their jurisdiction.
requirements_list: Household income cannot exceed 80 percent of the statewide or Washington, D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Area median income
Property must be an owner-occupied single-family home (duplexes, townhomes, condos, and manufactured homes are excluded)
Applicant must be the owner-occupant; renters and tenants are not eligible

Contractor must provide Certificate of Liability Insurance (current with per occurrence limits equal to or greater than $1,000,000)
Contractor must provide Letter of Good Standing from Maryland licensing authority
Contractor must provide completed and signed W-9 form with contractor's address where payments will be sent
Applicant must provide photo ID for applicant and any co-applicant (driver's license, passport, military ID, etc.)
Applicant must provide copy of deed and current mortgage statement
Applicant must provide copy of most recent Property Tax Bill
Applicant must provide copy of Declaration Page of Homeowners Insurance Policy
Applicant must provide copy of Flood Insurance Policy if applicable

Applicant must provide most recent 2 years' worth of complete Federal Income Tax Returns
Applicant must provide most recent 2 months' worth of bank statements
If income from Social Security, disability, pension, or public assistance, must provide copies of award letters and current statements verifying gross income
If reporting no income, must include signed and notarized Zero Income Statement
If not required to file Federal Income Tax Return, must provide signed affidavit explaining reason for each year
For health and safety repairs, applicant may apply for supplemental funding with additional financial documentation
No minimum credit score requirement
Cannot assist if there is active bankruptcy or foreclosure; both must be dismissed for minimum of 2 years before assistance can be provided
Work must meet critical health and safety needs requirements
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Contact your local county housing office or the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Special Loan Programs at (301) 429-7409, (301) 429-7564 (Baltimore area), or toll-free 877-218-8101. 2. Obtain at least one detailed estimate (bid) from a licensed Maryland Home Improvement Contractor or other licensed trade professional within the past 60 days for health and safety repairs needed. Include photographs documenting the issues in the bid. 3. Ensure the contractor completes the Bid Cover Page and provides all required documentation: current MHIC or trade license, Certificate of Liability Insurance, Letter of Good Standing, and signed W-9 form. 4. Gather all required income verification documents (paystubs, tax returns, bank statements, benefit letters, etc.). 5. Gather all required property ownership documentation (photo ID, deed, mortgage statement, property tax bill, homeowners insurance declaration page, flood insurance if applicable). 6. Complete the Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program application with all required information including applicant/co-applicant information, income details, housing expenses, assets, liabilities, personal debt history, demographic data, and lead-based paint notification receipt. 7. For applications including health and safety repairs, complete Supplemental Financial Information page with additional financial details. 8. Submit completed application and all required documents to: Email: DHCD.SLP_documentation@maryland.gov OR Mail: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, CDA, Special Loan Programs, 7800 Harkins Road, 3rd Floor, Lanham, MD 20706. 9. Local government housing rehabilitation offices process loan requests for properties within their jurisdiction. 10. Program staff will review the bid and all documentation to verify work meets health and safety requirements and contractor meets state requirements. 11. Upon approval, applicant must sign: Commitment letter, Rehabilitation contract, Construction agreement, and W-9 form. 12. Once all agreements are signed, funding is disbursed according to project timeline.

structured_extraction.program_description: A statewide initiative that reduces interest rates on loans for certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses by up to 2% when they obtain qualifying loans from participating banks.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Eligible borrowers can receive up to a 2% discount on interest rates for term loans obtained from participating banks. The Maryland State Treasurer's Office deposits an amount equal to the loan amount from the issuing bank and accepts a reduced interest rate on that deposit. Loans can be combined with other loan programs. Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years, and points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Certified Minority Business Enterprises and Small Businesses in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Loan proceeds must be used for projects or activities located in Maryland. Funds cannot be used for the furtherance of sectarian or religious purposes or instruction.

Borrower must notify the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development prior to obtaining qualifying loans from enrolled financial institutions
Borrower must obtain loan from a participating lender designated by the Maryland State Treasurer's Office
Loan must be a term loan or fixed-rate loan with one disbursement
Loan terms cannot exceed 10 years
Points charged by the lender cannot exceed 1% of the loan amount
Loan proceeds must be used for projects located in Maryland

Borrower must remain in good standing as a certified Minority Business Enterprise or small business with the State of Maryland to receive the interest rate reduction benefit for the full term of the loan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: An eligible applicant or participating lender submits a brief application via the Internet or paper form to the Linked Deposit Program, administered by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. After verifying the applicant's eligibility, the department forwards the application to all enrolled banks or notifies the lender of the borrower's eligibility. The borrower contacts participating banks to complete full application requirements. Banks underwrite the requested loan according to their standard underwriting with an interest rate up to 2% less than the standard rate. Upon loan approval and acceptance by the borrower, the bank enrolls the loan in the Linked Deposit Program. Participating lenders include Bank Annapolis, Industrial Bank, and Columbia Bank.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program increases the construction and rehabilitation of multifamily rental housing for families with limited incomes using tax-exempt bonds and notes. The bonds provide construction and permanent financing and work alongside federal Low-Income Housing Tax Credits. The program offers multiple financing structures including FHA-CDA Risk Sharing, GNMA loans, Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans, and Fannie Mae MBS collateral options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Tax-exempt bonds and notes provide construction and permanent financing for multifamily rental housing projects. Multiple financing structures are available: (1) FHA-CDA Risk Sharing with 40-year bond maturity and 40-year mortgage amortization at estimated all-in rates around 6.02%; (2) GNMA MBS (FHA Sections 221(d)(4)) with 40-year maturity at estimated rates around 5.92%; (3) Freddie Mac Tax Exempt Loans with 17-year maturity and 35-year amortization at estimated rates around 6.82%; (4) Cash Collateral/GNMA MBS options with 2-year construction periods and 40-year amortization; (5) Fannie Mae MBS Collateral with immediate start or forward start options at 17-year maturity with 35-year amortization. Interest rates are based on the Community Development Administration's bond rate and market conditions. Loan terms are generally 30 to 40 years for permanent financing. A first lien position is generally required. All loans must be insured or have other forms of credit enhancement acceptable to the program. GNMA Loans must have HUD/GNMA credit enhancement via Section 221(d), 220, or similar HUD programs. Upfront costs range from approximately $1,027,000 to $2,068,000 depending on financing structure. CDA Financing Fee is 1.625% on bond/loan amount. Additional fees apply for bond counsel, trustee, rating agencies, underwriters, closing attorneys, and ongoing servicing.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing Development Programs; Benedict DuRant (TEFRA matters); Kristen Musallam; Brien O'Toole

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, and rehabilitation of existing multifamily rental housing. Loans may be provided to refinance existing high interest rate private loans if done in conjunction with rehabilitation. Funds support projects with minimum five units in complete independent dwelling units.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office or specific program staff for application procedures. The program funds energy efficiency measures, limited health and safety repairs, and electrification of covered buildings. MEEHA includes two components: EmPOWER for general energy efficiency improvements and the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Program (GHGRP) for electrification and direct greenhouse gas reduction measures under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development

structured_extraction.assistance_description: EmPOWER provides either grants or loans with 0% interest and deferred payments, with $134.9 million allocated for calendar years 2024-2026. GHGRP provides grants only with $8.75 million in fiscal year 2024, and $5 million each in fiscal years 2025 and 2026. Projects receive funds during construction as work is completed and verified through a requisition process, with DHCD inspecting a sample of installed measures and processing payment within 4-5 weeks. For EmPOWER rehabilitation projects, funding is provided on a per-unit basis with different tiers based on affordability compliance periods. Tier 1 applies to projects with minimum 5 years of affordability at 80% AMI or below. Tier 2 applies to projects with minimum 15 years of affordability. GHGRP funding is limited to $15,000 per unit with a project cap of $1.25 million for eligible covered buildings with 35,000+ gross square feet.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of affordable multifamily rental housing developments seeking to reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. EmPOWER serves projects of all sizes. GHGRP specifically serves projects with existing buildings of 35,000 gross square feet or more, with at least 51% of tenants at or below 80% Area Median Income (AMI).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: EmPOWER: Reduce electric or gas consumption through energy efficiency measures including HVAC systems, insulation, fenestration, lighting, domestic hot water systems, air sealing, and appliances. Electrification measures to replace fossil fuel systems with electric equipment. Limited health and safety or incidental repairs. GHGRP: Reduce direct greenhouse gas emissions through replacing fossil fuel equipment with electric equipment, building energy conservation measures, alternative energy generating systems (solar photovoltaics), incidental repairs to change fossil fuel infrastructure to electric infrastructure. Gas reducing measures allowed only in BGE or WGL utility territory. Electrification costs cannot exceed 10% of total funding. Health and safety and incidental repair costs combined cannot exceed 10% of total energy efficiency measure funding.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All Maryland counties eligible. Gas reducing measures allowed only if customer is in Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (BGE) or Washington Gas Light Company (WGL) utility territory. GHGRP applies to covered buildings under Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards.

For EmPOWER Tier 2: Minimum 20% of households at 80% AMI or less for minimum 15 years
For GHGRP: Minimum 51% of units at or below 80% AMI for minimum 15 years

Mandatory measures must be included unless waiver granted on case-by-case basis

Insulation in gabled attics below R-19 is mandatory if accessible

HVAC replacement is mandatory when existing equipment is past useful life

Qualified Energy Professional submits funding request on behalf of project owner through MINT or Rehab Funding Request Form

For GHGRP: Minimum 15 years of affordability restrictions or property must accept regulatory restrictions for at least 15 years
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Submit completed MEEHA Application and supporting documents (application form, commercial utility bills, customer consent form, property deed, SDAT checks, MBE Plan, ACH Direct Deposit Form, affordability proof, W-9 Form) to MultifamilyEnergy.dhcd@maryland.gov. For GHGRP, also include Energy Star Portfolio Manager baseline report and third-party verification report. 2. Application reviewed by program team member for completeness and eligibility. 3. Once approved, project owner commissions Qualified Energy Professional from DHCD's QEP List to complete energy audit (for rehabilitation) or energy certification review (new construction), complying with BPI Multifamily Building Analyst standards with sampling of minimum 10% of units or 5 units, whichever is greater. 4. Qualified Energy Professional completes energy audit, determines recommended Energy Conservation Measures, obtains contractor bids, and submits Funding Request to DHCD through MINT or Rehab Funding Request Form. For GHGRP, must include greenhouse gas emissions reductions data using specified conversion factors. 5. DHCD reviews funding request and validates measure eligibility and funding amounts. 6. DHCD creates funding agreement and regulatory agreement if needed. 7. After all parties sign funding agreement, project cleared to begin construction. 8. During construction, project submits monthly requisitions with supporting documentation; for GHGRP, DHCD Project Manager conducts monthly meetings and visual inspections. 9. DHCD inspects sample of installed measures to verify proper installation and processes payment within 4-5 weeks. 10. After construction completion, project enters affordability monitoring period; DHCD monitors compliance with affordability requirements for duration of affordability period (minimum 5-15 years depending on funding tier). For GHGRP, project must provide annual energy use benchmarking reports for minimum of two years post-completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A below-market-rate loan program designed to help small businesses acquire or renovate owner-occupied real estate, purchase machinery and equipment, or expand operations. The program provides loans up to $5 million with flexible terms for working capital and real estate needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI portion of loan ranges from $350,000 to $5,000,000. Senior or junior debt available. Up to 30 percent program match. Interest rate determined by underwriting analysis. Flexible loan terms up to 30 years depending on use and loan amount. Flexible applicant cash contribution required. Personal guarantees and collateral required. Prepayment lockout period may apply. Private capital match target of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI or VSB, and 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI or VSB. Minimum required private capital match of 1:1.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses operating in Maryland with less than 500 employees. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and SEDI (Socially and Economically Disadvantaged Individuals) who own or operate for-profit or nonprofit Maryland-based small businesses. Local governments are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation, mixed-use projects combining residential and commercial uses, machinery and equipment, and other costs associated with sustaining or expanding a small business. Manufacturing, service providers, retail, office, or mixed-use projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Business must be located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area in Maryland.

Proof of private capital match with target private capital to SSBCI funds match of 4:1 (80-20) for non-SEDI/VSB or 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI/VSB

Business located or to be located in a CDFI Investment Area

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Complete an SSBCI Neighborhood BusinessWorks loan application package through the online portal. Upon loan approval, applicant receives a commitment letter from the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development. Loan approval requires applicants to meet underwriting guidelines. Applicants must execute necessary legal documents prior to loan disbursement. Application fee of $250 and closing fee of $250 apply.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program designed for Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) to relend funds to small businesses, particularly those owned and operated by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals and very small businesses located in CDFI Investment Areas. The program issues loans using State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) funds to CDFIs to be matched with private capital and relent to small businesses throughout Maryland.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI Loans of $2,000,000 to $15,000,000 to CDFIs for relending to small businesses. SSBCI Loans bear interest at 0%-2% with terms up to 7 years and annual renewal options thereafter. CDFIs must leverage private capital match with a goal of 4:1 for non-SEDI businesses and those with 10 or more employees, and a targeted private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 2.3:1 (70-30) for SEDI businesses or those with fewer than 10 employees. Each SBL to end-borrowers cannot exceed $250,000 unless prior written approval is granted. Interest rate to SBL Borrowers cannot exceed 18%. SBL terms cannot exceed 5 years unless for acquisition of assets with longer useful lives. CDFIs must have 20 percent at risk. SBL origination fees and points combined maximum 1%. Application fee maximum $100. No prepayment penalties allowed. Risk of loss is shared between DHCD and Lender on a loan-by-loan basis with SSBCI funds in top loss position.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Ongoing - Applications processed on first-come, first-served basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Community Development Financial Institutions (CDFIs) only. Priority given to SEDI (socially and economically disadvantaged individual-led) businesses and very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees located in CDFI Investment Areas.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: CDFIs relend funds to small businesses for: working capital, marketing/planning/feasibility studies, real estate acquisition down payments, minor renovations, minor leasehold improvements, machinery and equipment acquisition, and other costs associated with opening or expanding a small business.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland with focus on CDFI investment areas. Small businesses must be located in CDFI Investment Areas. Priority given to businesses located or locating in CDFI Investment Areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: CDFIs are encouraged to submit the SSBCI NBW Loan to Lender Application to DHCD. Applications are processed on a first-come, first-served basis. Once approved, Lenders receive a commitment letter from DHCD reflecting the total SSBCI Loan commitment amount, required private capital match, and proposed SBL funding timetable. SSBCI Loans must be closed in accordance with terms, conditions and documentation provided by Maryland Office of the Attorney General. Each Lender must outline its proposed SBL program with specific geographic, demographic and industry focus goals, SBL products with specific terms (interest rates, repayment terms, duration, targeted uses, credit and compliance underwriting requirements, origination and servicing fees). structured_extraction.program_description: An equity investment program dedicated to funding and supporting early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth. The program provides bridge financing to help companies reach their next equity raise after they have already secured initial investment and demonstrated traction.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: SSBCI provides venture debt on at least a pari passu (equal priority) basis with private capital match. SSBCI funds must cause and result in the private capital match. Venture debt rates with repayment in principal and interest or convertible notes. Target SSBCI portion of venture debt ranges from $500,000 to $2,500,000. Aggregate funding round must be less than $20,000,000. Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1, with target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1. Typical rounds are greater than $2,000,000. Designed for early-stage businesses with high potential job growth positioned to scale.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Early-stage businesses in Maryland with high potential for job growth that have already raised equity from early-stage investors and are seeking additional investors. Most companies are positioned to scale and need bridge financing to achieve milestones. Typical bridge rounds exceed $2,000,000. Priority given to very small businesses with fewer than 10 employees and SEDI owned and operated businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Bridge financing to help early-stage companies reach their next equity raise and scale operations.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Maryland.

Minimum required private capital match to SSBCI funds ratio of 1:1
Target matching private capital to SSBCI funds greater than 2:1
Existing paid-in capital greater than $2,000,000 or revenues greater than $1,000,000
Priority given to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and SEDI owned and operated businesses
Already raised equity from early-stage investors
High potential job growth

structured_extraction.program_name: National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund
structured_extraction.program_description: Funding program that supports strategic economic development and revitalization projects in the National Capital region of Maryland, focusing on capital projects that drive economic growth and community improvement. The program provides competitive funding for strategic investment in local housing and businesses to encourage healthy, sustainable communities with a growing tax base and enhanced quality of life.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Competitive funding for strategic investment in local housing and businesses. Award amounts vary; FY26 available funding is $8.6 million in capital and $200,000 in operating funds. Capital projects must have approximately 15-year shelf life. Operating costs support community revitalization activities. Beginning FY2026, a non-refundable Financial Assistance and Application Processing (FAAP) Fee of 4% of the awarded funds will be charged and included in the award project/program budget. The Department may also structure awards as loans or recoverable grants secured by Promissory Note and Deed of Trust, particularly for projects receiving $500,000 or more.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: July 2, 2025 at 3:00 PM (FY26 application round closed)
structured_extraction.contact_name: Jean Cannon, Program Officer (Region 6: Southern Maryland)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments and nonprofit community development organizations in the National Capital region seeking funding for strategic economic development and housing projects.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital projects and limited operating costs that support community revitalization activities and the goals and objectives outlined in a target area's Sustainable Communities Action Plan. Eligible uses include property acquisition, construction, rehabilitation, architectural and engineering designs, site development, public infrastructure improvements, and community revitalization activities. Funds support local housing and business development to create healthy, sustainable communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Sustainable Communities in the National Capital region of Maryland, specifically: (1) In Prince George's County, at least in part, within the boundary created by Interstate 495 in the State and the District of Columbia; OR (2) In Montgomery County, within an Enterprise Zone or the boundary created by Prince George's County, Maryland Route 200, Interstate 270, Interstate 495 to the Maryland state line, and the District of Columbia. Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify project eligibility.

Applicant must be eligible organization type: local government or nonprofit community development organization
Current awardees must be in compliance with terms and conditions of current award agreements and in good standing
New user account requests must be submitted by June 11 (two weeks before application deadline)
Site control documentation required

Project readiness to proceed must be demonstrated

All required legal exhibits and supporting documents must be submitted by application deadline
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Register as a new user in the Project Portal (new user deadline is June 11; approval may take up to 72 hours). Identify organization, project location, and interested funding program. Contact your regional project manager (Jean Cannon for Southern Maryland region at 410-209-5806 or jean.cannon@maryland.gov) to verify eligibility and authorize access. 2. Upload required organizational documents to your profile (see legal exhibits and supporting documents requirements). 3. Complete application in Project Portal including project information, proposed budget, timeline, readiness assessment, and project impact data sheet. Answer at least one question on the FY26 Project Impact Data Sheet to quantify results. 4. structured_extraction.program_description: The National Housing Trust Fund is an affordable housing production program that increases and preserves the supply of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: HTF funds may be used as broadly and flexibly as permitted by federal regulations to address the unique underwriting needs of each project. Forms of assistance include equity investments, interest-bearing loans or advances, non-interest-bearing loans or advances, deferred payment loans, grants, and other forms of assistance approved by HUD. Ninety percent (90%) of the HTF annual allocation is used for production, preservation and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. The Department retains ten percent (10%) of the HTF annual allocation for allowable administrative and planning expenses. Operating cost assistance may be provided but no more than one-third of the state's annual HTF allocation and must be fully utilized within 5 years of award. Projects funded through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Extremely low-income (ELI) households with incomes at or below 30% Area Median Income (AMI) or at or below the poverty line, and very low-income (VLI) households, including homeless families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Development hard costs, acquisition costs, related soft costs, relocation costs, and operating cost assistance for production, preservation, and rehabilitation of affordable rental housing through acquisition, new construction, reconstruction, or rehabilitation of non-luxury housing with suitable amenities. Projects must serve extremely low-income households and maintain a minimum 30-year affordability period for rental housing.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. For new construction projects, sites must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs) under Maryland's Smart Green and Growing Initiative, including incorporated municipalities, areas between Baltimore beltway and City limits and Washington DC beltway and boundary, Sustainable Communities, enterprise zones, county-designated PFAs, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas.

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: HTF projects are selected by the Department for funding consideration subject to availability of funds. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and evaluated using Threshold Criteria. HTF funds are awarded to eligible projects through a non-competitive, first-ready first-served basis. HTF funds may be requested by a Sponsor as part of a project application or Department staff may, in consultation with a sponsor, propose use of HTF funds during project review and underwriting. HTF funds are used to complement and work in conjunction with ongoing Department housing programs to leverage other project funding, make projects financially feasible, and increase the number of ELI households served in state-funded projects. HTF funds may be used with projects utilizing RHFP, LIHTC, MBP, STHGP, and other Department programs, or with non-Department housing program funds from state, federal, local/public, or private sources. HTF may not be used with funding sources that cannot be combined with HTF (e.g., Public Housing per 24 CFR §93.203). Successful recipients receive a Notice of Award stating Department's intent to award HTF funds. The Department requires all applications contain a description of eligible activities to be conducted with HTF funds. Projects must comply with Site and Neighborhood Standards at 24 CFR §93.150 for new construction. All rehabilitation projects must meet applicable HTF rehabilitation standards and 24 CFR §93.301(b) requirements. The HTF program requires the Department to commit funds within 24 months of HUD's execution of the HTF grant Agreement.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Community Development Administration issues bonds to fund loans for business projects. A business project qualifies if it is located in a priority funding area or Sustainable Communities and is acquired, owned, developed, constructed, reconstructed, rehabilitated or improved for the purposes of carrying on a business, whether or not for profit. The program has been financing small businesses in Maryland for over 20 years and currently manages a portfolio of 158 loans with an aggregate outstanding principal balance in excess of $20 million.
