structured_extraction.program_description: Provides funding to local jurisdictions and their ISP partners to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas. The program is administered through the Office of Statewide Broadband and was funded through the American Rescue Plan Act. Program is currently closed and not accepting applications.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants between $50,000 and $500,000 covering 70-90% of capital construction costs with 10-30% match required based on project density. Match percentage is determined by the average number of households per mile for wired projects (fewer than 8 households per mile requires 10% match, 8-14 households per mile requires 20% match, 15+ households per mile requires 30% match) or average households per tower for wireless projects (fewer than 40 households per tower requires 10% match, 40-69 households per tower requires 20% match, 70+ households per tower requires 30% match). Matching funds may come from the local jurisdiction and/or ISP partner and can include cash contributions or, for ISPs, in-kind capital construction costs. Program is currently closed and not accepting new applications.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: December 23, 2021 (Program closed - not accepting applications)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local jurisdictions (counties or municipalities) and their Internet Service Provider partners seeking to expand broadband service to unserved residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Capital construction costs to extend existing broadband service to unserved areas, including: construction of facilities to deploy broadband service at required speeds to all end users within the project area; middle mile infrastructure directly necessary to provide service to end users including interconnections between non-contiguous service areas; electronics necessary to deliver service including optical line terminals, optical network terminals, routers, switches, firewalls, wireless radio equipment, antennae, access points, modems, and necessary equipment shelters. Grant funds may not be used for engineering design services (except as allowed in match), land or tower purchases, building construction or renovation (except as allowed in match), operating expenses, or duplication of existing broadband service.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide Maryland, excluding areas that have received prior state grant funding. Project areas must be unserved, defined as lacking terrestrial, fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Megabits per second (Mbps) download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds.
requirements_list: Local jurisdiction must be the applicant and fiscal agent with an Internet Service Provider partner
Projects must serve unserved areas lacking terrestrial fixed internet service at speeds above 25 Mbps download and/or 3 Mbps upload and/or with latency above 50 milliseconds

Minimum network requirements: 100 Mbps download and 100 Mbps upload speeds with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds at served subscriber locations (exceptions allowed with ISP certification for geographic, topographic, or cost reasons, with scalability requirement to 100 Mbps symmetrical)
70-90% grant coverage with 10-30% match required based on project density
Match must be from identified sources committed by local jurisdiction and/or ISP partner
All equipment must be new and non-depreciated
Applicant must have strong incumbent ISP partner with means and desire to provide service
Project area must be identified with graphical maps showing properties to be served and infrastructure to be constructed
GIS shapefiles, KMZ, or KML files required showing project area and infrastructure
Detailed line-item capital construction budget required with quantity and cost breakdown
Projects must be completed by December 31, 2023
Local jurisdiction must enter into partnership agreement with ISP partner prior to funding agreement with Department
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete the Grant Application Form for the Neighborhood Connect Broadband Project. 2. Prepare Executive Summary describing the unserved area, how it was chosen, problems residents face, and how the project will alleviate those problems and provide enhanced opportunities. 3. Identify the ISP Partner and describe assistance or cooperation the local jurisdiction will offer. 4. Provide statement of experience of senior team from both applicant and ISP partner. 5. Submit detailed Network Design and Construction description including network speed, latency, backhaul methods, pole-attached vs. underground infrastructure for wired networks or tower information for wireless networks, and final facility ownership details. Include GIS files showing project area and infrastructure. 6. Provide Subscriber Profile with demographic data, projected subscriber take rate, and estimate of unserved households and businesses. 7. Submit Subscriber Costs and Limitations listing ISP partner service options, costs, and any limitations including data caps. 8. Provide detailed line-item Capital Construction Budget using the provided form showing all major construction work, equipment, and costs. 9. Submit Project Schedule with proposed timeline assuming Summer 2022 start, key milestones, and description of subscriber connection approach. 10. Submit one electronic PDF copy of complete Response to osb.md@maryland.gov with 'Neighborhood Connect', local jurisdiction name, and Project Name in subject line on or before December 23, 2021. 11. Include with submission: budget as both PDF and Excel spreadsheet; GIS shape/KMZ/KML file delineating served properties named to identify PFSA; separate GIS file or layer showing broadband infrastructure (line or tower locations); all items combined in single ZIP file with clearly identified filenames. 12. Identify any proprietary or confidential information in Response. 13. Applications evaluated on 25-point scoring system based on: Need for Service and Project Benefits (up to 5 points), Match Contribution Source (up to 6 points), Network Delivery Speed (up to 10 points), and Subscriber Options (up to 4 points). 14. Awards facilitated beginning April 2022 on high-to-low score basis as funding permits.

structured_extraction.program_description: Matching grants support the operating costs of certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that work with residents, financial institutions, community organizations, local governments, and the State to stabilize and improve the housing market in targeted low- and moderate-income neighborhoods. These organizations provide homeownership opportunities, home rehabilitation, homebuyer education and counseling, and community-organizing activities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Each eligible Neighborhood Housing Services corporation may apply for a matching grant up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of its annual operating budget. Umbrella corporations may apply for a grant for each program under their supervision up to $50,000 that does not exceed one-third of the annual operating budget of that program. The state grant must be matched by funds from local governments, private businesses, and individual contributions.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Low- and moderate-income households in neighborhoods served by certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs of Neighborhood Housing Services corporations that provide homeownership opportunities, closing cost assistance, homebuyer education and counseling, home rehabilitation for ownership and rental, and community-organizing activities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available in neighborhoods served by certified Neighborhood Housing Services corporations including Baltimore City, Baltimore County, and West Side, Church Street, and Camden neighborhoods in Salisbury, Maryland
requirements_list: Must be a Neighborhood Housing Services corporation approved and certified by the Neighborhood Reinvestment Corporation
Local political subdivision must agree to financially support the local Neighborhood Housing Services corporation
Local political subdivision must participate on the corporation's board of directors
Grant amount cannot exceed $50,000
Grant amount cannot exceed one-third of annual operating budget
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact the Poverty Solutions Team in the Division of Neighborhood Revitalization for information about the application process.

structured_extraction.program_description: A strategic and targeted investment designed to expand access to healthy and fresh foods in Maryland communities experiencing food insecurity by providing direct grants to eligible food retailers, supporting the development, stabilization, and expansion of retail outlets in areas where residents have limited or no access to nutritious food options.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
list_of_relevant_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants ranging from $25,000 to $150,000, with up to $2 million total funding available. Applicants may also request supplemental loan funding through DHCD's Neighborhood BusinessWorks (NBW) program, which will undergo financial review to assess debt management capacity. Funds can be used for equipment purchases (refrigeration, shelving, etc.), renovation and build-out, facility upgrades, capital costs for inventory expansion, working capital tied to expansion or construction, and infrastructure and technology for SNAP/EBT. A $250 processing fee is required for all applications and may be paid directly from awarded grant funds. No application fee. Recipients may also be eligible for co-awards through the Maryland Market Money (MMM) program administered by the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit or nonprofit food retailers serving communities with high fresh food gaps and committed to expanding access to healthy foods. Eligible food retailers include grocery stores, corner stores, farm stands, farmers' markets, food co-ops, delivery retailers, and small retail stores where the majority of inventory or sales are food-related.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of furniture, fixtures, and/or equipment (e.g., refrigeration, shelving); renovation and build-out; facility upgrades; capital needs related to inventory expansion (non-prepared foods); working capital involved with expansion or renovations/construction; and infrastructure/technology for SNAP/EBT setup. Funds must be used solely for improving or providing healthy food access.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Eligible retailers must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher. Exceptions may be granted on an individual basis.
requirements_list: Must be a for-profit or nonprofit food retailer
Must serve a community with a Maryland Community Business Compass (MCBC) Fresh Food Gap Score of 60% or higher
Must operate at least 5 days per week, year round (farmer's markets and on-farm markets exempt from 5-day requirement but must operate year round)
Must employ a maximum of 500 workers
Must be registered and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT)
Must currently offer or plan to offer fresh, frozen, or minimally processed healthy foods including fresh/frozen/preserved produce, whole grains, dairy products, and fresh meats/proteins
Must dedicate at least 20% of inventory or food-sales space to healthy food items, documented through square footage of food display space or dollar value of inventory
Must submit detailed written plan describing use of grant funds (not to exceed 2 pages)
Must provide information demonstrating how business meets healthy and fresh food criteria
Must provide one year of business tax returns, audited financial statements, or alternative documentation sufficient to demonstrate financial viability if operating less than one year
If relocation or expansion is involved, must provide supporting documentation such as lease agreement, letter of intent, or proof of site control
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants can schedule an initial consultation and submit complete applications through the online portal. The application portal opens January 20, 2026 at 12:00 p.m. EST and closes February 20, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. EST. All applications must include required documentation (use of funds plan, healthy food criteria information, financial documentation, and relocation/expansion documentation if applicable) to be eligible for review. DHCD staff evaluate eligible applications for completeness, impact, and alignment with program priorities from February-March 2026. The Review Committee (consisting of DHCD Division of Business Development leadership, Maryland Department of Agriculture, Maryland Department of Health, and DHCD Division of Neighborhood Revitalization representatives) makes funding determinations. Funding recommendations are finalized in April 2026. Award notifications and agreement processing occur in May 2026, followed by Board of Public Works approval and disbursements in June 2026.

structured_extraction.program_name: Operating Assistance Grants - Technical Assistance Grant
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to nonprofit organizations and local governments to help cover operating costs associated with community revitalization and economic development efforts, including housing and community development activities. Projects should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provide funding for operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. The maximum grant amount is $50,000 per award. No matching funds are required. All projects or activities should be completed within one year. Capital project costs and the following are not eligible: alcohol, legal controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, excursions, toiletries, fines, parking tickets, or travel costs for companions not on the team. An initial advance of up to 25% of the total award amount is permitted for the first payment request with no supporting documentation required; evidence of how the advanced funds were spent must be submitted with the next request for payment. Subsequent payment requests must include paid invoices, contracts, receipts, ledgers, and other documentation substantiating reimbursement. A minimum request for reimbursement is $1,000. The grant term is one year from the date the award agreement is signed by DHCD.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM (EDT)
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations and local governments in Maryland engaged in community and economic revitalization activities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Operating costs related to administering community revitalization efforts, including salaries, professional services contracts, technology costs, and other related administrative expenses. Eligible activities include staff and consultant services, general operating expenses, and other costs related to administering community revitalization programs. Capital project costs are not supported. Funds cannot be used for alcohol, legal controlled substances, entertainment, personal souvenirs, excursions, toiletries, fines, parking tickets, or travel costs for companions not on the team.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in Priority Funding Areas (PFAs). Use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper tool to verify if an organization or project/program is in a PFA. Additional consideration is given to projects in designated ENOUGH (Engaging Neighborhoods, Organizations, Unions, Governments and Households) areas, which represent rural, suburban and urban communities that have been historically impacted by barriers to economic mobility, and Just Communities, where all Marylanders, regardless of background, have access to fair housing and economic stability and opportunity.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a nonprofit organization or local government
Project must be located in or serve residents of a Priority Funding Area (PFA)
Project should align with local Sustainable Community Action Plans or support activities related to capital projects receiving funds from other Department or State agencies
Maximum grant request is $50,000
All projects or activities should be completed within one year
Applicants must register in the Project Portal before submitting an application
Organization profile must include all required documents before submitting application

Nonprofit applicants must provide evidence of nonprofit status (Bylaws, Articles of Incorporation, IRS Determination Letter), evidence of good standing from Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and evidence of charitable registration from Maryland Secretary of State

Current Operating Assistance Grant Program awardees must be in full compliance with all existing award agreements, including meeting all reporting deadlines and submitting all required final reports and payment requests from prior awards
Projects should be completed within one year from the grant agreement execution date
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, organizations must first register in the DHCD Project Portal by selecting 'New User?' and completing the registration request form. Registration approval may take up to 72 hours. Once approved, access the application through the Project Portal. The application portal opens February 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM and closes March 20, 2026 at 5:00 PM. Late applications will not be accepted. Applicants should request portal access and submit organizational documents at least two weeks before the application deadline to expedite processing. First-time applicants must contact a project manager for eligibility verification and system access. Make sure your organization profile includes all required documents (for nonprofits: evidence of nonprofit status, good standing, and charitable registration) before submitting, as applications missing documents may be disqualified. Virtual training sessions and a step-by-step application guide are available in the DHCD Project Portal. Applications will be evaluated using a 5-point scoring scale reflecting the overall strength and readiness of the application. Projects in ENOUGH areas may receive up to 10 bonus points, and projects in Just Communities areas will receive 10 bonus points. Review teams may conduct site visits and/or meetings with applicants.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program that provides financial assistance to help small businesses buy property they can operate in and use to build wealth. The program funds property acquisition and renovation for small business owners. Funding is provided through the federal State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) program. The program expands access to capital to small businesses across the state, with special focus on projects with significant community impacts including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_prioritized_industries: Grocery Stores and Fresh Food Retailers
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Loans ranging from $500,000 to $5 million with flexible terms designed to maximize community benefit. Borrowers must provide a minimum 1:1 private capital match. Loan terms include up to 30 years, senior or subordinate loan positions available, and interest rates determined by underwriting analysis. Borrowers must provide personal guarantees from all owners with more than 20% equity and adequate collateral. Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million. Program fees include $250 application fee, $250 closing fee, and 1% origination fee. Funds can be used for costs to sustain or expand a small business, such as purchasing machinery or equipment, and working capital; and owner-occupied real estate acquisition or renovation.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses with fewer than 500 employees that want to purchase or renovate commercial real estate, particularly those with limited opportunities for growth, including socially and economically disadvantaged individuals and micro-businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase, construct, or renovate commercial real estate, including buying the space where you currently operate, moving to a new location, buying property for the first time, or buying property as part of a company expansion. Funds can also be used for business expansion and growth, including machinery and equipment purchases, working capital. Renovation projects must be at least 51% owner-occupied upon completion. New construction must be at least 60% owner-occupied upon completion. Funds cannot be used for passive real estate investment, debt refinancing with same lender, tax repayment, equity buyouts (except majority ESOPs or worker co-ops), lobbying activities, federally guaranteed loans, or prohibited refinancing of tenant improvement loans.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide, with focus on communities and areas with high concentrations of small, micro, and socially and economically disadvantaged businesses.
requirements_list: Business must have fewer than 500 employees
Project cannot be 100% residential (mixed-use projects may qualify)
Must provide minimum 1:1 private capital match
Loan amount must be between $500,000 and $5 million
Personal guarantees required from all owners with more than 20% equity
Must provide adequate collateral
Total project costs cannot exceed $20 million
Business cannot be an adult entertainment facility, check cashing facility, gambling facility, gun shop, liquor store, massage parlor, pawn shop, tanning salon, tattoo parlor, or cannabis business
Information provided must be accurate and complete
Applicants must comply with all federal, state, and local laws including environmental, labor, and anti-discrimination regulations
Special focus given to projects with significant community impacts including job retention or creation, child care access, fresh food access, and community revitalization
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Apply online using the application portal at https://apps.dhcd.state.md.us/nbwapplication. Applicants can also apply directly with SSBCI lending partners. Schedule a consultation for more information by visiting dhcd.maryland.gov/Business/Pages/Own-Your-Future.aspx or emailing dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov. Email dhcd.businesslending@maryland.gov for a consultation about whether the program is the right solution for your business. Technical assistance is available through the MD Business Opportunity Center and F3Tech SEDI Program. All applications are subject to underwriting and final DHCD approval; program participation does not guarantee loan approval or funding. Eligible private capital lenders must be licensed in Maryland to offer small business lending and must be active in lending to Maryland-based small businesses.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. (Creating Opportunities for Revitalization and Equity)
structured_extraction.program_description: A four-year partnership between Governor Larry Hogan, Baltimore City, the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, and the Maryland Stadium Authority designed to demolish vacant buildings and catalyze redevelopment, reinvestment, and stabilization in Baltimore City neighborhoods. The initiative aims to improve economic opportunity and quality of life by creating safer neighborhoods, more jobs, more green space, and quality energy-efficient affordable housing.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Project C.O.R.E. provides funding and support for demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment activities in Baltimore City. The initiative supports workforce development training programs and partners with local trade organizations, non-profit organizations, and other state agencies to provide job-seeking residents with employment opportunities linked to demolition, deconstruction, stabilization, and redevelopment activities. The program results in creation of affordable single-family and multifamily housing, green space, and commercial development.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City residents, small businesses, job-seeking residents, non-profit organizations, and other community stakeholders in Baltimore City neighborhoods eligible for demolition and redevelopment.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds support demolition of vacant buildings, deconstruction, stabilization of properties, redevelopment activities, construction of affordable housing, creation of green space, commercial development, workforce training, and job creation activities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Project C.O.R.E. focuses exclusively on Baltimore City. The initiative specifically serves Baltimore City neighborhoods identified for demolition through community engagement processes. Other existing programs and resources serving Marylanders remain available statewide.
requirements_list: Affected residents must comply with the federal Uniform Relocation Assistance and Real Property Acquisition Policies Act of 1970 if relocation is necessary
Community input required for site selection
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Residents and organizations can participate by checking information posted to the Project C.O.R.E. web pages on the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development website. Baltimore City engages affected communities regularly through its Vacants to Value (V2V) program. The schedule of demolitions is determined after substantial community input. Details on how to apply for specific opportunities under Project C.O.R.E. are posted on the project website.

structured_extraction.program_name: Project C.O.R.E. Phase I – Demolition Of Blighted Properties
structured_extraction.program_description: The state invests funding to demolish blighted properties and city blocks in Baltimore City. After demolition or stabilization, sites are graded, seeded, and fenced for future redevelopment. Phase I includes demolition projects and redevelopment initiatives across multiple neighborhoods in Baltimore City.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The state invests $75 million over four years, with $18.5 million matching investment from Baltimore City, to demolish blighted properties and support redevelopment. FY17 Phase I awards totaled $15,860,000 distributed across 31 projects with individual award amounts ranging from $120,000 to $2,000,000. Baltimore City provides in-kind services valued at $0.25 for every $1 in state allocations. The Maryland Stadium Authority manages projects and handles site preparation including grading, seeding, and fencing. Eligible uses include demolition, stabilization, site preparation, and redevelopment of blighted residential and commercial properties.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Baltimore City agencies and nonprofit community development organizations working on property demolition and neighborhood revitalization
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Demolition of blighted properties, stabilization of historic structures, grading, seeding, and fencing of sites, and redevelopment projects including housing, retail, and community facilities
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City, with recommended demolition locations identified in Phase I clusters based on blight density mapping
requirements_list: Property must be identified as blighted by Baltimore City Department of Housing
Property must be reviewed and approved by Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
Applicants must be Baltimore City agencies or nonprofit community development organizations
Projects must align with Phase I cluster priority areas
Applicants must demonstrate capacity to manage projects and secure matching funds
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Baltimore City Department of Housing identifies potential properties for demolition and redevelopment based on blight density analysis. These properties and project proposals are reviewed with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development for final approval. The Maryland Stadium Authority serves as project manager. Awards are recommended through a competitive or prioritized selection process based on project readiness, alignment with Phase I priorities, and community impact.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Baltimore City
requirements_list: Property must be located in an area that has completed Phase I demolition
Applicant must be a public, private, or nonprofit development partner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development to access various department programs for redevelopment funding and support.

structured_extraction.program_description: A financial assistance program that activates vacant buildings, supports small businesses, creates jobs, improves commercial corridors, and increases local economic activity by providing grants to place-based economic development organizations working to revitalize Maryland's commercial corridors.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants provided to place-based economic development organizations (nonprofits and local government entities) to activate vacant buildings, support small businesses, create jobs, and improve commercial corridors. For FY2024, $8.0 million is available to be awarded. Grant funds can be used for rent, interior/exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment for small businesses occupying vacant commercial spaces. Place-based organizations can request up to 15% of the grant for operating costs (staff, professional services, marketing). Grants are disbursed when the Request for Payment/Progress Report is approved, which occurs before construction/purchasing begins. All grant funds must be expended and businesses must be operational by December 31, 2025. Operating funds are direct deposited if requested after the award agreement is executed. No match is required.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application currently closed; applications for FY2024 closed April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Place-based economic development organizations, including nonprofit organizations with missions focused on economic and community development in a district (such as Main Street Maryland programs or economic development associations) and local government entities (towns, cities, or counties). Small businesses are not eligible to apply directly but receive support as sub-grantees through awarded organizations.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Grants fund activation of vacant commercial buildings in designated Sustainable Communities. Eligible uses include: rent payments, interior and exterior renovation, furniture, fixtures, and equipment for small businesses occupying formerly vacant spaces. Up to 15% of grant funds can support operating costs for the place-based organization, including staff costs, professional services (e.g., architecture, legal), and marketing/promotion directly related to Project Restore 2.0. Funds cannot be used for: acquisition/building purchase, new construction, reimbursement for costs incurred prior to award, vehicles, or water/sewer infrastructure upgrades that are the responsibility of local government.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide in Maryland. All properties and applying organizations must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community at the time of application. Projects must activate vacant buildings in downtown and historic commercial corridors.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a place-based economic development organization with a mission focused on economic and community development in a specific district, OR a local government entity (town, city, or county)
Nonprofit applicants must have IRS-determined nonprofit status at time of application (501c3 status not required, but verified nonprofit status is required)
Organization must have at least 0.5 FTE paid staff at time of application
All properties for which funding is requested must be vacant at time of application (no executed lease with tenant at application date)
All properties must be located in a DHCD-designated Sustainable Community at time of application
Properties must be in downtown or historic commercial corridors with street-level retail that supports a walkable business district
Property must not be in indoor shopping malls, industrial parks, or office parks
Each entity can submit only one application
Eligible organization cannot apply for the same properties for which funding was previously awarded in FY22 or FY23
Property must remain vacant until the lease is executed; lease cannot be signed prior to application date
Sub-grantees (small businesses) must be legal businesses in good standing with the state
Sub-grantee businesses must be able to demonstrate ability to sustain operations beyond grant support
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are currently closed for FY2024 (deadline was April 24, 2024 at 5pm EST). When applications are open, interested parties submit via Maryland OneStop portal. Applications are reviewed after the deadline on a non-rolling basis. All applications are first reviewed for threshold eligibility. Applications meeting threshold requirements are then scored by DHCD staff (each application reviewed by two readers) on a 100-point scale based on: organizational readiness and capacity, creation of an equitable and inclusive process, project alignment with applicant's strategy, and advancement of Project Restore 2.0 goals. Highest-scoring applications are recommended for funding. Upon award, the grantee executes a grant agreement with DHCD. The grant term runs until December 31, 2025. Grantees must submit: (1) Request for Payment/Progress Report for each property before funds are disbursed; (2) Completion Report by property once the sub-grantee is operational (with U&O permit, photos, MHT determination, and paid invoices); (3) Final Report within 30 days of end of grant term (with operating cost documentation, sub-grantee operational status, and impact narrative). DHCD provides technical assistance through in-person training sessions held regionally across the state. Interested parties can sign up for DHCD news and alerts to be notified when future application rounds become available.

structured_extraction.program_description: Gap financing program that provides subordinate loans to create jobs and strengthen the Maryland economy by funding the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing. The program works in conjunction with the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Subordinate loans funded from State general obligation bonds with a maximum of $2.5 million per project (waivable in certain circumstances). Loans feature a 40-year term, 2% simple interest, and payments limited to 75% of annual cash flow. Loans are due on sale, refinancing, transfer of property, or default. During the Construction Loan Period, no payments of principal or interest are required. During the Permanent Loan Period (commencing after construction completion plus 3 months for cost certification), borrowers must pay Surplus Cash annually (on April 1 or 3 months after the borrower's fiscal year end, as specified) in an amount equal to the Applicable Surplus Cash Percentage, applied to reduce the outstanding principal balance. After full repayment of principal, Contingent Interest payments become payable from Contingent Interest Surplus Cash. Late charges of 5% apply to payments not made within 10 days of the due date.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
structured_extraction.program_audience: Developers and organizations seeking to create or preserve affordable rental housing in Maryland
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Gap financing for the creation and preservation of affordable rental housing projects financed through the Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide; available throughout Maryland
requirements_list: Project must be financed using Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development's Multifamily Bond Program and 4% Low Income Housing Tax Credits
Must meet requirements for both the Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credit Program as described in the Maryland Qualified Allocation Plan and Multifamily Rental Financing Program Guide

Required zoning for use and density must be in place at time of application with proper documentation (letter from local zoning office or approved PUD resolution satisfies this requirement; conditional use or special exception approval is not required at threshold)
Award of competitive public and private sources of funding necessary for financial feasibility must have been made
Project's Full Time Equivalent jobs must be documented using the Rental Housing Works Full Time Equivalent Job Calculator (where 1 FTE equals 2,080 hours per year)
Board of Public Works must approve all Rental Housing Works funding awards
Projects must meet scoring criteria for bond loans outlined in the Guide
Applicant must certify that competitive sources of public and private funding necessary for project feasibility have been awarded
Development or site plan approval is not required at application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis in conjunction with Multifamily Bond Program and Tax Credit applications. Applicants must submit a completed Application Submission Package with required threshold documentation including: completed CDA Form 202 clearly identifying RHW funds and conforming to RHW loan limitations; written documentation of required zoning for use and density; certification of award of competitive public and private funding; completed FTE Job Calculator; and certification form. A separate application for the Multifamily Bond Program (MBP), LIHTC, and any other DHCD funding must be completed using the Department's standard Application Submission Package and submitted in advance or simultaneously with the RHW application. Applications are tracked by date of receipt and reviewed with Multifamily Bond Program applications. If projects pass threshold, they are scored using evaluation criteria in the Guide. After scoring, kick-off meetings are scheduled with a timeline and critical path. Projects are funded on a first-ready, first-served basis. Maximum loan amount per project is $2.5 million (waivable in certain circumstances), and in no event shall RHW funding exceed an amount necessary to make a project financially feasible and viable as determined by the Department and in accordance with Section 42 of the Internal Revenue Code.

structured_extraction.program_name: Request for Interest: Federal Funding Application Assistance
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to Local Jurisdictions or their Internet Service Provider (ISP) partners to cover costs associated with preparing Federal Funding Applications for broadband expansion to unserved rural areas. The grant can pay for engineering, financial, legal, marketing studies and other approved services from outside consultants needed to prepare a Federal Funding Application. The OSB will assist applicants in developing competitive applications and coordinating with other State Agencies on the use of State assets where they will feasibly benefit the project.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants to cover costs of Federal Funding Application preparation. The OSB will reimburse for properly contracted services required for the application, such as engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other costs considered on a case-by-case basis. Maximum funding amount of $125,000 per applicant. Costs will only be reimbursed for projects that submit a completed application for the federal funding program and that meet the terms and conditions of the federal funding program.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling basis depending on federal funding opportunity and available state funding
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Jurisdictions or their ISP partners seeking to qualify for federal broadband financing opportunities to serve unserved rural residents and businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Engineering consultants, financial consultants, marketing studies, legal consultants, and other approved costs necessary for Federal Funding Application preparation. Projects must provide minimum internet connectivity of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds unless federal program is more restrictive.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Projects must be located in unserved areas as defined by federal program requirements or areas without internet service at 25 Mbps down and 3 Mbps up. Federal broadband funding programs typically do not allow funding in areas with other federal investments.
requirements_list: Must be a Local Jurisdiction or ISP partner
Project must be for broadband expansion in unserved rural areas
Must submit completed application for federal funding program
Must meet all terms and conditions of the federal funding program
Network must meet minimum requirements of 1000 Mbps down and 1000 Mbps up with maximum latency of 50 milliseconds unless federal program is more restrictive
Proposed service area must meet all federal program requirements for unserved areas
Technology neutral - any technology capable of meeting speed and latency requirements is permissible
Applicant will be project owner and responsible for overall funding and implementation
Submit electronic copy of response to OSB.MD@maryland.gov with applicant name and 'Federal Funding Assistance RFP response' in subject line

Response must include cover letter with jurisdiction and partner contact information, completed application form signed by both local jurisdiction and ISP partner, business model summary, experience statement, network design and construction description, customer profile, and implementation schedule
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested applicants should submit a Request for Proposals (RFP) response to the Office of Statewide Broadband at OSB.MD@maryland.gov. Response must include: (1) Cover letter with local jurisdiction name, authorized representative contact information; (2) Completed and signed application form; (3) Business model summary outlining network operations and customer operations; (4) Statement of experience of team participating in application preparation and service delivery; (5) Description of network to be constructed including speed, latency, backhaul method, pole vs. underground configuration; (6) Customer profile and competitive service description; (7) Implementation schedule with key milestones. The OSB will evaluate responses to guide partnership and funding allocation decisions. Evaluation is based on qualifications, submittals, and possible interviews. Response to RFP does not confer an obligation to establish a partnership. No reimbursement will be made for costs incurred in responding to the RFP.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program expands affordable housing for low-income adults with disabilities by providing rental assistance tied to specific units in approved rental housing. The program is a partnership with the Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Department of Health, helping eligible residents live in stable housing with access to supportive services.

structured_extraction.assistance_description: Section 811 provides project-based rental assistance that subsidizes the contract rent of eligible participants in rental properties that receive DHCD financing. Funds are awarded to eligible housing projects, not directly to individuals. Eligible properties receive assistance to support unit subsidies for people with disabilities.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on rolling basis; contact for additional information

Eligible residents are non-elderly adults between ages 18 and 61 with a qualifying disability who receive Medicaid and have a household income at or below 30 percent of the Area Median Income.

structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Statewide. Under the FY 2013 funding round, approximately 75 percent of units were expected to be in the Baltimore and Washington D.C. areas with the remaining 25 percent distributed on the Eastern Shore and Western Maryland. Under the FY 2012 funding round, units were anticipated to be evenly distributed between Baltimore and Washington D.C. Metropolitan Statistical Areas.

structured_extraction.program_name: Shelter and Transitional Housing Facilities Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: Provides grants to improve or create transitional housing and emergency shelters that include supportive services, with the goal of reducing homelessness in Maryland. The program provides capital financing for emergency shelters and transitional housing facilities that provide housing and support services to households to prevent homelessness and assist households to be able to live independently.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants support new construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters. Grant funds may cover up to one-half of total project costs, or under certain conditions, as much as 75 percent of total project costs. Eligible project activities include: acquiring land and buildings; conducting necessary studies, surveys, plans, specifications, and appraisals; site preparation; labor and materials for construction and rehabilitation; acquisition of machinery, equipment, and furnishings (such as HVAC systems) with a life expectancy of at least 15 years; and fees associated with real estate development including bonds and insurance. Sponsors must maintain the project as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years; if discontinued earlier, the grant becomes repayable. New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA). Equipment and furnishings must have a 15-year life expectancy, be durable, not become technically obsolete within 15 years, and not be elaborate or extravagant. Ineligible uses include refinancing existing debt, operating assistance, salaries/wages, maintenance, and replacement of existing furnishings.
structured_extraction.program_audience: 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations and local governments seeking to provide transitional housing or emergency shelter for homeless or at-risk individuals and families.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: New construction, acquisition, rehabilitation of housing, and purchase of capital equipment for transitional housing and emergency shelters with supportive services. Eligible expenditures include real property acquisition, architectural/engineering services, construction work, site development and improvements, utilities, and equipment/furnishings meeting specific durability and life-expectancy requirements. Ineligible uses include refinancing debt, operating assistance, salaries, administrative costs, and maintenance.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. All projects involving new construction must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA), which includes all incorporated municipalities (including Baltimore City with some exceptions), areas between Baltimore and Washington beltways, Sustainable Communities, Federal and State enterprise zones, areas designated by county governments as PFAs including rural villages, and certified heritage areas within locally designated growth areas. Local government letters of support are required for all projects, and new construction projects must include a letter from local government certifying location in a PFA.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization or local government
Residents served must be homeless (defined as households without permanent housing lacking resources to obtain it and in imminent danger of homelessness) or individuals
Project must be maintained as transitional housing or emergency shelter for 15 years
Local government letter of support required for all projects
New construction projects must be located in a Priority Funding Area (PFA) and include local government certification
Grant funds may cover up to 50 percent of total project costs, or up to 75 percent under certain conditions
Applicants must identify the homeless target population they expect to serve (families, women and children, single males, victims of domestic violence, etc.)
Applicants must provide complete description of supportive services to be offered to proposed target population
Applicants must submit commitment letters identifying funding sources for services and operating expenses
Supportive services must be specifically oriented to meeting needs of homeless target population and clearly defined with identified service providers
Eligible projects include apartments, condominiums, townhouses, single family detached homes, single room occupancy facilities, and group or shared housing

Equipment and furnishings must have life expectancy of at least 15 years, be unlikely to become technically obsolete for 15 years, be of durable construction, be heavy enough to prevent easy removal (except chairs), not replace adequate items already on hand, be necessary for intended functions, and not be elaborate or extravagant
All roofing projects must comply with State roofing policy (20-year minimum warranty; 60-year life cycle cost analysis for new construction)
Maryland Historical Trust must complete review and issue letter before funds are released
Comply with Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) participation requirements (State goal of 29%)
Projects must not use funds for sectarian religious instruction or sectarian religious buildings or programs
Forest Conservation Program applies to construction on land greater than 40,000 square feet
All prospective contractors must be checked against debarment list
Nonprofit organizations with Low-Income Housing Tax Credits must be sole managing general partner
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should contact the Housing Development Programs office or Multifamily Housing Programs (MHP) unit of the Community Development Administration (CDA). Applications must include local government support letters. Threshold requirements must be met for acceptance of applications. The Department conducts underwriting and construction review for projects involving new construction or substantial rehabilitation. Viability review and commitment review are conducted during processing. Maryland Historical Trust consultation must be completed before funds are disbursed. Standard processing time applies following submission of complete application materials.

structured_extraction.program_description: A designation program that supports community development, revitalization, and sustainability through coordinated strategies. It combines resources for historic preservation, housing, and economic development. The program helps local governments improve older communities and promote growth that is environmentally, economically, and socially responsible through infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and development that strengthens existing communities. Designated Sustainable Communities receive access to an interagency revitalization toolbox of financing programs and tax credit incentives.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a geographic designation that qualifies communities for access to state resources and funding programs. Communities receive support through coordinated state investment in historic preservation, housing, economic development, infrastructure improvements, and multimodal transportation. Designated areas can apply for state programs including Community Legacy Program (capital funding for business retention/attraction, homeownership encouragement, commercial revitalization, mixed-use development, and streetscape improvements), Neighborhood BusinessWorks (gap financing for small businesses and nonprofits), Strategic Demolition Fund (grants for predevelopment, demolition, and land assembly), Operating Assistance Grants (support for operating and technical assistance costs), National Capital Strategic Economic Development Fund (for grey field development), Seed Community Development Anchor Institution Program (grants and loans to anchor institutions), Main Street Maryland Program (technical assistance and training), Baltimore Regional Neighborhood Initiative (additional place-based revitalization investments for areas within and surrounding Baltimore City), and Maryland Façade Improvement Program (funds for commercial property exterior improvements). Tax incentives include enhanced Job Creation Tax Credits (up to $5,000 per job vs. $3,000 statewide, with lower job creation threshold of 25 vs. 60 jobs), Enhanced Local Tax Increment Financing Authority, and Low Income Housing Tax Credits with additional points. Financing programs include Water Quality Revolving Loan Fund, Bay Restoration Fund, Overflow and Stormwater Grants, State Highway Administration Transportation Alternatives Program, Safe Routes to School program, Sidewalk Retrofit Program, and Kim Lamphier Bikeways Network Program. The designation is valid for five years.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local governments (municipal or county) seeking to revitalize older communities and promote sustainable growth
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Communities can access state funding and programs for historic preservation, housing development, economic development, infrastructure improvements, multimodal transportation, and public amenities to strengthen commercial districts and residential communities. Eligible uses include mixed-use development consisting of residential, commercial and/or open space, business retention and expansion initiatives, streetscape improvements, homeownership and home rehabilitation programs, residential and commercial façade improvements, and real estate acquisition including land banking and strategic demolition.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The entire proposed area must be within a Priority Funding Area. The proposed community should be within or near a town center or transportation center. State Designated Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Areas automatically constitute Sustainable Community Areas. Applicants can use the Neighborhood Revitalization Mapper to verify if an address is within a Priority Funding Area or existing Sustainable Community area.
requirements_list: Entire area must be within a Priority Funding Area
Area must show a targeted approach
Proposed community must be within or near a town center or transportation center
Must demonstrate financial need for local revitalization
Must have a defined geographic area with existing built environment
Area must require revitalization or additional state investment to strengthen local market
Must submit a Sustainable Community Action Plan summarizing key initiatives and projects
Action Plan must be consistent with other existing community or comprehensive plans
Must obtain local government resolution supporting both boundary designation and Action Plan
For State Designated TOD Areas approved prior to 2023, must have approved Sustainable Community Action Plan or update TOD Designation Applications to be eligible for State SRP funding
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 1: Request an application template by sending an email to Tynan Stevenson at tynan.stevenson@maryland.gov with subject line including program type and community name. Note that for new designations, a meeting with program staff is required before applying. Step 2: Submit application including defined geographic area, Sustainable Community Action Plan, and local government resolution. Step 3: An interagency panel led by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development reviews the application. Step 4: Panel presents application to Governor's Smart Growth Subcabinet for final approval. Step 5: Once approved, designation is valid for five years.

structured_extraction.program_name: UPLIFT (Utilizing Progressive Lending Investments to Finance Transformation)
structured_extraction.program_description: A public-private partnership program designed to increase homeownership opportunities and property values in underserved communities affected by redlining and disinvestment. The program provides funding to close the appraisal gap—the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and what it can sell for on the market—to accelerate the development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing in low-income census tracts and designated Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State provides funding through UPLIFT to cover the difference between the cost to build or renovate a property and its market sale price (the appraisal gap). Qualified development teams acquire, develop, build, and sell quality affordable housing in targeted neighborhoods using a combination of public and private financing. Homebuyers acquire fee simple title using down payments, down payment assistance, first mortgage loans (Maryland Mortgage Program or other sources), other acceptable subsidy support, and a 'soft' promissory note from the Department. Developer loans are provided for the construction phase with an origination fee of 1% of the loan amount. The program includes a non-refundable application fee of $1,000 per project.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications accepted on a rolling basis as long as funding is available
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified nonprofit and for-profit development teams, local jurisdictions, and community-based organizations engaged in revitalization efforts seeking to develop affordable housing in historically redlined communities.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The assistance can be used to close the appraisal gap in historically redlined neighborhoods by funding the difference between the cost to build or renovate residential properties and the market price at which homes can be sold, enabling the development and sale of quality affordable housing. Funds support acquisition, development, construction, and sale of homes in low-income census tracts and Sustainable Communities.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be located in low-income census tracts (where 50% of households have incomes below 60% of Area Median Income or have a poverty rate of 25% or more) and designated Sustainable Communities. New construction projects are not permitted in FEMA Flood Zone areas, except on a waiver basis. The UPLIFT Qualified Areas Map identifies eligible locations.
requirements_list: Developers must submit a Pre-Application Meeting Request Form before applying
Projects must involve acquisition, development, construction, and sale of quality affordable housing
Projects must be located in both a low-income census tract and a designated Sustainable Community
Properties must be newly constructed or formerly vacant structures that will be substantially rehabilitated
Selected qualified development teams must meet all program standards and oversight requirements
Projects must comply with UPLIFT Design and Construction Standards
A non-refundable $1,000 application fee per project is required
Development teams must demonstrate acceptable credit history and current financial capacity
All development team members must submit appropriate financial statements (corporate entities submit audited, reviewed, or compiled statements; individuals submit personal financial statements)
Lead Developer must have a determinative or controlling position in the project entity

Each of the developer, builder/general contractor, architect, Neighborhood Engagement Facilitator, and marketing/sales entity must have experience as significant participants in comparably scaled projects
Projects must meet one of the following energy and environmental standards: EPA Energy Star, Enterprise Green Communities, USGBC LEED, or equivalent
Design must include accessibility features per latest USBC standards with 25% of units incorporating universal design features
New construction cost limits apply: $190 per square foot for cottages, single-family, semi-detached dwellings, and townhomes
Projects must address neighborhood conditions and strengthen community engagement
Site control documentation is required
Environmental assessments must be current (typically less than 12 months old)
All required exhibits must be included with application submission
Applications must include both electronic and hard copy versions
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Step 0: Applicants must review the UPLIFT Program Guide and schedule a pre-application meeting with DHCD staff for preliminary feedback on project specifics. Step 1: After the pre-application meeting, submit an Electronic Application Submission Request Form at https://dhcd.maryland.gov/HousingDevelopment/Pages/UPLIFT/Submission-Request.aspx; DHCD will provide access to the Application Submission Package. Step 2: Download the complete Application Submission Package composed of seven parts: (1) Application Portfolio General Elements, (2) Development Team, (3) Project Economics, (4) Project Location, (5) Design and Construction, (6) Marketing and Sales, and (7) Neighborhood Engagement. Complete all required forms, narratives, certifications, development information, and financial documentation. Step 3: Pay the $1,000 non-refundable application fee via ACH or check to the Community Development Administration Central Cashier and include proof of payment with the application. Step 4: Prepare two complete copies of the application—one hard copy addressed to Brien O'Toole, 7800 Harkins Rd, Lanham, MD 20706, and one electronic copy in the specified format. Upload all files to the provided Dropbox link in correct subfolders and submit the hard copy to DHCD's Lanham office. Step 5: DHCD evaluates applications for compliance with Threshold Criteria and scores against Evaluative Criteria across five areas: (1) Development Team Experience, Capacity, and Composition (60 points), (2) Project Impact (50 points), (3) Leveraging Resources (30 points), (4) Readiness to Proceed (30 points), and (5) Development Quality (20 points). Step 6: Projects passing threshold review and scoring adequately enter the underwriting pipeline. A Project Kick-off Meeting is generally held 45-60 days after complete application submission to determine the underwriting schedule. Step 7: Processing includes submission of a Final Underwriting Submission (FUS) updating financing, design, construction, and marketing elements. Step 8: The UPLIFT Loan Committee makes a recommendation to the Secretary for authorization to commit and deploy resources. Step 9: Following Secretary's determination and underwriting approval, DHCD issues a Commitment Letter specifying terms and conditions for closing. Step 10: Initial Financing Closing occurs with satisfactory submission of closing checklist items, represented by the Office of the Attorney General. Step 11: Shortly after closing and issuance of Notice to Proceed to the builder, a Construction Kick-off Meeting is held to coordinate construction phase, marketing, and occupancy requirements. Applicants should notify DHCD when hard copy application materials are expected to arrive. Materially incomplete applications will not be considered. All documents submitted must be current, usually less than 12 months old; updated due diligence reports may be required depending on processing length. If an application is rejected, written notice will state reasons for rejection; applicants may request reconsideration in writing within 7 calendar days to the Director of Community Development Administration.

structured_extraction.program_description: Maryland's largest residential energy conservation program that helps income-eligible homeowners and renters reduce heating and cooling costs through energy-conservation measures while addressing health and safety issues in their homes.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides energy conservation services at no cost to eligible participants. Services include a comprehensive home energy audit inspection followed by improvements such as blower door air infiltration reduction, insulation in attics, floors and walls, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace clean and tune services, safety repairs, burner retrofit or replacement, and health and safety items. Additional services may include HVAC system replacement or repair, combustion safety repairs, carbon monoxide and smoke detector installation, window and door weatherization, ductwork sealing and insulation, water heater insulation, low-flow fixtures, roof and attic ventilation, and structural repairs. All work includes a one-year warranty on labor and materials from the date of installation. Emergency heating system repairs and replacements are available November 1 through March 31 (October 1 through March 31 in Garrett County). Emergency cooling system repairs and replacements are available June 1 through September 30. Water heater repairs and replacements are available April 1 through September 30.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Housing and Building Energy Programs / Kiahnna Burney
structured_extraction.program_audience: Income-eligible homeowners and renters in Maryland, with priority given to elderly persons (over 60 years old), persons with disabilities, families with children, and households with high energy usage or energy burden.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Energy conservation measures including air infiltration reduction, insulation, hot water system improvements, lighting retrofit, furnace maintenance and replacement, health and safety repairs, HVAC system replacements, combustion safety repairs, and structural repairs in residential homes.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available throughout Maryland through local weatherization agencies in each territory. Local Weatherization Agencies (LWAs) serve the following counties and Baltimore City: Allegany County (Allegany County HRDC), Anne Arundel County, Baltimore County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Baltimore City (Baltimore City DHCD), Calvert County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Caroline County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation and Shore Up!), Carroll County, Cecil County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Charles County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Dorchester County (Shore Up!), Frederick County (Frederick Community Action Agency), Garrett County (Garrett County Community Action Committee), Harford County, Howard County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Kent County (Maryland Rural Development Corporation and Shore Up!), Montgomery County (Community Action Council of Howard County), Prince George's County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Queen Anne's County (Shore Up! and Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Somerset County (Shore Up!), St. Mary's County (Housing Authority of St. Mary's County), Talbot County (Shore Up! and Maryland Rural Development Corporation), Washington County (Allegany County HRDC and Frederick Community Action Agency), Wicomico County (Shore Up!), and Worcester County (Shore Up!).
requirements_list: Limited income household status
Household income at or below 60% of State Median Income (SMI) or 200% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL), whichever is higher

Currently participating in Utility Bill Pay Assistance through the Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP), Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or HUD housing assistance programs qualifies as automatically income-eligible
Must submit an application to apply for services
Must be a homeowner or renter in Maryland
Home must be in a condition that permits weatherization work; homes with severe structural, mechanical, sanitary, or health and safety issues may be deferred until conditions are corrected
Energy Auditors must have BPI HEP Energy Auditor Certification
Weatherization installers must have BPI HEP Retrofit Installer Technician training or equivalent skills
Crew Leaders must have BPI HEP Crew Leader training or equivalent skills
Quality Control Inspectors must have HEP Quality Control Inspector certification from BPI

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your Local Weatherization Agency (LWA) serving your county to submit an application. The agency will review your application and determine whether additional information is needed. Income and eligibility will be verified and documented. Once eligibility is certified, the local weatherization agency will schedule an energy audit inspection within 30 days of application certification. The energy audit identifies energy-saving opportunities and a package of feasible improvements is modeled. If the home's condition permits and measures are cost-effective, a work order is prepared and weatherization work begins according to program guidelines. A certified quality control inspector verifies completion of all work. Occupant education is provided to maximize energy savings. For emergency heating repairs during the no-heat season, the agency must schedule an assessment within 8 hours of receiving the lead and resolve the crisis within 5 days (36 hours for life-threatening situations).

Programs must be area eligible and provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment. The NSLP Afterschool Snack Service is a federally-assisted snack service that provides cash reimbursement to encourage or assist schools in serving snacks to children after the regular school day. Children participating in an approved afterschool care program age 18 and under, and participating children who turn 19 during the school year, are eligible to receive reimbursable snacks through the NSLP.
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts, non-profit organizations, and non-school-based organizations operating afterschool care programs for children.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for the cost of serving snacks and suppers to children in afterschool programs.

Afterschool program must provide educational or enrichment activities in a supervised environment
Non-school-based organizations must meet CACFP area eligibility requirements
Afterschool care program must primarily provide care for children after school
Program must have organized, regularly scheduled activities in a structured and supervised environment
Program must include education or enrichment activities, distinct from extracurricular programs organized primarily for scholastic, cultural or athletic purposes
Children participating must be age 18 and under, or turn 19 during the school year
Eligible education or enrichment activities include: homework assistance, tutoring, supervised drop-in athletic programs, extended day programs, drama activities, and arts and crafts programs

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Contact your local school district or the Maryland Public Schools nutrition program office for participation requirements and application procedures.
