SFAs are ultimately responsible for the administration of the snack service.

structured_extraction.program_name: Broadening Options and Opportunities for Students Today (BOOST) Scholarship Program
structured_extraction.program_description: A scholarship program that provides award funding for eligible students from low-income families to attend participating nonpublic schools. Priority is given to students who qualified for free and reduced-price school meals and received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year, as well as their siblings.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Scholarship awards are provided directly to eligible students to help pay tuition at participating nonpublic schools. Award amounts depend on household income, academic level, and any financial assistance the school provides. The base scholarship amount and additional awards for special education students are determined by the BOOST Advisory Board. Scholarship checks are sent to the school, and the parent or guardian must sign the back of the check. The award may be reduced if it exceeds the tuition owed to the school. If tuition is $10,000 with a $4,000 school discount (making family responsibility $6,000), and the award is $7,750, it will be reduced to $6,000. If the student was not enrolled, did not attend school days, or withdraws/is expelled before April 30, 2027, the school must return the undeposited check or provide a prorated refund to MSDE.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Parent applications are due May 8, 2026, no later than 11:59 p.m. EDT. Nonpublic school applications are due March 6, 2026.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Students entering kindergarten through 12th grade who qualify for free and reduced-price school meals and are enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school. Siblings of current BOOST recipients receive priority consideration. Priority is also given to students who received a BOOST scholarship in the previous year.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition and required fees for enrollment at participating nonpublic schools for grades kindergarten through 12. Funds may not be used for transportation or meals.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide. Only nonpublic schools registered to operate in Maryland and approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program are eligible to participate. As of March 2026, 178 nonpublic schools across Maryland are participating.
requirements_list: Student must qualify for free and reduced-price meals (FARMs) based on household income compared to federal poverty level guidelines
Student must be enrolled or accepted at a participating nonpublic school for the 2026-2027 school year
Student must be entering grades kindergarten through 12th grade (pre-K students are not eligible)
Parents must upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns to verify annual income and household size
Household income must meet FARMS income guidelines set by the U.S. Department of Agriculture
Nonpublic schools must hold a certificate of approval or be registered with the State Board of Education
Nonpublic schools must be approved to participate in the Nonpublic Textbook Program
Nonpublic schools must provide at least a 1st grade level program (not only pre-K and kindergarten)
Nonpublic schools must complete an online application to participate in the BOOST Scholarship Program

Nonpublic schools must comply with all reporting requirements by September 25, 2026, including: teacher certification data, student withdrawal/expulsion data, assessment results for English Language Arts, Mathematics, and Science in specified grade bands, and enrollment confirmation for BOOST students

Nonpublic schools must comply with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and not discriminate in admissions, retention, or expulsion based on race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, or gender identity or expression

Awards are ranked by priority: (1st) Renewals and their siblings, (2nd) New applicants from public school qualifying for free meals, (3rd) New applicants from public school qualifying for reduced meals, (4th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for free meals, (5th) Continuing nonpublic school students qualifying for reduced meals
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Parents complete an online BOOST Scholarship application through Submittable during the March 9 - May 8, 2026 application window and upload their 2025 Federal 1040 tax returns for income verification. Applications are reviewed for eligibility and completeness on a rolling basis. After May 30, 2026, all application data is compiled and ranked by household income as a percentage of the federal poverty index. The 7-member BOOST Advisory Board convenes in summer 2026 to determine base scholarship award amounts, additional awards for special education students, and other award criteria. Parents and guardians are notified by August 2026 via email of their award status and must accept or decline by the deadline provided. Participating nonpublic schools must confirm student enrollment for awarded applicants and provide copies of IEP, IFSP, or 504 plans for students receiving special education services. Once schools complete enrollment confirmation and required reporting, MSDE prepares scholarship checks at the Office of the Comptroller of Maryland. Scholarship checks are delivered to schools via FedEx between September and December 2026. No new awards are offered after December 11, 2026. MSDE offers customer service support sessions for parents on March 10, March 12 (with certified interpreter), and weekly Wednesdays from 12-1 pm (starting March 18, with interpreter available).

structured_extraction.program_name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
structured_extraction.program_description: The Child and Adult Care Food Program provides nutritionally balanced meals that contribute to the wellness, healthy growth, and development of young children, and the health and wellness of older adults and people with chronic disabilities. The program reimburses child and adult care agencies with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that comply with USDA nutrition standards and meal patterns.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The CACFP reimburses participating child and adult care agencies with federally-funded dollars for meals and snacks that meet USDA nutrition standards. CACFP sponsors receive cash-in-lieu of USDA Foods with their CACFP meal reimbursements. Over 300 agencies across Maryland participate in the program, including childcare centers, daycare homes, afterschool care programs, children in emergency shelters, and adult daycare facilities for people over 60 or living with disabilities. The annual maximum reimbursement for a child or adult care center serving 25 free-eligible participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week can reach approximately $28,000 (amount based on typical USDA reimbursement rates). Family Child Care Homes can receive up to approximately $6,500 annually for serving 6 Tier I participants breakfast, lunch and a snack 5 days per week.

For Family Child Care Homes: Contact a sponsoring organization in your region (Cecil County Government: 410-996-0253; Frederick County Community Action Agency: 301-600-6263; Montgomery County Public Schools: 301-284-4937; Prince George's County Public Schools: 301-817-0535; The Planning Council: 757-657-0716). Providers manage financial claims through the Maryland Accountability and Reporting System (MARS).

structured_extraction.program_description: A federal program that requires local education agencies identified as having disproportionate identification of students by race or ethnicity in special education, placement, or discipline to reserve 15 percent of IDEA Part B funds to implement proactive and responsive actions addressing root causes of over-identification. The program funds educational and behavioral evaluations, services, support including evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, and systemic change efforts.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local education agencies identified by the state as having significant disproportionality in identification, placement, or discipline of students by race or ethnicity must reserve 15 percent of their IDEA Part B Section 611 and Section 619 funds to implement comprehensive coordinated early intervening services. Funds support educational and behavioral evaluations, services and support including evidence-based literacy instruction, professional development, coaching, consultation, data systems development, and implementation of systemic changes to address root causes of over-identification. Allowable expenditures include salaries for coaches, mentors, general education teachers, guidance counselors, psychologists, RTI/MTSS coordinators, social workers, substitute teachers, and extended contracts for staff; professional development services; instructional materials and software for academic or behavioral interventions; computers and devices for intervention delivery; travel for professional development; tutoring services; and other implementation costs. Unallowable costs include special education evaluations for eligibility determination, universal screening, student transportation, furniture, office equipment, occupancy costs, and alternative programming that replaces core curriculum.
structured_extraction.contact_name: Gary W. Richardson, MBA (Branch Chief); Demetria White (Interagency Specialist)

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Local education agencies identified as having significant disproportionality submit a comprehensive coordinated early intervening services plan using the state template. Required fiscal documents include the MSDE Grant Budget C-1-25, separate Budget Detail Form for each C-1-25, and documentation of allowable costs aligned to the CCEIS Allowable Costs guidance. Grant amendment requests are due by August 15.

structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services Waiver for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (Autism Waiver)
structured_extraction.program_description: Community-based, long-term, person-centered therapeutic services and support for eligible children and youth with Autism Spectrum Disorder to enable home and community living as an alternative to institutional care.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The waiver provides funding for approved Medicaid provider agencies to deliver seven types of services: Intensive Individual Support Services (one-on-one assistance based on the child's need for interventions and support to acquire self-help, socialization, communication, daily living, functional living, behavior management, and adaptive skills); Therapeutic Integration-Regular or Intensive (structured programs outside school hours providing therapeutic activities and expressive therapies for children with socialization, isolation, hyperactivity, impulse control, and behavior problems); Respite Care (short-term supervision and assistance with activities of daily living); Environmental Accessibility Adaptations (funding for physical home adaptations to ensure health, welfare, and safety); Family Consultation (individualized consultation and training for the child's family); Adult Life Planning (family-centered support in accessing adult community services); and Residential Habilitation-Regular or Intensive (community-based residential placement for children who cannot live at home). Participants also receive Service Coordination and targeted case management through their local education agency. The waiver qualifies participants for full Medical Assistance benefits including health insurance, prescription coverage, dental care, physician and hospital care, home health, laboratory services, disposable medical supplies, durable medical equipment, and mental health services. Participants must maintain eligibility by using at least 5 hours of Autism Waiver services per month.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: 45 days from the date of application letter from MDH
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and youth ages 1 through the end of the school semester when the child turns 21 years old who have Autism Spectrum Disorder or an educational classification of Autism and reside in Maryland.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Community-based therapeutic services, home accessibility adaptations, family consultation, one-on-one support services, residential placement, respite care, after-school and weekend therapeutic programs, and full Medical Assistance benefits.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Children and youth must be residents of Maryland.
requirements_list: Be a resident of Maryland
Be between the age of 1 and 21 years old
Have a current educational classification of Autism or a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder

Receive early intervention or special education services identified through one of the following: an Individual Family Service Plan (IFSP) for ages 1-5, an Individual Education Program (IEP) in an early childhood or Kindergarten setting for ages 3-5, or an IEP with 15 hours or more of special education and related services and/or 1:1 adult supports per week for first grade through high school exit
Meet an institutional Level of Care for Intermediate Care Facilities for individuals with Intellectual Disabilities (ICF-IID) and choose to receive Autism Waiver services as an alternative
Be able to be served and safely maintained in the home and community with Autism Waiver services
Meet financial eligibility for Medical Assistance with monthly income not exceeding 300% of Supplemental Security Income (SSI) benefits and countable assets not exceeding $2,000
Choose the Autism Waiver as the waiver that best meets the child's needs

Military Exception: Dependents of US Military Service members invited to apply to the Autism Waiver while the family is out of state for military services shall be offered an opportunity to apply upon request when they return to Maryland and meet all technical eligibility requirements
Register with the Autism Waiver Registry at 1-866-417-3480 to be eligible to apply when a vacancy occurs
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Call the Autism Waiver Registry Helpline at 1-866-417-3480 to register as interested in Autism Waiver services and provide child information (name, date of birth, address, county of residence, contact information). Parents must confirm the child has an ASD diagnosis, an IFSP or IEP, and at least 15 hours of special education/related services per week on IEP (1st grade and above). 2. MDH vendor conducts initial screening during the intake call based on parent self-report to verify technical eligibility criteria. 3. If technical eligibility is met, the child's name is added to the Registry and MSDE is notified; a letter is sent to the family. 4. MSDE verifies technical eligibility (resident of MD, under age 21, Autism Spectrum Disorder diagnosis, IFSP or IEP with 15 hours of special education/health-related services). 5. If verified, the child is added to the Autism Waiver Waitlist; a letter is sent confirming the name is on the waitlist and includes the Autism Waiver Fact Sheet. 6. If additional information is needed, a letter is sent with a 30-day deadline to provide updated information. If not provided, a final notice is sent with a 15-day deadline. 7. When a vacancy occurs, MDH sends an invitation letter to apply and a 45-day deadline to accept the invitation, establish contact with the Autism Waiver Contact at the local education agency (LEA), complete the technical eligibility checklist, and submit the financial application. The invitation includes the Medical Assistance (MA) Financial Application, Parental Rights and Responsibilities, Autism Waiver Contact List, and Application Documentation Checklist. 8. The family works with the Autism Waiver Contact at the LEA to confirm technical, financial, and medical eligibility. 9. The child contributes to the Level of Care assessment process that determines medical eligibility. 10. LEA/MSDE track application progress. 11. Upon eligibility determination, the family receives notification from the State. If eligible, the letter includes a start date to begin Autism Waiver services. 12. The family attends a multidisciplinary team meeting to develop a Plan of Care. Application is based on chronological order from the time the child's name is placed on the Waitlist. Parents must ensure all demographic information stays up to date and contact the Helpline to report any changes.

structured_extraction.program_description: The program provides nutritionally balanced, low-cost, or free lunches to children each school day. School meals include expanded access to fresh fruits, vegetables, whole-grain menu items, with reduced sodium and saturated fat content.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses schools with federal dollars for meals that comply with USDA nutrition standards. Students receive lunches at no charge or at reduced price depending on eligibility. Children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level receive free meals. Children from families with incomes between 130 and 185 percent of the federal poverty level receive reduced-price meals. All children determined as eligible in the reduced-price category receive free meals due to state funding under the Maryland Cares for Kids Act. Income eligibility guidelines are updated annually (effective July 1, 2023 through June 30, 2024: free meals for household of 1 at $18,954 annual income; reduced-price meals at $26,973 annual income, with adjustments for larger household sizes).
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Annually
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children in Maryland public schools and participating private schools and residential childcare institutions. Eligibility includes children from families with incomes at or below 130 percent of the federal poverty level for free meals, or between 130 and 185 percent for reduced-price meals. Children in Head Start or Even Start programs, categorically eligible children, homeless or foster children, and children receiving Medicaid also qualify.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: School meal provision meeting USDA nutrition standards. Meals must comply with Maryland Nutrition Standards for all foods sold in school, including specific requirements for calories, sodium, fat, and sugar content. All foods sold must meet one general standard (whole grain-rich, fruit/vegetable/dairy/protein as first ingredient, or contain at least 1/4 cup fruit/vegetables) and all nutrient standards.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: All 24 Maryland public school systems and 22 non-profit private schools and residential childcare institutions participate in the program.
requirements_list: School must comply with USDA nutrition standards and Maryland Nutrition Standards for all foods sold in school
School must participate in the National School Lunch Program

Food must be whole grain-rich (at least 50% whole grain by weight or whole grain as first ingredient) OR have fruit, vegetable, dairy product, or protein food as first ingredient OR be a combination containing at least 1/4 cup fruit and/or vegetables
Snack/side dishes must not exceed 200 calories and 200mg sodium
Entrees must not exceed 350 calories and 480mg sodium
Total fat must not exceed 35% of calories; saturated fat must be less than 10% of calories
Sugar must comprise 35% or less of total weight of serving

Beverages must comply with specific standards: plain water unlimited; low-fat/non-fat milk limited to 8 fl oz (elementary) or 12 fl oz (middle/high school); 100% fruit/vegetable juice limited to 8 fl oz (elementary) or 12 fl oz (middle/high school); soda and caffeine not allowed

Policy applies to all foods and beverages sold on school campus from 12:01 am through 30 minutes after end of school day, including cafeteria a la carte items, vending machines, school stores, and fundraising activities
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Children qualify for free or reduced-price meals through: attending a Community Eligibility Provision school, attending a school participating in Maryland Meals for Achievement, enrollment in Head Start or Even Start, categorical eligibility through participation in federal assistance programs, direct certification through Medicaid participation, or income eligibility based on household income and family size as outlined in the annual Income Eligibility Guidelines. Schools evaluate household income by comparing reported income to the published Income Eligibility Guidelines for the appropriate frequency and household size. When household reports income sources at more than one frequency, annualize all income and compare to annual guidelines.

structured_extraction.program_description: State aid program that provides tuition reimbursement for students placed in nonpublic special education schools through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process. The State covers a portion of the cost of nonpublic special education based on the formula in Maryland Education Article §8-415. The program supports both MSDE-approved day and residential programs as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The State reimburses a portion of tuition costs for eligible students placed in nonpublic special education schools through the NTAP program. Students are included in the September 30th enrollment count with code 09 to indicate nonpublic placement. The State's share is calculated according to Maryland Education Article §8-415. Reimbursement covers standard educational and related services, extended school year services, residential services (when applicable), and additional related services and supplemental aids specified in the student's IEP. The specific reimbursable services and costs are detailed on an accompanying cost sheet submitted with each application. Reimbursement applies to MSDE-approved day and residential programs, as well as individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state special education programs with appropriate justification and documentation.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Applications must be submitted within specified timelines depending on entry date and program type
structured_extraction.program_audience: School districts and local education agencies placing students with special education needs in nonpublic schools, including MSDE-approved day and residential programs and individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tuition costs for students placed in nonpublic special education day and residential schools, including standard educational and related services, extended school year services, IEP residential services when applicable, and additional related services and supplemental aides as specified in the student's IEP

requirements_list: Student must be placed in a nonpublic special education school through the Individualized Education Program (IEP) process
School must be MSDE-approved for day and residential program placements, or justification must be provided for non-approved or out-of-state placements
Applications for ESY or entry dates occurring during July/August must be submitted by September 30
Applications for entry dates on or after September 1 to June 2 must be submitted within 30 calendar days of entry date
Applications for entry dates between June 3 and June 30 must be submitted by July 7
Discharge applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of discharge date
Service revision applications must be submitted within 30 calendar days of service revision date
An approved cost sheet must accompany each application

For individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, required documentation includes: approved cost sheet, IEP team minutes supporting placement, letter from service-providing school stating ability to implement FAPE in least restrictive environment, and copy of mediation or due process agreement if applicable
LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee signature required to authorize submission and assure compliance
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: School districts submit applications to MSDE for nonpublic special education placements. Applications must include completed NTAP application forms (separate forms for MSDE-approved day/residential programs versus individual non-approved or out-of-state placements), an accompanying approved cost sheet, and supporting documentation. For new or renewal individual placements in non-approved or out-of-state programs, districts must also submit IEP team minutes, a letter from the school confirming ability to provide FAPE, and documentation of any mediation or due process agreements. The LEA Special Education Supervisor/Director or designee must sign and date the application to authorize submission and verify accuracy of all information. Applications are reviewed and processed according to MSDE directions and guidelines. Specific submission timelines depend on the entry date and application type (new, renewal, re-entry, discharge, service revision, or correction). MSDE may audit and investigate application contents and supporting documentation. Discrepancies or noncompliance findings may result in requirement for refund of state funds.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Maryland State Department of Education provides annual grants to qualified non-profit organizations that offer enriching educational programs to Maryland students. These programs provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities and cannot be replicated in the classroom. Programs emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services, including free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, and professional development for teachers that connect programs to classroom curriculum.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are provided to qualified non-profit organizations. Grants support enriching educational programs including experiential learning, one-on-one support services, free or reduced admission, full-day and residential field trips with hands-on activities, mentoring, tutoring, pre- and post-visit activities for teachers to connect experiences to classroom curriculum, and professional development opportunities for teachers. Funds may be used for salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may not be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food. For FY 2027, approximately $6,706,449 is available with an estimated 60-65 grants to be awarded.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified non-profit organizations that are 501(c)(3) entities in good standing and provide direct service to Maryland students and teachers.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must be used to provide direct services to students and teachers within the fiscal year for which they are granted. Approved uses include: salaries, wages, and stipends for direct service to students and educators; supplies and materials to implement the educational program; outreach, engagement, informational, and marketing tools to expand reach; equipment necessary for direct service to students and teachers; and contractual expenses. Funds may not be used for construction or capital improvements, transportation of students, utilities or operating costs, or food.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Programs serving Maryland students. For fiscal year 2026, fifty-seven organizations were funded across the State. All Maryland counties are eligible.
requirements_list: Applicant must be a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in good standing
Organization must be incorporated or registered under the laws of Maryland
Organization must be exempt from federal income tax under section 501(c)(3), (4), or (6) of the Internal Revenue Code
Organization must be current in payment of all tax obligations to the State or any unit or subdivision of the State
Eligible programs must provide learning experiences that align with the State's curricular and educational priorities
Programs cannot be replicated in the classroom
Programs must emphasize experiential learning and one-on-one support services
Organization must provide direct service to Maryland school groups or to individuals with disabilities
Organization must submit a Fiscal Impact Statement describing the educational program, amount requested, populations served, educational goals and objectives, and anticipated outcomes
Organization must provide names and affiliations of independent governing board members
Organization must provide proof of 501(c)(3) status
Organization must provide a copy of the most recent independent annual audit or internally generated financial statement until audit is available
Organization must provide evidence of active liability insurance coverage

Organization must submit a detailed operating budget indicating less than 50% of budget comes from state grants (except Baltimore Zoo), specifying all sources of income including grants and all expenditures

Organization must provide evidence of direct service provision to Maryland school groups or individuals with disabilities, including data on age levels and projected numbers of students and teachers to be served statewide and by jurisdiction
Organization must submit plans for alignment of educational programs with MSDE educational and curricular priorities
New applicants must provide evidence that the program is not new and can show a track record of success
No more than 20% of participants served may come from nonpublic or homeschools
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications open May 1, 2025 and are due by June 13, 2025, no later than 5:00 p.m. EDT. Applicants must download the electronic application, complete it with all required attachments, save it as one PDF file, and submit via email to sai.applications@maryland.gov. MSDE reviews applications on a rolling basis and offers customer service support sessions on May 5 and May 23, 2025 to review program requirements and provide application walkthroughs. A review committee evaluates applications using a scoring rubric. For any application sections scored as Level 1 (does not meet criteria), written feedback is provided and an opportunity to revise and resubmit is offered. Results are communicated to the State Superintendent in July and provided to the State Board of Education for review in August. Final approval for awards is determined by legislation as authorized by the budget bill for fiscal year 2027. The Governor releases the draft budget bill in January-April 2026, which is voted on and finalized around April 2026. The grant period runs from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Grantees must submit interim progress reports by January 31, 2027 and final progress reports by August 15, 2027. Site visits occur throughout the grant period and must be completed by June 30, 2027.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally-funded, state-administered program that provides free nutritious meals to children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income areas during summer months when school is not in session. The program reimburses providers who serve meals and can be combined with summer activity and enrichment programs.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program reimburses organizations that serve free meals to children and teens in low-income areas during summer. Meals must meet federal nutrition requirements. Two program types are available: SUN Meals (meals consumed on-site with activities) and SUN Meals To-Go (multi-day meal boxes for pickup, registration required).
structured_extraction.program_audience: Children and teens 18 years and younger in low-income areas during summer months when school is not in session. Organizations seeking to become meal service sites.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Reimbursement for providing free nutritious meals that meet federal nutrition requirements to eligible children and teens during summer.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Available statewide in Maryland. Low-income areas are prioritized for meal site locations.
requirements_list: Must serve children and teens 18 years and younger
Meals must meet federal nutrition requirements
Meals must be provided during summer months when school is not in session
SUN Meals sites must provide on-site meal consumption and activities
SUN Meals To-Go sites require participant registration
Organizations must contact their county sponsoring organization to apply
Participant must be aged 18 and under
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations interested in becoming SUN Meals sites must contact the sponsoring organization for their county. Each county has a designated sponsoring organization (typically the county public school system or county department). Contact information for all 24 Maryland counties is provided on the program website. Eligible children and teens can access free meals at participating summer program sites throughout Maryland.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides additional funding to local education agencies participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option to support a USDA Team Nutrition grant project. The goal is to build state capacity to create new, high-quality, appealing standardized recipes for Maryland schools using local agricultural products, developed in partnership with chefs from Prince George's Community College. Funding supports staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and purchases food and supplies for these events. Feedback from tasting events is used to modify recipes to align with students' flavor preferences and school implementation capabilities. The program involves testing four types of recipes: Vegetable Side Dish, Chicken or Fish Bowl, Vegetarian Bowl, and Entrée Salad.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Local Education Agencies receive grant awards from MSDE to support staff time for training and recipe tasting events, and to purchase food and supplies for these events. MSDE anticipates awarding ten (10) grants, with additional grants possible if funds are available. Grant period: May 1, 2022 – September 30, 2023. Funds may be used for: (1) Salaries/wages to hire substitute school nutrition staff to allow staff to attend training; (2) Stipends for staff time to attend training activities outside of normal work hours; (3) Food and nutrition equipment and smallware costs (total value cannot exceed 5% of LEA subgrant total); (4) Food costs for grant-related training and taste tests (cannot exceed 20% of LEA subgrant total, must comply with Buy American Provision). Funds may not be used for: child nutrition program costs outside grant scope, purchasing meals and snacks for training participants, foods used for meals receiving reimbursement under FNS programs, foods used as incentives or prizes, foods provided to students and families for home preparation, foods not related to standardized recipes, any costs associated with prizes or incentive items, gardening tools or materials, or clothing such as chef hats, aprons, and shirts. Training and nutrition education resources related to the recipes are developed by Maryland SNAP-Ed and made available to school nutrition staff and teachers.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: April 22, 2022, no later than 5:00 pm EST
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local Education Agencies participating in the National School Lunch Program or Seamless Summer Option during School Year 2021-2022. Up to three schools per LEA, with at least two schools serving different grade levels if more than one school is selected.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Staff time for training and recipe tasting events, purchasing food and supplies for these events, substitute staff salaries, stipends for staff training outside normal work hours, and equipment/smallware for recipe development and preparation. Food expenditures limited to 20% of subgrant total; equipment limited to 5% of subgrant total.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Maryland statewide for Local Education Agencies. Priority consideration given to schools in rural zones as defined by USDA maps and schools located in Internal Revenue Service (IRS) designated Qualified Opportunity Zones.
requirements_list: Participation in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP) or Seamless Summer Option (SSO) during School Year 2021-2022
Local Education Agency (LEA) status in good standing
LEA must designate a Grant Coordinator to serve as primary liaison with MSDE and grant partners
Selected schools must be registered as Team Nutrition Schools prior to application submission
LEA commits to designate up to three participating schools
If more than one school selected, at least two schools must serve different grade levels
School nutrition staff must attend required training events hosted by MSDE and/or grant partners
Schools must prepare at least one chef-designed recipe and host two or more student taste tests per recipe between Spring 2022 - Spring 2023
LEA and schools must menu and serve at least one final recipe in a reimbursable meal by end of grant
Grant Coordinator must participate in periodic virtual meetings with grant partners
Grant Coordinator must submit quarterly reports on fund utilization
Grant Coordinator must manage data collection from recipe tasting events
Grant Coordinator must secure photographs, data, and success stories for MSDE quarterly progress reports to USDA
Schools must use provided nutrition education resources to implement nutrition education for local products used in recipes
All participating schools must be in NSLP or SSO
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants must complete the following steps: (1) Identify up to three schools to participate, ensuring they participate in NSLP or SSO and are registered as Team Nutrition Schools; (2) Complete a School Agreement Form for each participating school, requiring signatures from School Principal, Kitchen Manager, and a third school staff member (such as School Health Council member, Title 1 Coordinator, or Community Coordinator); (3) Complete the Team Nutrition Grant Application Form, including all required components (school listing, recipe selection for each school, budget, and school agreements); (4) Complete the Team Nutrition Budget Form (excel file) with budget narratives for each category (Salaries and Wages, Contracted Services, Supplies and Materials, Other Charges, Equipment and Furniture); (5) Obtain signatures from Local School System Superintendent, Food and Nutrition Services Director, and LEA Grant Coordinator on LEA Agreement Form; (6) Submit application electronically (saved as PDF) along with all required attachments to NutritionTraining.MSDE@maryland.gov. Required attachments include: MSDE Signed Assurances Page, signed copies of LEA and School Agreement Forms, and Team Nutrition Budget (excel file). MSDE reviews applications for eligibility and completeness, then scores applications using selection criteria based on Free and Reduced-Price enrollment percentage (0-3 points), rural zone location (up to 3 points), and Qualified Opportunity Zone location (up to 3 points). Award notification sent by email, with official Notice of Grant Awards (NOGA) processing beginning May 1, 2022, taking 4-6 weeks. An informational webinar is held on March 31, 2022, from 2:00-3:00 pm to describe the application process, overview grantee requirements, answer questions, and provide support.

structured_extraction.program_name: Title IV, Part B Nita M. Lowey 21st Century Community Learning Centers (CCLC) Grant Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program creates community learning centers that provide students with academic enrichment opportunities and services designed to complement their regular school programs. Community learning centers offer literacy instruction and related educational development programs for families of participating students. The program targets students and families who attend schools eligible for Title I schoolwide programs or schools serving high percentages of students from low-income families. Out-of-school time (OST) programs occur before school, after school, during the summer, and on Saturdays to keep students safe, assist working families, and improve academic achievement.
structured_extraction.agency: Maryland State Department of Education
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are awarded to eligible organizations to establish and operate community learning centers. Grant awards are level funded at 100% of the original award for all three years of programming, contingent on the availability of funding and satisfactory performance. Total funds available: $22.6 million (FY25). Grantees must meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served and demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives. Grantees are expected to attend bi-monthly networking meetings where the Maryland State Department of Education provides technical assistance, peer-to-peer support, and resources based on grantee needs. Grant funds must be expended in the grant year they were awarded; MSDE does not allow carryover of unobligated funds into the following grant year. Funds support academic enrichment opportunities, educational services, literacy instruction, and related educational development programs for students and their families, including core academic subject instruction, arts and music education, tutoring, mentoring, technology education, drug and violence prevention programs, and counseling services.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Friday, August 29, 2025
structured_extraction.contact_name: Reginald Burke, Executive Director, Office of Federal Programs
structured_extraction.program_audience: Local education agencies, community-based organizations, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, for-profit corporations, and consortiums of two or more eligible entities that provide services to students and families attending Title I schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Academic enrichment opportunities, educational services, literacy instruction, related educational development programs, salaries and fringe benefits for OST staff, professional development and trainings, consultants and evaluators, classroom materials and supplies, remedial and enrichment activities, core academic subject instruction, arts and music education, entrepreneurial education and college/career readiness programs, tutoring and mentoring programs, programs for limited English proficient students, recreational activities, technology and telecommunications education, expanded library services, drug and violence prevention programs, counseling programs, and character education programs.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Services must be provided to students and families primarily attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving a high percentage of students from low-income families. Schools eligible to receive services include: Title I schools serving at least 40% of students from low-income families, high schools with graduation rates less than 67%, and other schools determined by the LEA to need intervention and support. Comparable opportunities must be provided for both public and private school students in the area served by the grant.
requirements_list: Services must target students and families attending Title I eligible schools or schools serving high percentages of low-income students
Organizations must provide both student academic enrichment and family literacy instruction programs
Grantees must attend bi-monthly networking meetings for technical assistance
Grantees must attend required out-of-school (OST) national and regional conferences, MSDE grantee meetings and trainings
Grantees must meet or exceed 85% of the proposed level of students served as indicated in the original application or Grant Renewal Application
Grantees must demonstrate adequate progress toward achieving all measurable objectives
Eligible organizations include non-profit agencies, city or county government agencies, faith-based organizations, institutions of higher education, and for-profit corporations
A consortium of two or more agencies or organizations may apply
Grantees must submit required documentation timely, including monitoring components, corrective actions, monthly reimbursement reports, and detailed local narrative evaluation reports
Grantees must maintain and submit Government Performance and Results Act (GPRA) data to the U.S. Department of Education 21 Annual Performance Report database by established deadlines
Grantees must participate fully in statewide evaluation activities
Grantees must comply with all applicable state statutory and regulatory requirements
Grantees must provide evidence of compliance with federal, state, and local fire, health, zoning codes, and safety standards

Non-LEA subrecipients operating in non-public school facilities must submit all required licenses and certifications for health and safety including Use and Occupancy (U&O) permits and current Fire Inspection reports per operating site

Programs must provide minimum hours: School Year Programs require at least 12 hours per week for 25 weeks OR 4 hours on Saturdays only for 25 weeks, with at least 4 hours of academic programming per week OR 1 hour per Saturday for 25 weeks; Summer Programs require at least 80 hours with at least 32 hours on-site for academic and enrichment programming
Academic enrichment programs must be based on evidence-based research meeting Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA) evidence criteria
Grant funds must be expended in the grant year awarded; no carryover of unobligated funds is permitted
Final expenditure reports are due 60 days after end of grant period
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations submit grant renewal applications electronically through Qualtrics for their respective cohort (Fiscal Year 2024 or 2025). The renewal application requires submission of programmatic and fiscal outcome data for the prior grant award period and a grants management plan for review in consideration for continued funding. Applications must include Performance Goals and Indicators, Evaluation Plan, Management Plan, and Partner Plan as exhibits. MSDE reviews the grant renewal application and year performance data including Start-up reports, Critical Elements Monitoring stages, timely reimbursement invoice submissions, and total number of amendments. Upon review, subgrantees approved for continued funding receive a risk assessment level (1-5) reflected on the Notification of Grant Award (NOGA). Customer Service Support Sessions are available to assist with the application process. Applications are submitted by the stated deadline (August 29, 2025 for FY26). MSDE uses standards in the Uniform Guidance to impose specific or 'high risk' conditions on applicants selected for funding based on history of compliance, performance goal achievement, and other factors.

structured_extraction.program_description: A loan program that provides gap financing to small businesses seeking to locate or expand in Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. The program creates a revolving pool of money where businesses repay loans and funds are redeployed to make additional loans, supporting job creation and business expansion in the Appalachian region.
structured_extraction.agency: Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans from $10,000 to $400,000. It offers this financing as gap funding, meaning a bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. The interest rates connect to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate. Borrowers repay loans and the money is returned to the revolving loan fund to make additional loans, creating an ongoing financial tool. The program has been in operation since 1980 and operates by participating with banks and other lenders to assist in financing business projects.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Small businesses seeking to locate or expand in western Maryland's Appalachian region. This program is for businesses, including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships. The business must be in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County. It is for businesses that cannot get all their needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business financing for location or expansion projects, including business acquisition and expansion, land and building costs, buying machinery and equipment, start-up costs, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Garrett, Allegany, and Washington counties. Businesses must be located in one of these counties to be eligible.
requirements_list: Business must be small
Business must be seeking to locate or expand
Project must create or save jobs
A business plan is required
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee. Businesses work with Summit Financing Solutions and participate with banks and other lenders to obtain gap financing.

structured_extraction.program_description: A voluntary program that encourages landowners to agree that their land will not be developed for a period of ten years. In exchange, landowners receive protection from nuisance complaints, become eligible to sell Development Rights Easements through MALPF, and receive a property tax credit.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Landowners receive a property tax credit for enrolling their agricultural land in a ten-year preservation district agreement. The program provides county property tax credits for farmland, farm buildings, and a partial tax credit for the home. The program also provides protection from nuisance complaints through official county acknowledgement that farming is the preferred use of the land, and makes landowners eligible to sell Development Rights Easements to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation (MALPF). The district agreement runs with the land for at least ten years even if the property is sold or transferred during that period.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural landowners in Washington County who want to preserve their land from development for ten years.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The program does not provide direct funds but rather offers tax credits and legal protections for preserving agricultural land.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, outside water and sewer service areas, and outside of growth areas.
requirements_list: Land must be agricultural property
Land must be a minimum of 50 acres stand-alone or 20 acres if contiguous to other districts
Land must have a minimum of 50% of soil classes I, II, and III
Land must be outside water and sewer service areas
Land must be outside of growth areas
Landowner must voluntarily enter into the district agreement
Land must not be developed or subdivided for industrial, commercial, or residential use except for certain personal eligibility options
Land must be kept in agricultural use for a minimum period of ten years
Landowner agrees not to divide the land without county written approval
Landowner agrees not to construct non-agricultural buildings or structures without county approval
Soil erosion and water quality practices contained within an approved soil conservation plan must be implemented
No trash or rubbish may be dumped on the property except materials for regular agricultural use
No signs or billboards except for signs smaller than four feet square for property name, home-based occupation, or sale/rental
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Interested landowners must complete the Agricultural District Intake Form and the Agricultural Preservation District Agreement documents. These completed forms must be submitted to the Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning. The agreement must be notarized and recorded in the land records of Washington County. Once all current titled landowners have signed the agreement, it is recorded in the County Land Records and the district is established. The agreement becomes effective upon recordation.

structured_extraction.program_description: A federally funded program that provides grants to eligible entities for projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure, natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Grants are provided for projects in five strategic areas: Economic Opportunities (entrepreneurial and business development), Ready Workforce (education, skills, and health improvements), Critical Infrastructure (broadband, transportation, water and wastewater systems), Natural and Cultural Assets (community and economic development leveraging heritage), and Leadership and Community Capacity (building skills of leaders and organizations). Priority projects include Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure. Grants require a 50 percent match, with matching funds identified and committed at the time of application. Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact using ARC's acceptable performance measures.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: FY27 Project Submission (Preliminary Project Description) is April 3, 2026; formal application due November 15, 2026
structured_extraction.program_audience: Eligible entities in Washington County seeking to fund projects that advance economic development, workforce readiness, infrastructure improvements, cultural asset preservation, or community leadership capacity in Appalachia.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Projects related to economic opportunities, workforce development, critical infrastructure (including broadband, transportation, and water/wastewater systems), natural and cultural assets, and leadership and community capacity building. Projects must be consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement priorities and one of five ARC Investment Goals: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland. Projects must be in Appalachia and demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact.
requirements_list: 50 percent match funding must be identified and committed at time of application
Projects must demonstrate measurable outcomes and/or economic impact using ARC's acceptable performance measures
Submit Preliminary Project Description form
Submit ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources form

Projects must fall within one of five ARC Investment Goals: Building Appalachian Businesses, Building Appalachia's Workforce Ecosystem, Building Appalachia's Infrastructure, Building Regional Culture and Tourism, or Building Community Leaders and Capacity

Priority given to projects consistent with ARC 2024 Strategy Statement including Technology Development, Broadband, Education and Workforce Development, Tourism, Energy, Recovery Ecosystems, and Traditional Infrastructure
Project must align with State Strategic Goals and Objectives 2024-2028
All outputs and outcomes must be quantifiable with associated numeric values
Project should reference plans and/or economic documents showing it is part of an overall plan for stimulating economic development
Applicant must describe organizational capacity to administer a federal grant, including recent awards
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit the Preliminary Project Description and ARC Project Budget and Funding Sources forms to the Office of Grant Management by April 3, 2026. Forms must include project description, goals and objectives aligned with ARC Investment Goals and State objectives/strategies, performance measures with quantifiable outputs and outcomes, organizational capacity information, and all matching fund sources with commitment letters. Projects are reviewed and ranked by Washington County Commissioners. County-ranked projects are submitted to Tri-County Council for Western Maryland for regional ranking. Top-ranking projects receive an invitation letter in early Fall to submit a formal grant application to the Appalachian Regional Commission, with the formal application due November 15, 2026.

structured_extraction.program_description: A charitable gaming program that allows qualified organizations to conduct bingo games in Washington County. Organizations must obtain a permit from county commissioners and comply with regulations regarding permitted uses of proceeds, prize limitations, and operational requirements.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program allows nonprofit organizations to conduct bingo games as a fundraising activity. County commissioners review applications to verify the charitable purpose and intended use of proceeds. Nonprofit organizations are exempt from annual permit fees. For-profit operations are prohibited. Prize limits are set at a maximum of $1,000 per game for money prizes, merchandise prizes, or a combination thereof.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Nonprofit organizations seeking to conduct bingo games as a charitable fundraising activity in Washington County
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: The bingo proceeds must be used for charitable purposes as specified in the permit application. For-profit use of proceeds is prohibited.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland
requirements_list: Organization must be a nonprofit
Bingo must be conducted for a charitable purpose, not for profit
A permit must be obtained from the county commissioners before conducting bingo
County commissioners must review and approve the charitable purpose and intended use of receipts
Prize limits must not exceed $1,000 per game for money, merchandise, or combined prizes
Full application required if applicant is new, organization officers have changed, or more than two years have elapsed since last full application
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Submit either the full Bingo Application or Temporary Bingo Application Short Form to the Washington County Grant Management office. The County Commissioners will review the application to verify the nonprofit status, charitable purpose, and intended use of bingo proceeds. Once approved, the organization receives a bingo permit.

structured_extraction.program_name: City of Hagerstown Community and Economic Development Programs
structured_extraction.program_description: A suite of programs administered by the City of Hagerstown Department of Community and Economic Development to support economic development and business growth, including grants for redevelopment, façade improvements, and retail and restaurant incentives.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The City of Hagerstown offers multiple programs including Grants for City Center Redevelopment, City-Wide Redevelopment, Façade Grants, and Retail and Restaurant Incentives. Complete program guidelines apply, and programs are subject to funding availability.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses, property owners, and residents in Hagerstown
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: City center redevelopment, city-wide redevelopment, façade improvements, retail and restaurant business support, homeownership programs
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: City of Hagerstown
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants should consult the City of Hagerstown's complete program and services guide for specific requirements and application procedures for each program.

structured_extraction.program_description: Washington County provides financial support to charitable organizations within Washington County that provide services which improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. The program implements a prioritized approach to funding local non-profits based on specific community needs, with emphasis on efficient use of funds and achieving results-based programmatic outcomes.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Annual grants are awarded to eligible non-profit organizations. For Fiscal Year 2027, the Board of County Commissioners has allocated $1,200,000 in available funding distributed across priority service areas: Families and Children ($494,400), Domestic Violence ($386,400), Arts & Cultural ($135,600), Seniors ($136,800), Recreation ($33,600), and Other ($13,200). Grant awards are disbursed in four quarterly installments (25% each quarter) starting July 2026. All funds must be expended between July 1, 2026, and June 30, 2027. Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested. Eligible expenses include operating and capital expenses/projects that can be completed within the one-year funding period.

structured_extraction.contact_name: Carsten Ahrens, Senior Grant Manager; Maria Kramer, Director
structured_extraction.program_audience: Charitable organizations providing services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens, including services in priority areas: Families/Children, Domestic Violence, Cultural, Seniors, Recreation, and Other community services
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: To support charitable organizations providing services that improve the community and quality of life for Washington County citizens. Funds may be used for operating expenses, capital expenses, and projects. Funds cannot be used to benefit an individual or to fund an endowment.

requirements_list: Organization must be included on the Board of County Commissioners 'Recognized Non-Profit List' (Section 1-108 of the Code of Public Local Laws)
Organization must be a charitable non-profit recognized by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) with 'Valid' status

Organization must be incorporated as a business entity with the Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) and be 'In Good Standing' at the time of application submission with proof provided
Organization must have an office in and provide services within Washington County
Organization must have a recent audit (preferably) or detailed financial statement
Application must be submitted during the published application window by the established deadline
Organization must not have unpaid liens, judgments, or past due obligations to the Washington County Treasurer or any other government entity
Organization must not have submitted applications for the same program under more than one service priority area (multiple applications for different programs are permitted)
Administrative costs may not exceed 15% of the total amount requested
Submission must be signed by an authorized representative of the organization
Organization must be in good standing with the State of Maryland at time of submission
Grant proposal must impact at least one of the prioritized service areas
Letters of support are highly encouraged
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Organizations on the Recognized Non-Profit List receive a Notice of Funding Availability with application procedures and deadlines. The Office of Grant Management makes available online application guidelines, requirements, and forms on or about December 1, 2025. Applicants must complete the Community Organization Funding application packet including: Overview, Statement of Need, Past Performance, Organizational Capacity and Staffing Plan, Program Plan, Collaborations/Partnerships, letters of support, budget spreadsheet, IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter, SDAT proof of good standing, recent audit or financial statement, most recent IRS Form 990, and W-9/Vendor Remittance Form (if applicable). Application packets must contain six hard paper copies (unsecured with staples, binder clips, or rubber bands, no bound covers or tab dividers) and one electronic PDF copy. Hard copies should be placed in a manila envelope and mailed or dropped off at the Office of Grant Management, 100 West Washington Street, Room 1601, Hagerstown, MD 21740. Electronic copy must be emailed to cahrens@washco-md.net and cc jmackereth@washco-md.net with the PDF titled with organization name. All applications and attachments must be submitted by the deadline; applications received after the deadline will not be accepted. The COF Committee, consisting of OGM representatives and five members appointed by the BOCC, reviews and ranks applications using a scoring rubric with criteria: Application Submission (10 points), Statement of Need (20 points), Past Performance (5 points), Organizational Capacity and Staffing (10 points), Program Plan (30 points), Collaborations/Partnerships (10 points), and Budget/Narrative (15 points) for a maximum of 100 points. Additional factors considered include total funding allocated, amount per priority area, geographic distribution, and previous program performance. Applicants will be notified in writing when the budgetary process is complete. Technical assistance workshops are offered on December 2nd at 9:00-10:30am or 3:00-4:30pm via Zoom with limited in-person option.

structured_extraction.program_description: Provides qualifying businesses with State income tax credits and local real property tax credits in return for job creation and capital investments made in the designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
list_of_eligible_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services
structured_extraction.assistance_description: State Income Tax Credits: Qualifying businesses receive tax credits based on new jobs created. For most new jobs, the credit is a one-time maximum of $1,000. For economically disadvantaged employees certified by Maryland Department of Labor, credits are $3,000 the first year, $2,000 the second year, and $1,000 the third year. Employees must work at least 35 hours per week, earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage, spend at least 50% of working time in the Zone, and be employed for at least 6 months. Local Real Property Tax Credits: Property owners receive 10 years of credits on real property with capital investments. Credits are 80% of property taxes on increased assessment for years 1-5, declining to 30% in year 10. Commercial Building Excise Tax Exemption: New construction in Enterprise Zones is exempt from commercial building excise taxes. Ten-year total tax credit period available.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: No specific deadline
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualifying businesses making investments and creating jobs in Washington County Enterprise Zones, including proprietorships, partnerships, and corporations. New and existing for-profit businesses making job creation and capital investments in designated Enterprise Zones, including manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate offices, service industries, and retail businesses (with restrictions).
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credits applied to State income taxes and local real property taxes; exemption from commercial building excise taxes on new construction. State income tax credits for job creation and local real property tax credits for capital improvements such as new construction, building additions, and renovations in designated Enterprise Zones.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Three designated Enterprise Zones in Washington County: City of Hagerstown/Washington County Enterprise Zone (approximately 4,000 acres, originally approved 1982, renewed 1992, 2002, 2012) including Hopewell Valley Industrial Park, Washington County Business Park, CSX Valley Park, City of Hagerstown Business Park, and downtown Hagerstown Central Business District; Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres, originally approved 1995, renewed 2005, 2015). Designation dates: Hagerstown-Washington County Zone - December 15, 1982; Hancock Zone - December 15, 1995.
requirements_list: Business must be located in designated Enterprise Zone on designation date, relocated after designation date, or started construction/expansion after designation date
For income tax credits: new employment must begin after zone designation date (Hagerstown-Washington County: Dec 15, 1982; Hancock: Dec 15, 1995)
Income tax credit minimum job creation: Central Business District requires 1 new job; Outside Central Business District requires 5 new jobs (Hancock requires 1)
Property tax credit minimum capital investment: Central Business District requires $5,000+; Outside Central Business District requires $50,000+ (Hancock requires $5,000+)

Eligible business types: manufacturing, warehousing, research and development, corporate or regional headquarters offices, service industries; retail/mercantile only in Central Business District or Hancock Zone
Employees must be hired after zone designation or business location, not replacement hires
Full-time employment required: minimum 35 hours per week
Employees must earn at least 150% of federal minimum wage
Employees must work at least 6 consecutive months
Employees must spend at least 50% of work time in Enterprise Zone or on activities directly related to Zone
Property improvements must be certified to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation by December 31st of completion year to receive credits in upcoming tax year
Property tax credit application must be submitted prior to project completion and issuance of User/Occupancy Permits
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: For Property Tax Credits: Submit Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form to Washington County Department of Business Development prior to project completion. DBD sends approval letter to property owner; copies submitted to Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation and local assessor. Credits automatically applied to Washington County and Town of Hancock tax bills in July; City of Hagerstown issues credit voucher. For Income Tax Credits: Submit Request for Enterprise Zone Qualification form after hiring new employees, along with New Jobs Created form listing employees meeting requirements. Local Job Service Office (Maryland Department of Labor) contacts business to review employee list and determine individual eligibility as disadvantaged or non-disadvantaged. DBD sends approval or denial letter. Claim credits using Maryland Tax Form 500CR with copy of DBD approval letter on annual state tax return. For disadvantaged employee credits, contact Maryland Job Service Office at 301-393-8200 or visit 14 North Potomac Street, Hagerstown for employee screening and certification. Contact Washington County Department of Business Development at 240-313-2280 or edcinfo@washco-md.net for applications and information.
