structured_extraction.program_description: Tax credits available for property owners who undertake approved historic preservation work on their properties located in Washington County historic districts. The program offers stackable credits up to 70% of qualified rehabilitation expenses through county (25%), state (20%), federal (20%), and additional exterior work (5%) credits.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
list_of_relevant_industries: Real Estate and Rental and Leasing
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The Washington County Historic Properties Tax Credit provides a reduction in county property taxes for qualified rehabilitation expenses on eligible historic structures. The program offers a 25% county tax credit for rehabilitation, restoration, or preservation work that minimizes destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design. An additional 5% tax credit is available for exterior work on new construction attached to existing historic structures. Qualifying Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) include roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental. Unused credits can be carried over for up to 5 years or until expended. The program is stackable with state (20%), federal (20%), and additional exterior credits (5%), providing up to 70% possible total credits. Application for the county credit must be submitted before work starts.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Application must be submitted before work begins; no specific annual deadline
structured_extraction.contact_name: Washington County Department of Planning and Zoning; Historic District Commission
structured_extraction.program_audience: Residential and commercial property owners with historic properties in Washington County historic districts seeking to undertake preservation, restoration, or renovation work
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Qualified Rehabilitation Expenses (QREs) for historic preservation and rehabilitation work including roof repair/replacement, chimney repair/replacement, window restoration, storm doors/windows, masonry re-pointing, structural repairs, architectural/engineering/consulting fees, and tool/equipment rental on eligible historic structures
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, specifically properties: (1) within the Antietam Overlay (AO1 or AO2) district; (2) that are contributing structures to surveyed and adopted Historic Rural Villages (Antietam, Cavetown, Fairplay, Highfield, Leitersburg, Pen Mar, Ringgold, Rohrersville, Sandy Hook, or Tilghmanton); (3) with the Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay applied through a rezoning process; or (4) that are contributing structures within towns listed on the National Register of Historic Places with appropriate zoning and design guidelines. Properties must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties.
requirements_list: Property must be located in a designated historic district, Antietam Overlay zone, Historic Rural Village, or eligible municipality with appropriate zoning
Property must be documented on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties
Work must be approved by the Historic District Commission before rehabilitation begins
Applicant must follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and the Washington County Design Guidelines for Historic Structures
Work must minimize destruction of historic fabric with thoughtful and sympathetic design
For structures under Maryland Historical Trust (MHT) Easement, a copy of the easement document must be included with the application
Property owners with MHT Easements must comply with easement holder review requirements
Applicant is responsible for compliance with all Federal, State, and local laws including zoning, building, safety codes, licensing, permitting, and environmental requirements
Application must be submitted and approved before work begins; work started prior to approval may not be eligible for tax credit
Itemized documentation of all expenses with invoices/receipts and proof of payment is required for Part 3 certification
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The application process consists of three parts: Part I (Evaluation of Significance) - submitted during project planning phase to determine if the structure qualifies; owners of properties with Historic Preservation (HP) Overlay do not need to complete Part I unless there is a question about overlay inclusion. Part II (Description of Rehabilitation) - submitted before work begins for review by staff and Historic District Commission to ensure conformance with Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation and County Design Guidelines; must be approved before any work starts. Part III (Certification of Completed Work) - submitted after project completion with itemized expenses, invoices, receipts, proof of payment, and project photos for HDC review of eligible expenses and determination that work was completed as approved. Completed projects may be inspected by HDC representatives. Applications and supporting documents should be mailed to: Washington County Historic District Commission, c/o Washington County Department of Planning & Zoning, 747 Northern Avenue, Hagerstown, MD 21742, or emailed to askplanning@washco-md.net. All application parts require signatures done using Digital ID, printed and wet signed, or digitized original handwritten signatures. If applicant is not the fee-simple owner, an Owner's Representative Affidavit must be included. Upon HDC approval, the credit amount is forwarded to the Treasurer's Office for property bill updates.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides grants to stimulate and assist Washington County organizations, agencies, and businesses in developing tourism attractions, enhancing economic development, and supporting cultural and recreational projects. Projects must generate overnight stays in the County

Projects must reach a broad segment of the community

structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Requests can be made throughout the fiscal year and are contingent on available funding. Applications can be accessed from the County's website under the Office of Grant Management, submitted by email, or printed and mailed in. All applications are received by the Office of Grant Management (OGM). The OGM will: (1) determine if the applicant is qualified to receive funding; (2) determine if the event or project is qualified to receive funding; (3) determine if the request meets the funding goals of the County Commissioners and the purpose of the Hotel Rental Tax Funding; (4) for requests of $25,000 and below, approve or deny the request with the concurrence of the County Administrator; (5) for requests of more than $25,000, process the application and forward it to the County Administrator for review, and upon favorable review the County Commissioners will hear the request; and (6) notify the applicant in writing of approval or denial. All organizations receiving grant funding must complete a Hotel Rental Tax Grant Report with supporting documentation (budget itemizations and/or receipts) within 60 days of project completion.

structured_extraction.program_description: A program created to accelerate land preservation easement purchases by allowing agricultural landowners to sell their development rights to the County in exchange for annual installment payments over ten years.

structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Purchase of agricultural preservation easements on the entire contiguous acreage of the land less one acre per existing dwelling on the property
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County
requirements_list: Property must be agricultural land meeting minimum qualifications
Owner must own the entire contiguous acreage
Easement applies to entire contiguous acreage of the land less one acre per existing dwelling on the property
Program is very competitive and dependent on current economic climate

Once the landowner agrees to the County's offer, an Installment Purchase Agreement is written that includes the total amount of money, terms, and fixed interest rate.

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides up to a fifteen year tax credit on the County portion of real estate taxes for qualified businesses that either expand or locate and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. The program includes three tiers based on investment and job creation levels, offering varying credit durations and rates.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Real property tax credits on the increased assessed property value for eligible businesses that expand or locate in Washington County. The program offers three tiers: TIER ONE (1,500 sq. ft. and 5 new FTEs within 12 months) provides 3 years of credits at 55%, 40%, 25%; TIER TWO (2,500 sq. ft. and 25 new FTEs within 24 months) provides 6 years of credits at 55%, 55%, 40%, 40%, 25%, 25%; TIER THREE ($20M investment and 200 new FTEs within 24 months, with 80% of FTEs paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage) provides 15 years of credits at 75% for the first five years, then reduced by 5% annually over the next 10 years until it reaches 25%. Lessors must reduce the amount of taxes for which an eligible business entity is contractually liable by the amount of the tax credit for which the business qualifies.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Qualified for-profit businesses that expand or locate in Washington County and meet specific investment and job creation thresholds. Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Tax credit applies to real estate taxes on increased assessed property value of newly constructed, renovated, expanded, or previously unoccupied properties
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County. Note: Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program and must apply under the Enterprise Zone Program.
requirements_list: Meet specific investment thresholds (Tier 1: 1,500 sq. ft., Tier 2: 2,500 sq. ft., Tier 3: $20M investment)
Meet specific job creation thresholds (Tier 1: 5 new FTEs within 12 months, Tier 2: 25 new FTEs within 24 months, Tier 3: 200 new FTEs within 24 months)
For Tier 3, 80% of all new FTEs must be paid 200% of Maryland State minimum wage
Either expand or locate in Washington County

Apply before occupying space or hiring employees
Create required FTEs within 12 months for Tier 1 or 24 months for Tiers 2 and 3
Submit Annual Employment and Certification Report by February 1 each year

Cannot have received a tax credit or exemption for the same property during the same taxable year under any other state or county law
Businesses in Enterprise Zones are not eligible for this program
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: 1. Complete and submit the official Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit application with required information including company details, property information, and project details. 3. structured_extraction.program_name: Maryland Economic Development Assistance Authority and Fund (MEDAAF)
structured_extraction.program_description: A state financing program offering six different assistance capabilities to help businesses and jurisdictions with economic development projects. The program provides loans, grants, and loan guarantees to support strategic economic development opportunities and local economic needs.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MEDAAF offers six financing capabilities: (1) Significant Strategic Economic Development Opportunities providing loans up to $10 million or 20 percent of current fund balance; (2) Local Economic Development Opportunity providing loans up to $5 million or grants/conditional loans up to $2 million with local jurisdiction participation; (3) Direct Assistance to Local Jurisdictions providing up to $3 million (or more for qualified distressed counties) for land acquisition, infrastructure, fixed assets, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development plans; (4) Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund grants of $250,000 annually with local matching funds required; (5) Special Purposes Loans for specific state initiatives including Brownfield Revitalization, Seafood and Aquaculture, Animal Waste, Arts and Entertainment, and Child Care Center programs; (6) Economic Development Opportunities Fund (Sunny Day Fund) requiring minimum capital investment of five times the state assistance amount. Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs with limited exceptions.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses located in priority funding areas and eligible industries; local jurisdictions
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Economic development projects including land acquisition, infrastructure improvements, fixed asset acquisition, leasehold improvements, feasibility studies, and economic development plans
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in a priority funding area. Applicants are restricted to eligible industry sectors.
requirements_list: Business must be located in a priority funding area
Business must operate in an eligible industry sector
Assistance cannot exceed 70 percent of total project costs with limited exceptions
For Local Economic Development Opportunity, local jurisdiction must sponsor the business and participate with guarantee, direct loan, or grant equal to at least 10 percent of state assistance
For Regional or Local Revolving Loan Fund grants, local government must provide matching funds
For Economic Development Opportunities Fund, applicants must have strong balance sheet and be creditworthy, and projects must be consistent with state's strategic economic development plan
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with DBED to determine eligibility and apply for specific MEDAAF capabilities based on their project needs.

structured_extraction.program_description: A state program that facilitates capital access for economic development projects by issuing private activity revenue bonds and providing credit insurance to reduce lender risk.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: MIDFA offers Industrial Revenue Bonds (taxable bonds for fixed asset financing and tax-exempt bonds for non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects) and credit insurance programs. Conventional credit insurance covers up to 80 percent of transactions, not to exceed $2.5 million (up to 90 percent for export transactions). Bond program credit insurance covers up to 100 percent of bonds, not to exceed $7.5 million of taxable or tax-exempt bonds. In certain rural areas with qualifying high unemployment, MIDFA offers linked deposits where a certificate of deposit is provided to the lender as a funding source to enable below-market-rate loans to eligible small businesses.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses seeking long-term capital financing for fixed assets; 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations; manufacturing facilities
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Fixed asset financing; infrastructure projects; solid waste projects (for tax-exempt bonds)

requirements_list: Project must be located in Priority Funding Area
Tax-exempt bonds limited to 501(c)(3) non-profit organizations, manufacturing facilities, and certain solid waste projects
Federal tax law restrictions apply
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants work with MIDFA through participating financial institutions to structure Industrial Revenue Bonds or credit insurance arrangements.

Call any registered provider to schedule rides and pay the driver with your vouchers.

structured_extraction.program_description: Comprehensive tax incentives and financial assistance programs designed to support business development, expansion, and job creation in Washington County, including tax credits, loans, grants, and workforce training support.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: Washington County offers multiple tax incentive programs including: (1) Job Creation & Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credits ranging from 6-15 years (52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6 for Section 4a; 30% years 1-2, 20% years 3-4, 10% years 5-6 for Section 4b; 100% years 1-5, 75% years 6-10, 50% years 11-15 for Section 4c); (2) New Jobs Tax Credit providing 6-year credits at 52% years 1-2, 39% years 3-4, 26% years 5-6; (3) Research & Development Equipment Tax Exemption exempting R&D equipment from County Business Personal Property Tax; (4) Manufacturing Machinery & Equipment Tax Exemption; (5) Business Inventory Tax Exemption; (6) Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program offering 3-year tax credits at 0.4% of construction costs; (7) Brownfield Revitalization Incentive Program (BRIP) providing 50-70% real property tax credits for 5 years (up to 10 years in Enterprise Zones); (8) C-PACE loans for energy efficiency and renewable energy projects with up to 100% fixed-rate financing and 20-year payback periods. City of Hagerstown offers additional programs: Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund up to $200,000 or 80% of project cost (microenterprise loans up to $5,000), CDBG Microenterprise Grants, and Invest Hagerstown Grants ranging from $5,000-$250,000. Workforce training grants up to $4,500 per worker available through Western Maryland Consortium. Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program provides tax credits and financial incentives for hiring apprentices.
structured_extraction.program_audience: For-profit businesses, non-profits, and individuals seeking to establish, expand, or relocate operations in Washington County; businesses in manufacturing, construction, and other industries; companies interested in energy efficiency and clean energy projects; small businesses and microenterprises; job seekers and businesses seeking workforce training.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Business expansion and relocation; capital improvements; equipment and machinery purchases; building construction and renovation; land improvements; façade enhancements; code compliance; working capital; energy efficiency and renewable energy projects; research and development; inventory; employee recruitment, training, and retention; job creation.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Washington County, Maryland; City of Hagerstown (for city-specific programs); Foreign Trade Zone #255 locations including Hagerstown Regional Airport, Williamsport, Hopewell Valley, Lakeside Corporate Center at Cascade, and Hancock; Enterprise Zones including Hagerstown-Washington County Enterprise Zone (nearly 5,000 acres) and Town of Hancock Enterprise Zone (1,500 acres); Priority Funding Areas for certain programs.
requirements_list: Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4a): Minimum 1,500 sq ft new/expanded premises; at least 1 new permanent full-time employee during 12-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4b): Minimum 2,500 sq ft; at least 5 additional new permanent full-time employees during 24-month period
Job Creation & Capital Investment (Section 4c): $10M in capital improvements; create 100 new permanent full-time employees
New Jobs Tax Credit: Minimum 10,000 sq ft expansion; at least 25 new permanent full-time positions; 50% of new jobs must pay at least 135% of average weekly wage; must be in Priority Funding Area
BRIP: Site must qualify for cleanup program; must be owned by inculpable person; must be in participating jurisdiction
C-PACE: Commercial property or non-profit organization; project must involve energy efficiency, renewable energy, or water conservation

CDBG Microenterprise Grant (City of Hagerstown): Located in City of Hagerstown corporate boundaries; 5 or fewer total employees including owner; private for-profit business; in good standing with City and State; in compliance with all City regulations; established and operating for at least 12 months (or provide business plan and business counseling consultation)

Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund: Organized as proprietorship, partnership, LLC, or corporation; business sales less than $5M annually for last 2 years; credit check required; non-refundable application fee
Hagerstown Revolving Loan Fund Job Requirements: For each $35,000 or fraction thereof borrowed, one full-time job must be created or retained within 2 years from loan closing

Invest Hagerstown Programs: Private developer partnership; projects must address vacant/underutilized properties; 2:1 match required from developer; for homeownership programs, property must be built prior to 1960 and vacant 12 months, or be conversion of rental to owner-occupied
Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus Program: Approved parcel; new improvement must meet construction cost thresholds
Enterprise Zone Program: Located within designated Enterprise Zone boundaries; qualified business status; job creation and capital investment requirements
Maryland Apprenticeship & Training Program: Participating business; apprentice employee
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applications vary by program. For tax credit programs (Job Creation & Capital Investment, New Jobs Tax Credit, BRIP, Pad-Ready Site Commercial Stimulus), businesses should contact the Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development at (240) 313-2280 or visit www.washco-md.net/business-development. City of Hagerstown programs (Revolving Loan Fund, CDBG Microenterprise Grants, Invest Hagerstown) have specific application requirements and forms available online. C-PACE applications are processed through Abacus Property Solutions in coordination with the Maryland Clean Energy Center; contact (240) 313-2280 for facilitation. Western Maryland Consortium (Debora Gilbert, 301-791-3164, dgilbert@westmdcon.org) handles workforce training grant applications. Maryland Apprenticeship & Training Program inquiries go through Jennifer Runkles, Western MD Apprenticeship & Training Navigator, at 443-615-4758 or jennifer.runkles@maryland.gov. For Enterprise Zone program, contact Washington County Department of Business Development and Economic Development.
